[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of meeting

- **[[138]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-138
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Notice of the time and place of a
  meeting of shareholders or members of a bank must be sent within the
  prescribed period to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} each shareholder or member entitled to vote at the
    meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each director;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the auditor or auditors of the bank; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(1.01)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a bank that is not a federal credit
  union and that is not a distributing bank, notice may be sent within
  any shorter period specified in its by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of eligible votes

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A bank with equity of twelve billion dollars or
  more that is not a federal credit union must set out in the notice of
  a meeting the number of eligible votes, as defined under subsection
  156.09(1), that may be cast at the meeting as of the record date for
  determining shareholders entitled to receive the notice of meeting or,
  if there are to be separate votes of shareholders at the meeting, the
  number of eligible votes, as defined in that subsection, in respect of
  each separate vote to be held at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication in newspaper

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the notice required under subsection
  (1), where any class of shares of a bank is publicly traded on a
  recognized stock exchange in Canada, notice of the time and place of a
  meeting of shareholders shall be published once a week for at least
  four consecutive weeks before the date of the meeting in a newspaper
  in general circulation in the place where the head office of the bank
  is situated and in each place in Canada where the bank has a transfer
  agent or where a transfer of the bank's shares may be recorded.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 138
- 2001, c. 9, s. 63
- 2005, c. 54, s. 18
- 2007, c. 6, s. 132
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1950
- 2012, c. 5, ss. 5, 223
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-138-20120524.html "Link to previous version of section 138"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice not required

- **[[139]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-139 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  notice of a meeting is not required to be sent to shareholders or
  members who are not registered on the records of the bank or the
  bank's transfer agent on the record date fixed under paragraph
  137(5)(c) or determined under paragraph 137(6)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of default

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Failure to receive a notice of a meeting does not
  deprive a shareholder or member of the right to vote at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 139
- 2005, c. 54, s. 19
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1951
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-139-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 139"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of adjourned meeting

- **[[140]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-140 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  meeting is adjourned for less than 30 days, it is not necessary,
  unless the by-laws otherwise provide, to give notice of the adjourned
  meeting, other than by announcement at the earliest meeting that is
  adjourned.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice if adjournment is longer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a meeting is adjourned by one or more adjournments
  for a total of 30 days or more, notice of the continuation of the
  meeting must be given as for an original meeting but, unless the
  meeting is adjourned by one or more adjournments for a total of more
  than 90 days, subsection 156.04(1) does not apply.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 140
- 1997, c. 15, s. 8
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1952(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-140-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 140"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special business

- **[[141]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-141 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} All
  matters dealt with at a special meeting of shareholders or members and
  all matters dealt with at an annual meeting, except consideration of
  the financial statements, report of the auditor or auditors, election
  of directors, remuneration of directors and reappointment of the
  incumbent auditor or auditors, are deemed to be special business.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of special business

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notice of a meeting of shareholders or members at
  which special business is to be transacted must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} state the nature of the special business in
    sufficient detail to permit a shareholder or member to form a
    reasoned judgment in respect of that special business; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contain the text of any special resolution to be
    submitted to the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 141
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1953
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-141-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 141"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nominations for directors

- **[[141.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-141.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If shareholders of a federal credit
  union are entitled to elect one or more directors,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a nomination for the election of a director may be
    made only by one or more registered holders or beneficial owners of
    shares representing in the aggregate not less than 5 per cent of the
    shares of the federal credit union or 5 per cent of the shares of a
    class of its shares entitled to vote at the meeting at which the
    election is to take place; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a notice of a meeting of shareholders must include
    any nomination made in accordance with paragraph (a) for the
    election of a director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply if the nomination is
  submitted to the federal credit union at least the prescribed number
  of days before the anniversary date of the previous annual meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1954
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver of notice

- **[[142]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-142 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  shareholder, a member and any other person entitled to attend a
  meeting may in any manner waive notice of the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance is a waiver

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Attendance at a meeting of shareholders or members is
  a waiver of notice of the meeting, except when a person attends the
  meeting for the express purpose of objecting to the transaction of any
  business on the grounds that the meeting is not lawfully called.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 142
- 2001, c. 9, s. 64(F)
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1955
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-142-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 142"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposals

- **[[143]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-143
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (1.1) and
  (1.2), a registered holder or beneficial owner of shares of a bank
  that is not a federal credit union that may be voted at an annual
  meeting of shareholders may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the bank notice of any matter that they
    propose to raise at the meeting (in this section and section 144
    referred to as a "proposal"); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} discuss at the meeting any matter in respect of
    which they would have been entitled to submit a proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility to submit proposal

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} To be eligible to submit a proposal a person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for at least the prescribed period be the
    registered holder or beneficial owner of at least the prescribed
    number of the bank's outstanding shares; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} have the support of persons who, in the aggregate
    and including or not including the person who submits the proposal,
    have for at least the prescribed period been the registered holders
    or beneficial owners of at least the prescribed number of the bank's
    outstanding shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} A proposal is to be accompanied by the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person submitting the
    proposal and the names and addresses of their supporters, if any;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of shares held or owned by the person
    and their supporters, if any, and the date that the shares were
    acquired.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not part of proposal

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} The information provided under subsection (1.2)
  does not form part of a proposal or of the supporting statement
  referred to in subsection (3) and is not to be included for the
  purpose of the prescribed maximum number of words referred to in
  subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof may be required

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} If the bank requests within the prescribed period
  that a person provide proof that they are eligible to submit a
  proposal, the person shall within the prescribed period provide proof
  that they meet the requirements of subsection (1.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Management proxy

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank that solicits proxies shall, in the management
  proxy circular required by subsection 156.05(1), set out any proposal
  of a shareholder submitted for consideration at a meeting of
  shareholders or attach the proposal to the management proxy circular.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supporting statement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} At the request of the person who submits a proposal,
  the bank shall set out in the management proxy circular or attach to
  it the person's statement in support of the proposal and their name
  and address. The statement and proposal together are not to exceed the
  prescribed maximum number of words.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nomination of directors

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A proposal may include nominations for the election
  of directors if it is signed by one or more registered holders or
  beneficial owners of shares representing in the aggregate not less
  than 5% of the shares of the bank or 5% of the shares of a class of
  its shares entitled to vote at the meeting at which the proposal is to
  be presented.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A bank is not required to comply with subsections (2)
  and (3) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the proposal is not submitted to the bank at least
    the prescribed number of days before the anniversary date of the
    notice of meeting that was sent to shareholders in respect of the
    previous annual meeting of shareholders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it clearly appears that the primary purpose of the
    proposal is to enforce a personal claim or redress a personal
    griev­ance against the bank or its directors, officers or security
    holders;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} it clearly appears that the proposal does not
    relate in a significant way to the business or affairs of the bank;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person submitting the proposal failed within
    the prescribed period before the bank receives their proposal to
    present, in person or by proxy, at a meeting of shareholders a
    proposal that at their request had been set out in or attached to a
    management proxy circular;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} substantially the same proposal was set out in or
    attached to a management proxy circular or dissident's proxy
    circular relating to, and presented to shareholders at, a meeting of
    shareholders held within the prescribed period before the receipt of
    the proposal and did not receive the prescribed minimum amount of
    support at the meeting; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the rights conferred by subsections (1) to (4) are
    being abused to secure publicity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bank may refuse to include proposal

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} If a person who submits a proposal fails to
  continue to hold or own shares in accordance with paragraph (1.1)(a)
  or, as the case may be, does not continue to have the support of
  persons who are in the aggregate the registered holders or beneficial
  owners of the prescribed number of shares in accordance with paragraph
  (1.1)(b) until the end of the meeting, the bank is not required to set
  out any proposal submitted by that person in or attach it to a
  management proxy circular for any meeting held within the prescribed
  period after the day of the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Immunity for proposal and statement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} No bank or person acting on behalf of a bank incurs
  any liability by reason only of circulating a proposal or statement in
  compliance with subsections (2) and (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 143
- 1997, c. 15, s. 9
- 2005, c. 54, s. 20
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1956
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-143-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 143"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of refusal

- **[[144]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-144 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  bank refuses to include a proposal in a management proxy circular, it
  shall in writing notify the person submitting the proposal of its
  intention to omit the proposal from the management proxy circular and
  of the reasons for the refusal. It shall notify the person within the
  prescribed period after either the day on which it receives the
  proposal or, if it has requested proof under subsection 143(1.4), the
  day on which it receives the proof.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the application of a person submitting a proposal
  who claims to be aggrieved by a bank's refusal under subsection (1), a
  court may restrain the holding of the meeting at which the proposal is
  sought to be presented and make any further order that it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A bank or any person claiming to be aggrieved by a
  proposal may apply to a court for an order permitting the bank to omit
  the proposal from the management proxy circular, and the court, if it
  is satisfied that subsection 143(5) applies, may make such order as it
  thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An applicant under subsection (2) or (3) shall give
  the Superintendent written notice of the application and the
  Superintendent may appear and be heard at the hearing of the
  application in person or by counsel.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 144
- 2005, c. 54, s. 21
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-144-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 144"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposals --- members of federal credit
union

- **[[144.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-144.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  a member of a federal credit union may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the federal credit union notice of any
    matter that they propose to raise at an annual meeting (in this
    section referred to as a "proposal"); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} discuss at an annual meeting any matter in respect
    of which they would have been entitled to submit a proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility to submit proposal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} To be eligible to submit a proposal a member must
  have been a member of the federal credit union for at least the
  prescribed period before making the proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A proposal is to be accompanied by a statement
  setting out the name and address of the member submitting the proposal
  and the period of time the member has been a member.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not part of proposal

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The information provided under subsection (3) does
  not form part of a proposal or of the supporting statement referred to
  in subsection (6) and is not included for the purposes of the
  prescribed maximum number of words referred to in subsection (6).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof may be required

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the federal credit union requests within the
  prescribed period that a member provide proof that they are eligible
  to submit a proposal, the member must within the prescribed period
  provide proof that they meet the requirement of subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal and statement to accompany
  notice of meeting

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A proposal submitted for consideration at a meeting
  must be attached to the notice of the meeting, together with, if
  requested by the member making the proposal, a statement in support of
  the proposal and the name and address of the member making the
  proposal. The statement and the proposal must together not exceed the
  prescribed maximum number of words.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nomination of directors

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A proposal may include nominations for the election
  of directors if it is signed by the lesser of 250 members and 1 per
  cent of the members who are entitled to vote at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A federal credit union need not comply with
  subsection (6) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the proposal is not submitted to the federal credit
    union at least the prescribed number of days before the anniversary
    date of the notice of meeting that was sent to members in connection
    with the previous annual meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it clearly appears that the primary purpose of the
    proposal is to enforce a personal claim or redress a personal
    grievance against the federal credit union or its directors,
    officers, members or security holders;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person submitting the proposal has failed,
    within the prescribed period before the federal credit union
    receives the person's proposal, to present, at a meeting, a proposal
    that, at the person's request, had been attached by the federal
    credit union to the notice of the meeting;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} substantially the same proposal was attached to a
    notice of meeting, and presented at a meeting, of the federal credit
    union held not more than the prescribed period before the receipt of
    the proposal and the proposal did not receive the prescribed minimum
    amount of support at the meeting; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the rights conferred by subsection (1) are being
    abused to secure publicity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Federal credit union may refuse to
  include proposal

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} If a member who submits a proposal withdraws from
  membership in accordance with section 47.05 before the meeting, the
  federal credit union is not required to attach any proposal submitted
  by that member to the notice of a meeting held within the prescribed
  period following the date of the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Immunity

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} No federal credit union or person acting on behalf
  of a federal credit union incurs any liability by reason only of
  circulating a proposal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1957
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refusal to include proposal

- **[[144.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-144.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a federal credit union refuses to
  include a proposal in a notice of a meeting referred to in section
  138, it must, within the prescribed period after the day on which it
  receives the proposal or the day on which it receives the proof of
  eligibility under subsection 144.1(5), as the case may be, notify in
  writing the person submitting the proposal of its intention to omit
  the proposal from the notice and of the reasons for the refusal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restraining order by court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the application of a person submitting a proposal
  who claims to be aggrieved by a federal credit union's refusal under
  subsection (1), a court may restrain the holding of the meeting at
  which the proposal is sought to be presented and make any further
  order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order to omit proposal from notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A federal credit union or any person claiming to be
  aggrieved by a proposal may apply to a court for an order permitting
  the federal credit union to omit the proposal from a notice of
  meeting, and the court, if it is satisfied that subsection 144.1(7)
  applies, may make any order that it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An applicant under subsection (2) or (3) must give
  the Superintendent written notice of the application, and the
  Superintendent may appear and be heard at the hearing of the
  application in person or by counsel.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1957
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of shareholders entitled to notice

- **[[145]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-145 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall prepare an alphabet­ical list of shareholders entitled to
  receive notice of a meeting showing the number of shares held by each
  shareholder

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a record date is fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(c), no later than 10 days after that date; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no record date is fixed, on the record date
    determined under paragraph 137(6)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of members entitled to notice

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A federal credit union must also prepare an
  alphabetical list of members entitled to receive notice of a meeting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a record date is fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(c), no later than 10 days after that date; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no record date is fixed, on the record date
    determined under paragraph 137(6)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting list

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The bank shall prepare an alphabetical list of
  shareholders entitled to vote as of the record date showing the number
  of shares held by each shareholder

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a record date is fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(d), no later than 10 days after that date; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no record date is fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(d), no later than 10 days after a record date is fixed under
    paragraph 137(5)(c) or no later than the record date determined
    under paragraph 137(6)(a), as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting list --- members

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} A federal credit union must also prepare an
  alphabetical list of members entitled to vote as of the record date

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a record date is fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(d), no later than 10 days after that date; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no record date is fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(d), no later than 10 days after a record date is fixed under
    paragraph 137(5)(c) or no later than the record date determined
    under paragraph 137(6)(a), as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entitlement to vote

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 156.09, a shareholder whose name
  appears on a list prepared under subsection (2) is entitled to vote
  the shares shown opposite their name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of list

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder of a bank that is not a federal credit
  union may examine the list of shareholders

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during usual business hours at the head office of
    the bank or at the place where its central securities register is
    maintained; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the meeting of shareholders for which the list
    was prepared.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of list

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person who is entitled to vote at a meeting of a
  federal credit union may examine a list that relates to the meeting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during usual business hours at the head office of
    the federal credit union or at the place where its members register
    or central securities register is maintained; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the meeting for which the list was prepared.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 145
- 2001, c. 9, s. 65
- 2005, c. 54, s. 22
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1958
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-145-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 145"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum

- **[[146]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-146
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise
  provide, a quorum of shareholders is present at a meeting of
  shareholders if the holders of a majority of the shares who are
  entitled to vote at the meeting are present in person or represented
  by proxyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum --- members

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise provide, a quorum of
  members is present at a meeting of members of a federal credit union
  if at least 500 members who are entitled to vote at the meeting, or
  one per cent of the total number of members entitled to vote at the
  meeting, whichever is the lesser, are present in person or represented
  by a personal representative or delegate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum at opening of meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a quorum is present at the opening of a meeting of
  shareholders or members, the shareholders or members present may,
  unless the by-laws otherwise provide, proceed with the business of the
  meeting even though a quorum is not present throughout the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjournment permitted

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a quorum is not present at the opening of a
  meeting of shareholders or members, the shareholders or members
  present may adjourn the meeting to a fixed time and place but may not
  transact any other business.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 146
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1959
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-146-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 146"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}One shareholder meeting

**[[147]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-147 .sectionLabel}** If a bank has only one
shareholder, or only one holder of any class or series of shares, the
shareholder present in person or represented by a proxyholder
constitutes a meeting of shareholders or a meeting of shareholders of
that class or series.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}One share --- one vote

**[[148]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-148 .sectionLabel}** Subject to section
156.09, if a share of a bank entitles the holder of the share to vote at
a meeting of shareholders, that share entitles the shareholder to one
vote at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 148
- 2001, c. 9, s. 66
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representative of shareholder or member

- **[[149]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-149 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an entity is a shareholder or member of a bank, the bank must
  recognize any natural person authorized by a resolution of the
  directors or governing body or similar authority of the entity to
  represent it at meetings of shareholders or members of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A natural person authorized under subsection (1) to
  represent an entity may exercise on behalf of the entity all the
  powers the entity could exercise if it were a natural person as well
  as a shareholder or member.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 149
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1960
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-149-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 149"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Joint shareholders

**[[150]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-150 .sectionLabel}** Unless the by-laws
otherwise provide, if two or more persons hold shares jointly, one of
those holders present at a meeting of shareholders may in the absence of
the others vote the shares, but if two or more of those persons who are
present in person or represented by proxyholder vote, they shall vote as
one on the shares jointly held by them.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting by hands or ballot

- **[[151]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-151
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise
  provide, voting at a meeting of shareholders or members is to take
  place by show of hands except when a ballot is demanded by a person
  entitled to vote at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person entitled to vote at a meeting of
  shareholders or members may demand a ballot either before or after any
  vote by show of hands.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic voting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1) and unless the by-laws provide
  otherwise, any vote referred to in that subsection may be held
  entirely by means of a telephonic, electronic or other communication
  facility if the bank makes one available.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting while participating
  electronically

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise, any person who
  is participating in a meeting under subsection 136(2) and entitled to
  vote at that meeting may vote by means of the telephonic, electronic
  or other communication facility that the bank has made available for
  that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The by-laws of a federal credit union may, subject to
  the regulations, allow members to vote, prior to the meeting, subject
  to any conditions set out in the by-laws,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by mail;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in person, at one of its branches;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} by telephonic or electronic means; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} by any other prescribed means.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the manner of and conditions for voting
    at a meeting of members or shareholders by means of a telephonic,
    electronic or other communication facility; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting the manner and conditions of voting
    referred to in paragraphs (5)(a) to (d) by members of federal credit
    unions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 151
- 2005, c. 54, s. 23
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1961
- [2019, c. 29, s. 87](#1155581-1170878){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1155581-1170878.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution in lieu of meeting

- **[[152]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-152
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where a written statement is
  submitted by a director under section 174 or by an auditor under
  subsection 321(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a resolution in writing signed by all the persons
    entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of shareholders or
    members is as valid as if it had been passed at a meeting of the
    shareholders or members; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a resolution in writing dealing with all matters
    required by this Act to be dealt with at a meeting of shareholders
    or members, and signed by all the persons entitled to vote at that
    meeting, satisfies all the requirements of this Act relating to
    meetings of shareholders or members.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing resolution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A copy of every resolution referred to in
  subsection (1) must be kept with the minutes of the meetings.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless a ballot is demanded, an entry in the minutes
  of a meeting that the chairperson declared a resolution to be carried
  or defeated is in the absence of evidence to the contrary proof of
  that fact without proof of the number or proportion of votes recorded
  in favour of or against the resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 152
- 2005, c. 54, s. 24
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1962
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-152-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 152"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requisitioned meeting

- **[[153]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-153
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Shareholders who together hold not
  less than 5 per cent of the issued and outstanding shares of a bank
  that carry the right to vote at a meeting sought to be held may
  requisition the directors to call a meeting of shareholders for the
  purposes stated in the requisition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requisitioned meeting --- members

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} At least two members entitled to vote at a meeting
  of a federal credit union that is sought to be held, or one per cent
  of the total number of members entitled to vote at a meeting of a
  federal credit union that is sought to be held, whichever is greater,
  may requisition the directors to call a meeting of members, or of
  members and shareholders, for the purposes stated in the requisition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The requisition

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} must state the business to be transacted at the
    meeting and must be sent to each director and to the head office of
    the bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may consist of several documents of like form, each
    signed by one or more shareholders or members, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors calling meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of the requisition, the directors must
  call a meeting of shareholders or members, as the case may be, to
  transact the business stated in the requisition, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a record date has been fixed under paragraph
    137(5)(c) and notice of it has been given under subsection 137(7);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors have called a meeting of shareholders
    or members, as the case may be, and have given the notice required
    by section 138; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business of the meeting as stated in the
    requisition includes matters described in paragraphs 143(5)(b)
    to (e) or 144.1(8)(b) to (e).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power of others to call meeting

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the directors do not call a meeting within 21 days
  after receiving the requisition, any person who signed the requisition
  may call the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A meeting called under this section shall be called
  as nearly as possible in the manner in which meetings are to be called
  pursuant to the by-laws and this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reimbursement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Unless the shareholders or members, as the case may
  be, otherwise resolve at a meeting called under subsection (4), the
  bank must reimburse the shareholders or members for any expenses
  reasonably incurred by them in requisitioning, calling and holding the
  meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 153
- 2005, c. 54, s. 25
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1963
:::

[Previous
Version](section-153-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 153"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may order meeting to be called

- **[[154]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-154 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  court may, on the application of a director of a bank, a person who is
  entitled to vote at a meeting of shareholders or members of a bank or
  the Superintendent, order a meeting to be called, held or conducted in
  the manner that the court directs if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is impracticable to call the meeting within the
    time or in the manner in which it is to be called;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is impracticable to conduct the meeting in the
    manner required by this Act or the by-laws; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the court thinks that the meeting ought to be
    called, held or conducted within the time or in the manner that it
    directs for any other reason.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Varying quorum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without restricting the generality of subsection (1),
  a court may order that the quorum required by the by-laws or this Act
  be varied or dispensed with at a meeting called, held and conducted
  pursuant to this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Valid meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A meeting called, held and conducted under this
  section is for all purposes a meeting of shareholders or members, as
  the case may be, of the bank duly called, held and conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 154
- 2005, c. 54, s. 26
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1964
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-154-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 154"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court review of election

- **[[155]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-155 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank or any of its shareholders, members or directors may apply to a
  court to resolve any dispute in respect of the election or appointment
  of a director or an auditor of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On an application under subsection (1), a court may
  make any order it thinks fit including, without limiting the
  generality of the foregoing,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an order restraining a director or auditor whose
    election or appointment is challenged from acting pending
    determination of the dispute;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an order declaring the result of the disputed
    election or appointment;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an order requiring a new election or appointment,
    and including in the order directions for the management of the
    business and affairs of the bank until a new election is held or the
    new appointment is made;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an order determining the voting rights of
    shareholders and of persons claiming to own shares; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an order determining the voting rights of members
    and of persons claiming to be members.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 155
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1965
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-155-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 155"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

- **[[156]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who makes an application under subsection 154(1) or 155(1)
  shall give notice of the application to the Superintendent before the
  hearing and shall deliver a copy of the order of the court, if any, to
  the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent representation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may appear and be heard in person
  or by counsel at the hearing of an application referred to in
  subsection (1).

### [Proxies]{.HTitleText2} {#h-12163 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[156.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.01 .sectionLabel}** The definitions
in this section apply in this section and sections 156.02 to 156.08.

[[intermediary]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[intermediary]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who holds a
    security on behalf of another person who is not the registered
    holder of the security, and includes

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a securities broker or dealer required to be
      registered to trade or deal in securities under the laws of any
      jurisdiction;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a securities depositary;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a financial institution;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a clearing agency, a securities
      dealer, trust company, association within the meaning of section 2
      of the [Cooperative Credit Associations Act](/eng/acts/C-41.01),
      bank or other person, including another clearing agency, on whose
      behalf the clearing agency or its nominee holds securities of an
      issuer;

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a trustee or administrator of a self-administered
      retirement savings plan, retirement income fund or education
      savings plan or another similar self-administered savings or
      investment plan that is registered under the [Income Tax
      Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3);

    - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a nominee of a person referred to in any of
      paragraphs (a) to (e); and

    - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a person who performs functions similar to those
      performed by a person referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e)
      and holds a security registered in their name, or in the name of
      their nominee, on behalf of another person who is not the
      registered holder of the
      security. ([intermédiaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[registrant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[registrant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2005, c. 54, s.
    27\]]{.Repealed}

[[solicitation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[solicitation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} includes

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a request for a proxy whether or not
        accompanied by or included in a form of proxy,

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a request to execute or not to execute or, in
        Quebec, to sign or not to sign a form of proxy or to revoke a
        proxy,

      - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the sending of a form of proxy or other
        communication to a shareholder under circumstances reasonably
        calculated to result in the procurement, withholding or
        revocation of a proxy, and

      - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the sending of a form of proxy to a
        shareholder under subsection 156.04(1); but

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not include

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the sending of a form of proxy in response to
        an unsolicited request made by or on behalf of a shareholder,

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the performance of administrative acts or
        professional services on behalf of a person soliciting a proxy,

      - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the sending by an intermediary of the
        documents referred to in subsection 156.07(1),

      - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a solicitation by a person in respect of
        shares of which they are the beneficial owner,

      - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a prescribed public announcement by a
        shareholder of how they intend to vote and the reasons for that
        decision,

      - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} a communication for the purpose of obtaining
        the support of persons in accordance with paragraph 143(1.1)(b),
        or

      - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} a communication, other than a solicitation by
        or on behalf of the management of a bank, that is made to
        shareholders in the prescribed
        circumstances. ([sollicitation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[solicitation by or on behalf of the management of a bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[solicitation by or on behalf of the management of a
    bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a solicitation by any person
    pursuant to a resolution or instruction of, or with the acquiescence
    of, the directors or a committee of the directors of the
    bank. ([sollicitation effectuée par la direction d'une banque ou
    pour son compte]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
- 2005, c. 54, s. 27
- [2019, c. 29, s. 91(E)](#1033260-1485890){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1033260-1485890.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-156.01-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 156.01"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointing proxyholder

- **[[156.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder who is entitled to
  vote at a meeting of shareholders may, by executing a form of proxy,
  appoint a proxyholder or one or more alternate proxyholders, who are
  not required to be shareholders, to attend and act at the meeting in
  the manner and to the extent authorized by the proxy and with the
  authority conferred by the proxy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Execution of proxy

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A form of proxy shall be executed by a shareholder or
  by a shareholder's attorney authorized in writing to do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on authority

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No appointment of a proxyholder provides authority
  for the proxyholder to act in respect of the appointment of an auditor
  or the election of a director unless a nominee proposed in good faith
  for the appointment or election is named in the form of proxy, a
  management proxy circular, a dissident's proxy circular or a proposal
  under subsection 143(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required information

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A form of proxy must indicate, in bold-face type,
  that the shareholder by whom or on whose behalf it is executed may
  appoint a proxyholder, other than a person designated in the form of
  proxy, to attend and act on the shareholder's behalf at a meeting to
  which the proxy relates, and must contain instructions as to the
  manner in which the shareholder may do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of proxy

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A proxy is valid only at the meeting in respect of
  which it is given or at a continuation of the meeting after an
  adjournment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation of proxy

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder may revoke a proxy

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by depositing an instrument in writing executed by
    the shareholder or by the shareholder's attorney authorized in
    writing to do so

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} at the head office of the bank at any time up to
      and including the last business day before the day of a meeting,
      or a continuation of the meeting after an adjournment, at which
      the proxy is to be used, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} with the chairperson of the meeting on the day
      of the meeting or a continuation of the meeting after an
      adjournment; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other manner permitted by law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deposit of proxies

**[[156.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.03 .sectionLabel}** The directors may
specify, in a notice calling a meeting of shareholders or a continuation
of a meeting of shareholders after an adjournment, a time before which
executed forms of proxy to be used at the meeting or the continued
meeting must be deposited with the bank or its transfer agent. The time
specified may not be more than forty-eight hours, excluding Saturdays
and holidays, before the meeting or the continued meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory solicitation

- **[[156.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and
  140(2), the management of a bank shall, concurrently with sending
  notice of a meeting of shareholders, send a form of proxy that is in
  accordance with the regulations to each shareholder entitled to
  receive notice of the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The management of a bank is not required to send a
  form of proxy under subsection (1) if the bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is not a distributing bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has 50 or fewer shareholders who are entitled to
    vote at a meeting, two or more joint holders of a share being
    counted as one shareholder.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
- 2005, c. 54, s. 28
- [2019, c. 29, s. 88](#1155590-1170880){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1155590-1170880.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156.04-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 156.04"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Soliciting proxies

- **[[156.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person shall not solicit proxies
  unless a proxy circular that is in accordance with the regulations is
  sent to the auditor or auditors of the bank, to each shareholder whose
  proxy is solicited and, in the case set out in paragraph (b), to the
  bank as follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of solicitation by or on behalf of the
    management of a bank, a management proxy circular, either as an
    appendix to or as a separate document accompanying the notice of
    meeting; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any other solicitation, a
    dissident's proxy circular stating the purposes of the solicitation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- limited solicitation

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may solicit
  proxies, other than by or on behalf of the management of a bank,
  without sending a dissident's proxy circular, if the total number of
  shareholders whose proxies are solicited is 15 or fewer, with two or
  more joint holders being counted as one shareholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- solicitation by public
  broadcast

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may solicit
  proxies, other than by or on behalf of the management of a bank,
  without sending a dissident's proxy circular if the solicitation is,
  in the prescribed circumstances, conveyed by public broadcast, speech
  or publication.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy to Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who sends a management proxy circular or
  dissident's proxy circular shall concurrently send to the
  Superintendent a copy of it together with the form of proxy, any other
  documents for use in connection with the meeting and, in the case of a
  management proxy circular, a copy of the notice of meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the application of an interested person, the
  Superintendent may, on any terms that the Superintendent thinks fit,
  exempt the person from any of the requirements of subsection (1) and
  section 156.04, and the exemption may be given retroactive effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of exemptions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall publish in a publication
  generally available to the public, a notice of a decision made by the
  Superintendent granting an exemption under subsection (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
- [2019, c. 29, s. 89](#1155594-1170892){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1155594-1170892.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156.05-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 156.05"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance at meeting

- **[[156.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who solicits a proxy and is
  appointed proxyholder shall attend in person or cause an alternate
  proxyholder to attend the meeting in respect of which the proxy is
  valid, and the proxyholder or alternate proxyholder shall comply with
  the directions of the shareholder who executed the form of proxy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rights of proxyholder

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A proxyholder or an alternate proxyholder has the
  same rights as the appointing shareholder to speak at a meeting of
  shareholders in respect of any matter, to vote by way of ballot at the
  meeting and, except where a proxyholder or an alternate proxyholder
  has conflicting instructions from more than one shareholder, to vote
  at the meeting in respect of any matter by way of a show of hands.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vote by show of hands

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections (1) and (2) and unless a
  shareholder or proxyholder demands a ballot, if the chairperson of a
  meeting of shareholders declares to the meeting that, if a ballot were
  conducted, the total number of votes attached to shares represented at
  the meeting by proxy required to be voted against what, to the
  knowledge of the chairperson, would be the decision of the meeting on
  a matter or group of matters is less than 5% of all the votes that
  might be cast by shareholders in person or by proxy,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the chairperson may conduct the vote in respect of
    that matter or group of matters by way of a show of hands; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a proxyholder or alternate proxyholder may vote in
    respect of that matter or group of matters by way of a show of
    hands.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
- 2005, c. 54, s. 30
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156.06-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 156.06"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of intermediary

- **[[156.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Shares of a bank that are registered
  in the name of an intermediary or an intermediary's nominee and not
  beneficially owned by the intermediary may not be voted unless the
  intermediary sends to the beneficial owner

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the notice of the meeting, annual
    statement, management proxy circular and dissident's proxy circular
    and any other documents, other than the form of proxy, that were
    sent to shareholders by or on behalf of any person for use in
    connection with the meeting; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a written request for voting instructions except if
    the intermediary has already received written voting instructions
    from the beneficial owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When documents to be sent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The intermediary shall send the documents referred to
  in subsection (1) without delay after they receive the documents
  referred to in paragraph (1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on voting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An intermediary or a proxyholder appointed by them
  may not vote shares that the intermediary does not beneficially own
  and that are registered in the name of the intermediary or their
  nominee unless the intermediary or proxyholder, as the case may be,
  receives written voting instructions from the beneficial owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person by or on behalf of whom a solicitation is
  made shall on request and without delay provide the intermediary, at
  the person's expense, with the necessary number of copies of the
  documents referred to in paragraph (1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Instructions to intermediary

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The intermediary shall vote or appoint a proxyholder
  to vote in accordance with any written voting instructions received
  from the beneficial owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Beneficial owner as proxyholder

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a beneficial owner so requests and provides an
  intermediary with the appropriate documentation, the intermediary
  shall appoint the beneficial owner or a nominee of the beneficial
  owner as proxyholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of intermediary's failure to
  comply

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The failure of an intermediary to comply with any of
  subsections (1) to (6) does not render void any meeting of
  shareholders or any action taken at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Intermediary may not vote

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this Part gives an intermediary the right
  to vote shares that they are otherwise prohibited from voting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
- 2005, c. 54, s. 31
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156.07-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 156.07"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

**[[156.071]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.071 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the powers that may be granted by a
  shareholder in a form of proxy;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting proxy circulars and forms of proxy,
  including the form and content of those documents; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting the conditions under which a bank is
  exempt from any of the requirements of sections 156.02 to 156.07.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 31
- [2019, c. 29, s. 90](#1155603-1170898){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1155603-1170898.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156.071-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 156.071"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restraining order

- **[[156.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a form of proxy, management proxy
  circular or dissident's proxy circular contains an untrue statement of
  a material fact or omits to state a material fact that is required to
  be contained in it or that is necessary to make a statement contained
  in it not misleading in light of the circumstances in which the
  statement is made, an interested person or the Superintendent may
  apply to a court and the court may make any order it thinks fit,
  including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an order restraining the solicitation or the
    holding of the meeting, or restraining any person from implementing
    or acting on a resolution passed at the meeting, to which the form
    of proxy, management proxy circular or dissident's proxy circular
    relates;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an order requiring correction of any form of proxy
    or proxy circular and a further solicitation; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an order adjourning the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a person other than the Superintendent is an
  applicant under subsection (1), the applicant shall give notice of the
  application to the Superintendent and the Superintendent is entitled
  to appear and to be heard in person or by counsel.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 10
:::

### [Restrictions on Voting]{.HTitleText2} {#h-12281 .Subheading}

Meaning of [[eligible votes]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[156.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[eligible
  votes]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the total number of votes that may
  be cast by or on behalf of shareholders on a vote of shareholders or a
  vote of holders of a class or series of shares, as the case may be, in
  respect of any particular matter, calculated without regard to
  subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} At a meeting of shareholders of a bank with equity of
  twelve billion dollars or more, no person and no entity controlled by
  any person may, in respect of any vote of shareholders or holders of
  any class or series of shares of the bank, cast votes in respect of
  any shares beneficially owned by the person or the entity that are, in
  aggregate, more than 20 per cent of the eligible votes that may be
  cast in respect of that vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- federal credit union

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of a
  meeting of shareholders or members of a federal credit union.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proxyholders

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person who is a proxyholder for a person or for an
  entity controlled by a person may cast votes to which the proxy
  relates that the person or entity may not cast by reason of subsection
  (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a person is, with respect to a bank, a person
  referred to in subsection 375(1), subsections (2) and (3) do not apply
  with respect to votes cast by or on behalf of the person during any
  period that the person is entitled under section 375 to remain a major
  shareholder of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply in respect of
  votes cast by or on behalf of any entity that controls the bank or any
  entity that is controlled by an entity that controls the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of a vote
  held under section 218.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of vote

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A vote in respect of a particular matter is not
  invalid merely because a person voted contrary to subsection (2) or
  (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition of shareholdings

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} If, with respect to any bank, a person contravenes
  subsection (2) or (3), the Minister may, by order, direct the
  shareholder of the shares to which the contravention relates or any
  person controlled by that shareholder to dispose of any number of
  shares of the bank beneficially owned by any of those persons that the
  Minister specifies in the order, within the time specified in the
  order and in the proportion, if any, as between the shareholder and
  the persons controlled by that shareholder that is specified in the
  order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on voting rights

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister makes an order under subsection (8),
  the person to whom the order relates may not, in person or by proxy,
  exercise any voting rights that are attached to shares of the bank
  beneficially owned by the person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subsection (9) ceases to apply

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (9) ceases to apply in respect of a
  person when the shares to which the order relates have been disposed
  of.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reliance on number in notice

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of this section, a person is
  entitled to rely on the number of eligible votes set out in a notice
  of a meeting under subsection 138(1.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation of persons

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of this section, the Minister may,
  with respect to a particular bank, designate two or more persons who
  are parties to an agreement, commitment or understanding referred to
  in section 9 to be a single person.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 67
- 2007, c. 6, s. 132
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1966
- 2012, c. 5, s. 6
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156.09-20120524.html "Link to previous version of section 156.09"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Directors and Officers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-12311 .Subheading}

#### [Duties]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12312 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to manage

- **[[157]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-157
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, the directors
  of a bank shall manage or supervise the management of the business and
  affairs of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Specific duties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without limiting the generality of subsection (1),
  the directors of a bank shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish an audit committee to perform the duties
    referred to in subsections 194(3) and (4);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish a conduct review committee to perform the
    duties referred to in subsection 195(3);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish procedures to resolve conflicts of
    interest, including techniques for the identification of potential
    conflict situations and for restricting the use of confidential
    information;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} designate a committee of the board of directors to
    monitor the procedures referred to in paragraph (c);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} designate a committee of the board of directors to
    perform the duties set out in section 195.1; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 27, s. 316\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} establish investment and lending policies,
    standards and procedures in accordance with section 465.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Paragraphs (2)(a) and (b) do not apply to the
  directors of a bank if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all the voting shares of the bank are beneficially
    owned by a Canadian financial institution described in any of
    paragraphs (a) to (d) of the definition [[financial
    institution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 2; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the audit committee or conduct review committee of
    the financial institution performs for and on behalf of the bank all
    the functions that would otherwise be required to be performed by
    the audit committee or conduct review committee of the bank under
    this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 157
- 1997, c. 15, s. 11
- 2001, c. 9, s. 68(F)
- [2018, c. 27, s. 316](#1039538-1368996){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039538-1368996.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-157-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 157"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of care

- **[[158]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-158
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every director and officer of a bank
  in exercising any of the powers of a director or an officer and
  discharging any of the duties of a director or an officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} act honestly and in good faith with a view to the
    best interests of the bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} exercise the care, diligence and skill that a
    reasonably prudent person would exercise in comparable
    circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every director, officer and employee of a bank shall
  comply with this Act, the regulations, the bank's incorporating
  instrument and the by-laws of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No exculpation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No provision in any contract, in any resolution or in
  the by-laws of a bank relieves any director, officer or employee of
  the bank from the duty to act in accordance with this Act and the
  regulations or relieves a director, officer or employee from liability
  for a breach thereof.

#### [Qualification and Number --- Directors]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12340 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum number of directors

- **[[159]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-159 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall have at least seven directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Residency requirement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} At least one half of the directors of a bank that is
  a subsidiary of a foreign bank and a majority of the directors of any
  other bank must be, at the time of each director's election or
  appointment, resident Canadians.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 159
- 2001, c. 9, s. 69
- 2007, c. 6, s. 12
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-159-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 159"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors as members

**[[159.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-159.1 .sectionLabel}** Not less than two
thirds of the directors of a federal credit union, or any greater
proportion that is provided for by the by-laws, must be members of the
federal credit union or representatives of members of the federal credit
union.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1967
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualified persons

**[[160]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-160 .sectionLabel}** The following persons
are disqualified from being directors of a bank:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is less than eighteen years of age;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who is of unsound mind and has been so found
  by a court in Canada or elsewhere;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person who has the status of a bankrupt;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who is not a natural person;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a person who is prohibited by subsection 156.09(9) or
  section 392 or 401.3 from exercising voting rights attached to shares
  of the bank or whose voting rights attached to the shares are
  suspended under section 402.2 or subsection 973.03(4);

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an officer, director or full time
  employee of an entity that is prohibited by subsection 156.09(9) or
  section 392 or 401.3 from exercising voting rights attached to shares
  of the bank or whose voting rights attached to the shares are
  suspended under section 402.2 or subsection 973.03(4);

- [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an officer, director, employee or
  agent of --- or any other person acting on behalf of --- an eligible
  agent within the meaning of subsection 370(1);

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2013, c. 40, s. 161\]]{.Repealed}

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a minister of Her Majesty in right of Canada or in
  right of a province;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an agent or employee of the
  government of a foreign country or any political subdivision thereof;
  and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} if the bank is a federal credit union, a person who
  fails to meet any of the qualification requirements set out in its
  by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 160
- 1994, c. 47, s. 15
- 1997, c. 15, s. 12
- 2001, c. 9, s. 70
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1968
- 2012, c. 19, s. 330, c. 31, s. 109
- 2013, c. 40, s. 161
- [2023, c. 26, s. 540](#1410953-1415364){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1410953-1415364.html"}
:::

:::

**[[160.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-160.1 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2013,
c. 40, s. 162\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-160.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 160.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No shareholder requirement

**[[161]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-161 .sectionLabel}** A director of a bank is
not required to hold shares of the bank.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affiliated person

**[[162]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-162 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may make regulations specifying the circumstances under which a natural
person is affiliated with a bank for the purposes of this Act.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affiliated director determination

- **[[162.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-162.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding section 162, the
  Superintendent may determine that a particular director is affiliated
  with a bank for the purposes of this Act if, in the opinion of the
  Superintendent, the director has a significant or sufficient
  commercial, business or financial relationship with the bank or with
  an affiliate of the bank to the extent that the relationship can be
  construed as being material to the director and can reasonably be
  expected to affect the exercise of the director's best judgment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification by Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A determination by the Superintendent under
  subsection (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} becomes effective on the day of the next annual
    meeting of the persons who are entitled to elect directors unless a
    notice in writing by the Superintendent revoking the determination
    is received by the bank prior to that day; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ceases to be in effect on the day of the next
    annual meeting of those persons after a notice in writing by the
    Superintendent revoking the determination is received by the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 5
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1969
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-162.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 162.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unaffiliated directors

- **[[163]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-163 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} At
  the election of directors at each annual meeting of a bank and at all
  times until the day of the next annual meeting, no more than two
  thirds of the directors may be persons affiliated with the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply where all the voting
  shares of a bank, other than directors' qualifying shares, if any, are
  beneficially owned by a Canadian financial institution incorporated by
  or under an Act of Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of affiliation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), whether or not a
  person is affiliated with a bank is to be determined as at the day the
  notice of the annual meeting is sent under section 138 and that
  determination becomes effective on the day of that meeting, and a
  person is deemed to continue to be affiliated or unaffiliated, as the
  case may be, until the next annual meeting of the shareholders or
  members, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a bank
  that was in existence immediately prior to the day that subsection
  comes into force until the day that is three years after the day that
  subsection comes into force.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 163
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1970
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-163-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 163"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on directors

**[[164]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-164 .sectionLabel}** No more than 15 per
cent of the directors of a bank may, at each director's election or
appointment, be employees of the bank or a subsidiary of the bank,
except that up to four persons who are employees of the bank or a
subsidiary of the bank may be directors of the bank if those directors
constitute not more than one half of the directors of the bank.

#### [Election and Tenure --- Directors]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12394 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of directors

- **[[165]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-165
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 159(1) and
  sections 168 and 217, the directors of a bank that is not a federal
  credit union must, by by-law, determine the number of directors or the
  minimum and maximum number of directors, but no by-law that decreases
  the number of directors shortens the term of an incumbent director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of directors --- federal credit
  union

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 159(1), the members of a
  federal credit union must, by by-law, determine the number of
  directors or the minimum and maximum number of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election at annual meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A by-law made under subsection (1) or (2) that
  provides for a minimum and maximum number of directors may provide
  that the number of directors to be elected at any annual meeting of
  the shareholders or members, as the case may be, be the number that is
  fixed by the directors before the annual meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 165
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1971
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-165-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 165"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election or appointment as director

**[[165.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-165.1 .sectionLabel}** The election or
appointment of a person as a director is subject to the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person was present at the meeting when the
  election or appointment took place and did not refuse to hold office
  as a director; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person was not present at the meeting when the
  election or appointment took place but

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} consented in writing to hold office as a director
    before the election or appointment or within 10 days after it, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} acted as a director after the election or
    appointment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 32
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of directors

- **[[166]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-166
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where this Act or the by-laws
  of a bank provide for cumulative voting, a bank may, by by-law,
  provide that the directors be elected for terms of one, two or three
  years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of one, two or three years

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director elected for a term of one, two or three
  years holds office until the close, as the case may be, of the first,
  second or third annual meeting of shareholders or members, as the case
  may be, following the election of the director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No stated term

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director who is not elected for an expressly stated
  term of office ceases to hold office at the close of the next annual
  meeting of shareholders or members, as the case may be, following the
  election of the director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} It is not necessary that all directors elected at a
  meeting of shareholders or members hold office for the same term.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law of a bank provides that the directors be
  elected for a term of two or three years, it may also provide that the
  term of office of each director be for the whole of that term, or
  that, as nearly as may be, one half of the directors retire each year
  if the term is two years, and that one third of the directors retire
  each year if the term is three years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Composition requirements

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 163(4), if a director of a bank
  is elected or appointed for a term of more than one year, the bank
  must comply with subsections 159(2) and 163(1) and section 164 at each
  annual meeting of shareholders or members, as the case may be, during
  the director's term of office as if that director were elected or
  appointed on that date.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 166
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1972
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-166-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 166"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determining election of directors

- **[[167]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-167
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where this Act or the by-laws
  of a bank provide for cumulative voting, the persons, to the number
  authorized to be elected, who receive the greatest number of votes at
  an election of directors of a bank shall be the directors thereof.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at any election of directors referred to in
  subsection (1), two or more persons receive an equal number of votes
  and there are not sufficient vacancies remaining to enable all the
  persons receiving an equal number of votes to be elected, the
  directors who receive a greater number of votes or the majority of
  them shall, in order to complete the full number of directors,
  determine which of the persons so receiving an equal number of votes
  are to be elected.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cumulative voting

- **[[168]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-168
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where this Act or the by-laws
  provide for cumulative voting,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there shall be a stated number of directors fixed
    by by-law and not a minimum and maximum number of directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each shareholder entitled to vote at an election of
    directors has the right to cast a number of votes equal to the
    number of votes attached to the shares held by the shareholder
    multiplied by the number of directors to be elected, and the
    shareholder may cast all such votes in favour of one candidate or
    distribute them among the candidates in any manner;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a separate vote of shareholders shall be taken with
    respect to each candidate nominated for director unless a resolution
    is passed unanimously permitting two or more persons to be elected
    by a single vote;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a shareholder has voted for more than one
    candidate without specifying the distribution of the votes among the
    candidates, the shareholder is deemed to have distributed the votes
    equally among the candidates for whom the shareholder voted;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if the number of candidates nominated for director
    exceeds the number of positions to be filled, the candidates who
    receive the least number of votes shall be eliminated until the
    number of candidates remaining equals the number of positions to be
    filled;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} each director ceases to hold office at the close of
    the next annual meeting of shareholders following the director's
    election;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a director may be removed from office only if the
    number of votes cast in favour of a motion to remove the director is
    greater than the product of the number of directors required by the
    by-laws and the number of votes cast against the motion; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the number of directors required by the by-laws may
