    be decreased only if the number of votes cast in favour of a motion
    to decrease the number of directors is greater than the product of
    the number of directors required by the by-laws and the number of
    votes cast against the motion.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory cumulative voting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the aggregate of the voting shares beneficially
  owned by a person and any entities controlled by the person carries
  more than 10 per cent of the voting rights attached to all the
  outstanding voting shares of a bank, the directors shall be elected by
  cumulative voting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where all the voting shares of the bank that are
    outstanding are beneficially owned by

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one person,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one person and one or more entities controlled
      by that person, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} one or more entities controlled by the same
      person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a bank that was in existence
    immediately prior to the day that subsection comes into force whose
    shareholders are confined to entities incorporated or formed by or
    under an Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province that
    are, in the opinion of the directors, operating as credit unions or
    cooperative associations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply to a widely held bank
  with equity of twelve billion dollars or more or to a bank in respect
  of which subsection 378(1) applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional election

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where this Act or the by-laws of a bank provide for
  cumulative voting, the shareholders of the bank shall,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the first annual meeting of shareholders held
    not earlier than ninety days following the date that cumulative
    voting is required under subsection (2) or provided for in the
    by-laws, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at each succeeding annual meeting,

  elect the stated number of directors to hold office until the close of
  the next annual meeting of shareholders following their election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this Act precludes the holders of any
  class or series of shares of a bank from having an exclusive right to
  elect one or more directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 168
- 1997, c. 15, s. 14
- 2001, c. 9, s. 73
- 2005, c. 54, s. 33
- 2007, c. 6, s. 132
- 2012, c. 5, s. 7
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-168-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 168"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No cumulative voting

**[[168.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-168.1 .sectionLabel}** Despite section 168
or any provision of its by-laws, cumulative voting is not permitted in a
federal credit union.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1973
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Re-election of directors

**[[169]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-169 .sectionLabel}** A director who has
completed a term of office is, if otherwise qualified, eligible for
re-election.

#### [Incomplete Elections and Director Vacancies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12469 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Void election or appointment

- **[[170]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-170 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If,
  immediately after the time of any purported election or appointment of
  directors, the board of directors would fail to comply with subsection
  159(2) or 163(1) or section 164, the purported election or appointment
  of all persons purported to be elected or appointed at that time is
  void unless the directors, within forty-five days after the discovery
  of the non-compliance, develop a plan, approved by the Superintendent,
  to rectify the non-compliance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to elect minimum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at the close of a meeting of shareholders or
  members of a bank, the shareholders or members have failed to elect
  the number or minimum number of directors required by this Act or the
  by-laws of a bank, the purported election of directors at the meeting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is valid if the directors purported to be elected
    and those incumbent directors, if any, whose terms did not expire at
    the close of the meeting, together constitute a quorum; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is void if the directors purported to be elected
    and those incumbent directors, if any, whose terms did not expire at
    the close of the meeting, together do not constitute a quorum.

- [(3) and (4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 15\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 170
- 1997, c. 15, s. 15
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1974
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-170-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 170"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors where elections or appointments
incomplete or void

- **[[171]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-171
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections 166(2) and (3)
  and paragraphs 168(1)(f) and 172(1)(a), if subsection 170(1) or (2)
  applies at the close of any meeting of shareholders or members of a
  bank, the board of directors, until their successors are elected or
  appointed, consists solely of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where paragraph 170(2)(a) applies, the directors
    referred to in that paragraph; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where subsection 170(1) or paragraph 170(2)(b)
    applies, the persons who were the incumbent directors immediately
    before the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where there is no approved
  rectification plan

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding subsections 166(2) and (3) and
  paragraphs 168(1)(f) and 172(1)(a), where a plan to rectify the
  non-compliance referred to in subsection 170(1) has not been approved
  by the Superintendent by the end of the forty-five day period referred
  to in that subsection, the board of directors shall, until their
  successors are elected or appointed, consist solely of the persons who
  were the incumbent directors immediately before the meeting at which
  the purported election or appointment referred to in that subsection
  occurred.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors to call meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If subsection (1) or (2) applies, the board of
  directors referred to in that subsection must, without delay, call a
  special meeting of shareholders or members, as the case may be, to
  fill the vacancies if paragraph 170(2)(a) applies, or elect a new
  board of directors if subsection 170(1) or paragraph 170(2)(b)
  applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Others may call meeting

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the directors fail to call a special meeting
  required by subsection (3), the meeting may be called by any person
  who would be entitled to vote at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 171
- 1997, c. 15, s. 16
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1975
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-171-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 171"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ceasing to hold office

- **[[172]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-172 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director ceases to hold office

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the close of the annual meeting at which the
    director's term of office expires;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the director dies or resigns;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when the director becomes disqualified under
    section 160 or ineligible to hold office pursuant to subsection
    203(2);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} when the director is removed under section 173; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} when the director is removed from office under
    section 647 or 647.1.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Date of resignation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The resignation of a director of a bank becomes
  effective at the time a written resignation is sent to the bank by the
  director or at the time specified in the resignation, whichever is
  later.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 172
- 2001, c. 9, s. 74
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of director

- **[[173]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-173
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraph 168(1)(g), the
  shareholders of a bank that is not a federal credit union may by
  resolution at a special meeting of shareholders remove any director or
  all the directors from office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of director --- federal credit
  union

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A director of a federal credit union may be removed
  from office by resolution at a special meeting of the persons who are
  entitled to vote in the election of that director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the holders of any class or series of shares of
  a bank have the exclusive right to elect one or more directors, a
  director so elected may be removed only by a resolution at a meeting
  of the shareholders of that class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- members

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} If members of a federal credit union have the
  exclusive right to elect one or more directors, a director so elected
  may be removed only by a resolution of the members having that right.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vacancy by removal

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraphs 168(1)(b) to (e), a vacancy
  created by the removal of a director may be filled at the meeting of
  the shareholders or members, as the case may be, at which the director
  is removed or, if not so filled, may be filled under section 177 or
  178.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 173
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1976
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-173-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 173"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of director

- **[[174]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-174 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} resigns,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns of a meeting
    called for the purpose of removing the director from office, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns of a meeting
    of directors, shareholders or members at which another person is to
    be appointed or elected to fill the office of director, whether
    because of the director's resignation or removal or because the
    director's term of office has expired or is about to expire,

  is entitled to submit to the bank a written statement giving the
  reasons for the resignation or the reasons why the director opposes
  any proposed action or resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement re disagreement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a director resigns as a result of a
  disagreement with the other directors or the officers of a bank, the
  director shall submit to the bank and the Superintendent a written
  statement setting out the nature of the disagreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 174
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1977
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-174-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 174"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circulation of statement

- **[[175]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-175 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank that is not a federal credit union must without delay on receipt
  of a director's statement referred to in subsection 174(1) relating to
  a matter referred to in paragraph 174(1)(b) or (c), or a director's
  statement referred to in subsection 174(2), send a copy of it to each
  shareholder entitled to receive a notice of meetings and to the
  Superintendent, unless the statement is included in or attached to a
  management proxy circular required by subsection 156.05(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circulation of statement --- federal
  credit union

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A federal credit union must, without delay on receipt
  of a director's statement referred to in subsection 174(1) relating to
  a matter referred to in paragraph 174(1)(b) or (c), or a director's
  statement referred to in subsection 174(2), send a copy of it to the
  Superintendent, to each member and, if the director was elected by the
  holders of shares of a class, to those shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Immunity for statement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No bank or person acting on its behalf incurs any
  liability by reason only of circulating a director's statement in
  compliance with subsection (1) or (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 175
- 1997, c. 15, s. 17
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1978
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-175-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 175"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholders filling vacancy

- **[[176]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-176 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  by-laws of a bank that is not a federal credit union may provide that
  a vacancy among the directors is to be filled only

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by a vote of the shareholders; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a vote of the holders of any class or series of
    shares having an exclusive right to elect one or more directors if
    the vacancy occurs among the directors elected by the holders of
    that class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filling vacancy --- federal credit
  union

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The by-laws of a federal credit union may provide
  that a vacancy among its directors is to be filled by election or
  appointment by members only or by an election or appointment by
  persons having an exclusive right to elect or appoint one or more
  directors if the vacancy occurs among the directors appointed or
  elected by those persons.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 176
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1978
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-176-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 176"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors filling vacancy

- **[[177]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-177
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 183 but subject to
  subsection (2) and sections 176 and 178, a quorum of directors may
  fill a vacancy among the directors except a vacancy resulting from a
  change in the by-laws by which the number or the minimum or maximum
  number of directors is increased or from a failure to elect the number
  or minimum number of directors provided for in the by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where composition fails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding sections 176 and 183, where by reason
  of a vacancy the number of directors or the composition of the board
  of directors fails to meet any of the requirements of section 159,
  subsection 163(1) and section 164, the directors who, in the absence
  of any by-law, would be empowered to fill that vacancy shall do so
  forthwith.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 177
- 2005, c. 54, s. 34
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-177-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 177"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vacancy

**[[178]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-178 .sectionLabel}** Despite section 183, if
a class of persons have an exclusive right to elect one or more
directors and a vacancy occurs among those directors, then, subject to
section 176,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the remaining directors elected by those persons may
  fill the vacancy except one resulting from an increase in the number
  or the minimum or maximum number of directors who may be elected by
  that class from a failure to elect the number or minimum number of
  directors provided for in the by-laws for that class;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if there are no such remaining directors and, by
  reason of the vacancy, the number of directors or the composition of
  the board of directors fails to meet any of the requirements of
  section 159, subsection 163(1) and section 164, the other directors
  may fill that vacancy; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if there are no such remaining directors and
  paragraph (b) does not apply, any person of that class may call a
  meeting of the class for the purpose of filling the vacancy.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 178
- 2005, c. 54, s. 35
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1979
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-178-20060427.html "Link to previous version of section 178"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unexpired term

- **[[179]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-179
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise
  provide, a director elected or appointed to fill a vacancy holds
  office for the unexpired term of the director's predecessor in office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affiliation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding subsection 163(3), the affiliation of
  a person to be elected or appointed to fill a vacancy shall be
  determined as at the date of the person's election or appointment and
  that person shall be deemed to continue to be affiliated or
  unaffiliated, as the case may be, until the next annual meeting of the
  shareholders.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional directors

- **[[179.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-179.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The directors of a bank that is not
  a federal credit union may appoint one or more additional directors if
  the by-laws of the bank allow them to do so and the by-laws determine
  the minimum and maximum numbers of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of office

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director appointed under subsection (1) holds
  office for a term expiring not later than the close of the next annual
  meeting of shareholders of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on number appointed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The total number of directors appointed under
  subsection (1) may not exceed one third of the number of directors
  elected at the previous annual meeting of shareholders of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 18
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1980
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-179.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 179.1"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Meetings of the Board]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12575 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meetings required

- **[[180]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-180 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors shall meet at least four times during each financial year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place for meetings

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors may meet at any place unless the
  by-laws provide otherwise.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice for meetings

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The notice for the meetings must be given as required
  by the by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 180
- 1997, c. 15, s. 19
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of meeting

- **[[181]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-181 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  notice of a meeting of directors shall specify each matter referred to
  in section 198 that is to be dealt with at the meeting but, unless the
  by-laws otherwise provide, need not otherwise specify the purpose of
  or the business to be transacted at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver of notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director may in any manner waive notice of a
  meeting of directors and the attendance of a director at a meeting of
  directors is a waiver of notice of that meeting except where the
  director attends the meeting for the express purpose of objecting to
  the transaction of any business on the grounds that the meeting is not
  lawfully called.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjourned meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notice of an adjourned meeting of directors is not
  required to be given if the time and place of the adjourned meeting
  was announced at the original meeting.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum

- **[[182]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-182
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 183, the number
  of directors referred to in subsection (2) constitutes a quorum at any
  meeting of directors or a committee of directors and, notwithstanding
  any vacancy among the directors, a quorum of directors may exercise
  all the powers of the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The number of directors constituting a quorum at any
  meeting of directors or a committee of directors shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a majority of the minimum number of directors
    required by this Act for the board of directors or a committee of
    directors; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} such greater number of directors than the number
    calculated pursuant to paragraph (a) as may be established by the
    by-laws of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director continues to be present

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director who is present at a meeting of directors
  or of a committee of directors but is not, in accordance with
  subsection 203(1), present at any particular time during the meeting
  is considered to be present for the purposes of this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 182
- 2005, c. 54, s. 36
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-182-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 182"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resident Canadian majority

- **[[183]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-183 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a bank shall not transact business at a meeting of
  directors unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a bank that is a subsidiary of a
    foreign bank, at least one half of the directors present are
    resident Canadians; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, a majority of the directors
    present are resident Canadians.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the directors of a bank may
  transact business at a meeting of directors without the required
  proportion of directors who are resident Canadians if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a director who is a resident Canadian unable to be
    present approves, in writing or by telephonic, electronic or other
    communications facilities, the business transacted at the meeting;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there would have been present the required
    proportion of directors who are resident Canadians had that director
    been present at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 183
- 2001, c. 9, s. 75
- 2013, c. 33, s. 105
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-183-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 183"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors of federal credit union

**[[183.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-183.01 .sectionLabel}** The directors of
a federal credit union that has issued shares that provide for the
election of directors must not transact business at a meeting of
directors or of a committee of directors unless the majority of the
directors present at the meeting are members.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1981
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Presence of unaffiliated director

- **[[183.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-183.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The directors of a bank shall not
  transact business at a meeting of directors unless at least one of the
  directors who is not affiliated with the bank is present.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the directors of a bank may
  transact business at a meeting of directors if a director who is not
  affiliated with the bank and who is not able to be present approves,
  in writing or by telephonic, electronic or other communications
  facilities, the business transacted at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if all the voting
  shares of the bank, other than directors' qualifying shares, if any,
  are beneficially owned by a Canadian financial institution
  incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic meeting

- **[[184]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-184
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the by-laws of a bank, a
  meeting of directors or of a committee of directors may be held by
  means of such telephonic, electronic or other communications
  facilities as permit all persons participating in the meeting to
  communicate adequately with each other during the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed present

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director participating in a meeting by any means
  referred to in subsection (1) is deemed for the purposes of this Act
  to be present at that meeting.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution outside board meeting

- **[[184.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-184.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A resolution in writing signed by
  all the directors entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of
  directors is as valid as if it had been passed at a meeting of
  directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing directors' resolution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the resolution referred to in
  subsection (1) shall be kept with the minutes of the proceedings of
  the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution outside committee meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A resolution in writing signed by all the directors
  entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of a committee of
  directors, other than a resolution of the audit committee in carrying
  out its duties under subsection 194(3) or a resolution of the conduct
  review committee in carrying out its duties under subsection 195(3),
  is as valid as if it had been passed at a meeting of that committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing committee resolution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the resolution referred to in
  subsection (3) shall be kept with the minutes of the proceedings of
  that committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Unless a ballot is demanded, an entry in the minutes
  of a meeting that the chairperson declared a resolution to be carried
  or defeated is in the absence of evidence to the contrary proof of
  that fact without proof of the number or proportion of votes recorded
  in favour of or against the resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 20
- 2005, c. 54, s. 37
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-184.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 184.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissent of director

- **[[185]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-185 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director of a bank who is present at a meeting of directors or a
  committee of directors is deemed to have consented to any resolution
  passed or action taken at that meeting unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director requests that the director's dissent
    be entered or the director's dissent is entered in the minutes of
    the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the director sends a written dissent to the
    secretary of the meeting before the meeting is adjourned; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the director sends the director's dissent by
    registered mail or delivers it to the head office of the bank
    immediately after the meeting is adjourned.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loss of right to dissent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director of a bank who votes for or consents to a
  resolution is not entitled to dissent under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissent of absent director

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director of a bank who is not present at a meeting
  at which a resolution is passed or action taken is deemed to have
  consented thereto unless, within seven days after the director becomes
  aware of the resolution, the director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} causes the director's dissent to be placed with the
    minutes of the meeting; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sends the director's dissent by registered mail or
    delivers it to the head office of the bank.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record of attendance

- **[[186]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-186 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall keep a record of the attendance at each meeting of
  directors and each committee meeting of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement to shareholders and members

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank must attach to the notice of each annual
  meeting it sends to its shareholders or members, as the case may be, a
  statement showing, in respect of the financial year immediately
  preceding the meeting, the total number of directors' meetings and
  directors' committee meetings held during the financial year and the
  number of those meetings attended by each director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 186
- 1997, c. 15, s. 21
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1982
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-186-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 186"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meeting required by Superintendent

- **[[187]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-187
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where in the opinion of the
  Superintendent it is necessary, the Superintendent may, by notice in
  writing, require a bank to hold a meeting of directors of the bank to
  consider the matters set out in the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance of Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may attend and be heard at a
  meeting referred to in subsection (1).

#### [By-laws]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12669 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws

- **[[188]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-188
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless this Act otherwise provides,
  the directors of a bank that is not a federal credit union may by
  resolution make, amend or repeal any by-law that regulates the
  business or affairs of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors shall submit a by-law, or an amendment
  to or a repeal of a by-law, that is made under subsection (1) to the
  shareholders at the next meeting of shareholders, and the shareholders
  may, by resolution, confirm or amend the by-law, amendment or repeal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless this Act otherwise provides, a by-law, or an
  amendment to or a repeal of a by-law, is effective from the date of
  the resolution of the directors under subsection (1) until it is
  confirmed, confirmed as amended or rejected by the shareholders under
  subsection (2) or until it ceases to be effective under subsection (4)
  and, where the by-law is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, it
  continues in effect in the form in which it was so confirmed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect where no shareholder approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law, or an amendment to or a repeal of a
  by-law, is rejected by the shareholders, or is not submitted to the
  shareholders by the directors as required under subsection (2), the
  by-law, amendment or repeal ceases to be effective from the date of
  its rejection or the date of the next meeting of shareholders, as the
  case may be, and no subsequent resolution of the directors to make,
  amend or repeal a by-law having substantially the same purpose or
  effect is effective until it is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, by
  the shareholders.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 188
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1983
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-188-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 188"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder proposal of by-law

**[[189]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-189 .sectionLabel}** A shareholder entitled
to vote at an annual meeting of shareholders may, in accordance with
sections 143 and 144, make a proposal to make, amend or repeal a by-law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 189
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1984(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-189-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 189"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws of existing bank

**[[190]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-190 .sectionLabel}** Subject to section 191,
where a by-law of a bank that was in existence immediately prior to the
day this section comes into force was in effect immediately prior to
that day, the by-law continues in effect until amended or repealed,
unless it is contrary to a provision of this Act.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws re remuneration

- **[[191]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-191 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  by-law of a bank respecting the remuneration of the directors of the
  bank, as directors, that is in effect on the coming into force of this
  section ceases to have effect on the day on which the first annual
  meeting is held following the coming into force of this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Existing by-laws

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A by-law made by the directors of a bank under
  section 45 of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), being chapter B-1 of
  the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, as that section read immediately
  prior to the day this section comes into force, and not confirmed by
  the shareholders of the bank in accordance with that section on or
  before the day this section comes into force, continues to have
  effect, unless it is contrary to the provisions of this Act, until the
  first meeting of the shareholders following the day this section comes
  into force.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A by-law referred to in subsection (2) shall be
  submitted to the shareholders at the first meeting of shareholders
  following the coming into force of this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of ss. 188(3) and (4) and
  189

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 188(3) and (4) and section 189 apply in
  respect of a by-law referred to in this section as if it were a by-law
  made under section 188.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed by-laws

- **[[192]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  matter that,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately prior to the day this section comes
    into force, was provided for in the incorporating instrument of a
    bank that was in existence immediately prior to that day, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} immediately prior to the day a body corporate is
    continued as a bank other than a federal credit union, was provided
    for in the incorporating instrument of the body corporate,

  and that, under this Act, would be provided for in the by-laws of a
  bank, is deemed to be provided for in the by-laws of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law prevails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a by-law of the bank made in accordance with
  sections 188 and 189 amends or repeals any matter referred to in
  subsection (1), the by-law prevails.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 192
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1985
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-192-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 192"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws --- mandatory provisions

- **[[192.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The by-laws of a federal credit
  union must provide for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the qualifications of members and the procedures
    for acceptance of members;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the membership obligations of members, including
    any obligation to use the services of the federal credit union and
    any fees to be paid by members;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the rights of joint members, if any;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the fact that a delegate has only one vote even
    though the delegate is a member or represents more than one member;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the limit, if any, on the number of membership
    shares;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the selection, qualifications, term of office and
    removal of directors and members of committees of directors;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the manner of distribution of any surplus earnings
    arising from the operations of the federal credit union;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the rights of withdrawing members and members who
    are expelled;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the federal credit union wishes to permit
    members or shareholders to attend a meeting of the federal credit
    union by means of a communication facility referred to in subsection
    136(2), the ways in which votes must be held; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the federal credit union's
    financial year ends.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws --- other provisions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The by-laws of a federal credit union may provide for
  any other matter that the members consider necessary or desirable,
  including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} restrictions on the classes of persons to which
    membership may be available, as long as the restrictions are
    consistent with applicable laws with respect to human rights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the representation of members by delegates;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the distribution of patronage allocations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manner of distribution of any remaining
    property on the voluntary liquidation and dissolution of the federal
    credit union;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a formula for calculating the value of membership
    shares;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a formula for calculating the redemption price of
    membership shares; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} voting by mail.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Selection and removal of delegates

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the by-laws of a federal credit union provide for
  the representation of members by delegates, the by-laws must set out
  procedures for their selection and removal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies

- **[[192.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each member and shareholder of a
  federal credit union may on request, not more than once in each
  calendar year, receive free of charge one copy of the letters patent
  and by-laws of the federal credit union, and one copy of any
  amendments to them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The federal credit union must provide each creditor,
  and, if the federal credit union is a distributing federal credit
  union, any other person, on payment of a reasonable fee, with a copy
  of the federal credit union's letters patent and by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Making or amendment of by-law by members

- **[[192.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The members of a federal credit
  union may, by special resolution, make, amend or repeal any by-law
  that regulates the business and affairs of the federal credit union,
  including a by-law changing the federal credit union's name or the
  province in which its head office is situated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Making or amendment of by-law by
  directors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws of a federal credit union provide
  otherwise, the directors may, by special resolution, make a by-law or
  amend a by-law of the federal credit union, including a by-law
  changing the federal credit union's name or the province in which its
  head office is situated, but only if the by-law or amendment is not
  contrary to a by-law made by the members.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The directors must present a by-law or an amendment
  to a by-law that is made under subsection (2) to the members at the
  next meeting of members and the members may, by special resolution,
  confirm or amend it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law not confirmed

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law or an amendment to a by-law made by the
  directors is not confirmed, with or without amendments, under
  subsection (3), the by-law or amendment is repealed as of the date of
  the meeting of members at which it was not confirmed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law, or an amendment to or a repeal of a
  by-law, made under subsection (1) or (2) does any thing referred to in
  subsection 218(1) in relation to any class or series of shares, the
  by-law, amendment or repeal is not effective until it is confirmed or
  confirmed as amended by the holders of shares of that class or series
  in accordance with section 218.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law or an amendment to a by-law made under
  subsection (1) or (2) changes the name of the federal credit union,
  the by-law or the amendment is not effective until it is approved by
  the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the name of a federal credit union or the province
  in which its head office is situated is changed under subsection (1)
  or (2), the Superintendent may issue letters patent to amend the
  federal credit union's incorporating instrument accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent issued under subsection (7) become
  effective on the day stated in the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal of by-law

**[[192.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.04 .sectionLabel}** A member may, in
accordance with section 144.1, make a proposal to make, amend or repeal
a by-law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

- **[[192.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A by-law or an amendment to or
  repeal of a by-law made by the members is effective from the later of
  the date of the resolution made under subsection 192.03(1) and the
  date specified in the by-law, amendment or repeal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A by-law or an amendment to a by-law made by the
  directors of a federal credit union is effective from the later of the
  date the by-law is made or amended by the directors and the date
  specified in the by-law, until it is confirmed, with or without
  amendment, under subsection 192.03(3) or repealed under subsection
  192.03(4) and, if the by-law is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, it
  is in effect in the form in which it was so confirmed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}If by-law not approved

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law or an amendment to a by-law made by the
  directors under subsection 192.03(2) is not submitted by the directors
  to the next meeting of the members as required under subsection
  192.03(3), the by-law or amendment ceases to be effective from the
  date of that meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New resolution of directors

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law or an amendment to a by-law made by the
  directors under subsection 192.03(2) is repealed under subsection
  192.03(4) or ceases to be effective under subsection (3), no
  subsequent resolution of the directors to make or amend a by-law that
  has substantially the same purpose or effect is effective until it is
  confirmed, or confirmed as amended, by the members.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws of continued body corporate

**[[192.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.06 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 192.05, the by-laws of a body corporate that is continued as a
federal credit union under this Act continue in effect until amended or
repealed, unless contrary to a provision of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Existing resolutions

**[[192.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.07 .sectionLabel}** If the
remuneration of directors of a body corporate that is continued as a
federal credit union was, immediately before the issuance of the federal
credit union's letters patent, fixed by a resolution of the directors,
that resolution continues to have effect, unless it is contrary to the
provisions of this Act, until the first meeting of the federal credit
union's members.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed by-laws

- **[[192.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any matter provided for in the
  incorporating instrument of a body corporate that is continued as a
  federal credit union that, under this Act, is to be provided for in
  the by-laws of a federal credit union is deemed to be provided for in
  the by-laws of the federal credit union.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law prevails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law of the federal credit union made in
  accordance with section 192.03 amends or repeals any matter referred
  to in subsection (1), the by-law prevails.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rights preserved

**[[192.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.09 .sectionLabel}** No amendment to
the letters patent or by-laws of a federal credit union affects an
existing cause of action or claim or liability to prosecution in favour
of or against the federal credit union or its directors or officers, or
any civil, criminal or administrative action or proceeding to which the
federal credit union or any of its directors or officers are a party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws binding

**[[192.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-192.1 .sectionLabel}** Subject to this
Act, every by-law of a federal credit union binds the federal credit
union and its members to the same extent as if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} each member had duly approved the by-law; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} there were in the by-law a covenant under seal on the
  part of each member, and the successors and assigns of the member, to
  conform to the by-law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1986
:::

#### [Committees of the Board]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12798 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committees

**[[193]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-193 .sectionLabel}** The directors of a bank
may appoint from their number, in addition to the committees referred to
in subsection 157(2), such other committees as they deem necessary and,
subject to section 198, delegate to those committees such powers of the
directors, and assign to those committees such duties, as the directors
consider appropriate.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Audit committee

- **[[194]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-194 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  audit committee of a bank shall consist of at least three directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Membership

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A majority of the members of the audit committee must
  consist of directors who are not persons affiliated with the bank and
  none of the members of the audit committee may be officers or
  employees of the bank or a subsidiary of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of audit committee

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The audit committee of a bank shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} review the annual statement of the bank before the
    annual statement is approved by the directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review such returns of the bank as the
    Superintendent may specify;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the bank to implement and
    maintain appropriate internal control procedures;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} review, evaluate and approve those procedures;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} review such investments and transactions that could
    adversely affect the well-being of the bank as the auditor or
    auditors or any officer of the bank may bring to the attention of
    the committee;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} meet with the auditor or auditors to discuss the
    annual statement and the returns and transactions referred to in
    this subsection; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} meet with the chief internal auditor of the bank,
    or the officer or employee of the bank acting in a similar capacity,
    and with management of the bank, to discuss the effectiveness of the
    internal control procedures established for the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of the annual statement and returns of a
  bank that under this Act must be approved by the directors of the
  bank, the audit committee of the bank shall report thereon to the
  directors before the approval is given.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required meeting of directors

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The audit committee of a bank may call a meeting of
  the directors of the bank to consider any matter of concern to the
  committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2), in so far as it relates to the
  affiliation of directors with the bank, does not apply in respect of a
  bank that was in existence immediately prior to the day that
  subsection comes into force until the day that is three years after
  the day that subsection comes into force.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 194
- 1997, c. 15, s. 22
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conduct review committee

- **[[195]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-195 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  conduct review committee of a bank shall consist of at least three
  directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Membership

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A majority of the members of the conduct review
  committee of a bank must consist of directors who are not persons
  affiliated with the bank and none of the members of the conduct review
  committee may be officers or employees of the bank or a subsidiary of
  the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of conduct review committee

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The conduct review committee of a bank shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the bank to establish
    procedures for complying with Part XI;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review those procedures and their effectiveness in
    ensuring that the bank is complying with Part XI;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} if a widely held bank holding company or a widely
    held insurance holding company has a significant interest in any
    class of shares of the bank,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} establish policies for entering into transactions
      referred to in subsection 495.1(1), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} review transactions referred to in subsection
      495.3(1); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} review the practices of the bank to ensure that any
    transactions with related parties of the bank that may have a
    material effect on the stability or solvency of the bank are
    identified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bank report to Superintendent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A bank shall report to the Superintendent on the
  mandate and responsibilities of the conduct review committee and the
  procedures referred to in paragraph (3)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committee report to directors

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} After each meeting of the conduct review committee of
  the bank, the committee shall report to the directors of the bank on
  matters reviewed by the committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors' report to Superintendent

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Within ninety days after the end of each financial
  year, the directors of a bank shall report to the Superintendent on
  what the conduct review committee did during the year in carrying out
  its responsibilities under subsection (3).

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 23\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 195
- 1997, c. 15, s. 23
- 2001, c. 9, s. 77
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committee

- **[[195.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-195.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The committee designated under
  paragraph 157(2)(e) shall consist of at least three directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Membership

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A majority of the members of the committee shall
  consist of directors who are not persons affiliated with the bank, and
  none of the members of the committee may be officers or employees of
  the bank or a subsidiary of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of committee

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The committee shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the bank to establish
    procedures for complying with the consumer provisions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review those procedures to determine whether they
    are appropriate to ensure that the bank is complying with the
    consumer provisions; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the bank to report at
    least annually to the committee on the implementation of the
    procedures and on any other activities that the bank carries out in
    relation to the protection of its customers.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bank's report to Commissioner

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A bank shall report to the Commissioner on the
  mandate and responsibilities of the committee and the procedures
  referred to in paragraph (3)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committee's report to directors

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} After each meeting of the committee, the committee
  shall report to the directors of the bank on matters reviewed by the
  committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors' report to Commissioner

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Within 90 days after the end of each financial year,
  the directors of a bank shall report to the Commissioner on what the
  committee did during the year in performing its duties under
  subsection (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 317](#1039540-1369014){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039540-1369014.html"}
:::

#### [Directors and Officers --- Authority]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12845 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief executive officer

- **[[196]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-196 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a bank shall appoint from their number a chief executive
  officer who must be ordinarily resident in Canada and, subject to
  section 198, may delegate to that officer any of the powers of the
  directors.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 24\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 196
- 1997, c. 15, s. 24
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of officers

- **[[197]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-197 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a bank may, subject to the by-laws, designate the offices
  of the bank, appoint officers thereto, specify the duties of those
  officers and delegate to them powers, subject to section 198, to
  manage the business and affairs of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors as officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 164, a director of a bank may be
  appointed to any office of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Two or more offices

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Two or more offices of a bank may be held by the same
  person.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limits on power to delegate

**[[198]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-198 .sectionLabel}** The directors of a bank
that is not a federal credit union may not delegate the power to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the shareholders a question or matter
  requiring the approval of the shareholders;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} fill a vacancy among the directors, on a committee of
  directors or in the office of auditor, or appoint additional
  directors;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} issue or cause to be issued securities, including an
  issue of shares of a series that is authorized in accordance with
  section 62, except in accordance with any authorization made by the
  directors;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} declare a dividend;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} authorize the redemption or other acquisition by the
  bank pursuant to section 71 of shares issued by the bank;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} authorize the payment of a commission on a share
  issue;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} approve a management proxy circular;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} except as provided in this Act, approve the annual
  statement of the bank and any other financial statements issued by the
  bank; or

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} adopt, amend or repeal by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 198
- 1997, c. 15, s. 25
- 2005, c. 54, s. 38
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1987
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-198-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 198"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limits on power to delegate

**[[198.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-198.1 .sectionLabel}** The directors of a
federal credit union may not delegate the power to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the members or shareholders a question or
  matter requiring their approval;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} admit members, except in accordance with any
  authorization made by the members;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} fill a vacancy among the directors, on a committee of
  directors or in the office of auditor;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} issue or cause to be issued securities, including an
  issue of shares of a series that is authorized in accordance with
  section 62, except in accordance with any authorization made by the
  directors;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} declare a dividend on membership shares or shares or
  allocate an amount as a patronage allocation;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} authorize the redemption or other acquisition by the
  federal credit union under section 71 of membership shares, or shares,
  issued by the federal credit union;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} authorize the payment of a commission on a share
  issue;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} approve a management proxy circular;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} except as provided in this Act, approve the annual
  statement of the federal credit union and any other financial
  statements it issued;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} expel members; or

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} adopt or amend by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1988
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration of directors, officers and
employees

- **[[199]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-199
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this section and the
  by-laws, the directors of a bank may fix the remuneration of the
  directors, officers and employees of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law required

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No remuneration shall be paid to a director as
  director until a by-law fixing the aggregate of all amounts that may
  be paid to all directors in respect of directors' remuneration during
  a fixed period of time has been confirmed by special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 199
- 1994, c. 26, s. 4
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

- **[[200]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-200 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  act of a director or an officer of a bank is valid notwithstanding a
  defect in the director's qualification or an irregularity in the
  director's election or in the appointment of the director or officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An act of the board of directors of a bank is valid
  notwithstanding a defect in the composition of the board or an
  irregularity in the election of the board or in the appointment of a
  member of the board.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to attend meetings

**[[201]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-201 .sectionLabel}** A director of a bank is
entitled to attend and to be heard at every meeting of shareholders or
members.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 201
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1989
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-201-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 201"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Conflicts of Interest]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12903 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure of interest

- **[[202]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-202 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director or officer of a bank shall disclose to the bank, in writing
  or by requesting to have it entered in the minutes of a meeting of
  directors or a meeting of a committee of directors, the nature and
  extent of any interest they have in a material contract or material
  transaction with the bank, whether entered into or proposed, if they

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are a party to the contract or transaction;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are a director or officer of a party to the
    contract or transaction or a person acting in a similar capacity; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} have a material interest in a party to the contract
    or transaction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- director

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure shall be made in the case of a
  director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the meeting of directors, or of a committee of
    directors, at which the proposed contract or transaction is first
    considered;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if at the time of the meeting referred to in
    paragraph (a) the director was not interested in the proposed
    contract or transaction, at the first one after they become
    interested in it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the director becomes interested after a contract
    or transaction is entered into, at the first one after they become
    interested; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a person who is interested in a contract or
    transaction becomes a director, at the first one after they become a
    director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure shall be made in the case of an
  officer who is not a director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately after they become aware that the
    contract, transaction, proposed contract or proposed transaction is
    to be considered or has been considered at a meeting of directors or
    of a committee of directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if they become interested after the contract or
    transaction is entered into, immediately after they become
    interested; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if a person who is interested in a contract or
    transaction becomes an officer, immediately after they become an
    officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- contract not
  requiring approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the material contract or material transaction,
  whether entered into or proposed, is one that in the ordinary course
  of the bank's business would not require approval by the directors,
  shareholders or members, as the case may be, the director or officer
  must disclose to the bank, in writing or by requesting to have it
  entered in the minutes of a meeting of directors or of a committee of
  directors, the nature and extent of their interest immediately after
  they become aware of the contract or transaction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 202
- 2005, c. 54, s. 39
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1990
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-202-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 202"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director to abstain

- **[[203]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-203 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who is required to make a disclosure under subsection 202(1)
  shall not be present at any meeting of directors, or of a committee of
  directors, while the contract or transaction is being considered or
  vote on any resolution to approve it unless the contract or
  transaction

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} relates primarily to their remuneration as a
    director, officer, employee or agent of the bank, an entity
    controlled by the bank or an entity in which the bank has a
    substantial investment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is for indemnity under section 212 or insurance
    under section 213; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is with an affiliate of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any director who knowingly contravenes subsection (1)
  ceases to hold office as director and is not eligible, for a period of
  five years after the date on which the contravention occurred, for
  election or appointment as a director of any financial institution
  that is incorporated or formed by or under an Act of Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An act of the board of directors of a bank, or of a
  committee of the board of directors, is not invalid because a person
  acting as a director had ceased under subsection (2) to hold office as
  a director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 203
- 1997, c. 15, s. 26
- 2005, c. 54, s. 40
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-203-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 203"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}General notice

- **[[204]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-204 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purposes of subsection 202(1), a general notice to the directors
  declaring that a director or officer is to be regarded as interested
  for any of the following reasons in a contract or transaction entered
  into with a party is a sufficient declaration of interest in relation
  to any contract or transaction with that party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer is a director or officer of
    a party referred to in paragraph 202(1)(b) or (c) or a person acting
    in a similar capacity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer has a material interest in
    the party; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} there has been a material change in the nature of
    the director's or officer's interest in the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to disclosures

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The shareholders and members of the bank may examine
  the portions of any minutes of meetings of directors or committees of
  directors that contain disclosures under subsection 202(1), or the
  portions of any other documents that contain those disclosures, during
  the usual business hours of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 204
- 2001, c. 9, s. 77.1(F)
- 2005, c. 54, s. 41
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1991
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-204-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 204"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Avoidance standards

- **[[205]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-205 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  contract or transaction for which disclosure is required under
  subsection 202(1) is not invalid and a director or officer is not
  accountable to the bank or its shareholders or members for any profit
  realized from it by reason only of the director's or officer's
  interest in the contract or transaction or the fact that the director
  was present or was counted to determine whether a quorum existed at
  the meeting of directors, or of a committee of directors, that
  considered it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer disclosed their interest in
    accordance with section 202 and subsection 204(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors approved the contract or transaction;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction was reasonable and fair
    to the bank at the time that it was approved.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Even if the conditions set out in subsection (1) are
  not met, a director or officer acting honestly and in good faith is
  not accountable to the bank or its shareholders or members for any
  profit realized from a contract or transaction for which disclosure
  was required and the contract or transaction is not invalid by reason
  only of the director's or officer's interest in it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction is approved or
    confirmed by special resolution at

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a bank that is not a federal
      credit union, a meeting of shareholders, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a federal credit union, at a
      meeting of its members and, if it has shareholders, at a meeting
      of its shareholders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} disclosure of the interest was made to the
    shareholders or, in the case of a federal credit union, to the
    members and shareholders, if any, in a manner sufficient to indicate
    its nature before the contract or transaction was approved or
    confirmed; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction was reasonable and fair
    to the bank at the time that it was approved or confirmed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 205
- 2005, c. 54, s. 41
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1992
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-205-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 205"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may set aside or require accounting

**[[206]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-206 .sectionLabel}** If a director or
officer of a bank fails to comply with any of sections 202 to 205, a
court, on application of the bank or any of its shareholders or members,
may set aside the contract or transaction on any terms that the court
thinks fit and may require the director or officer to account to the
bank for any profit or gain realized on it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 206
- 2005, c. 54, s. 41
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1992
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-206-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 206"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Liability, Exculpation and Indemnification]{.HTitleText3} {#h-12966 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director's liability

- **[[207]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-207
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Directors of a bank who vote for or
  consent to a resolution of the directors authorizing the issue of a
  share contrary to subsection 65(1), the issue of a membership share
  contrary to subsection 79.1(2) or the issue of subordinated
  indebtedness contrary to section 80 for a consideration other than
  money are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable to the bank to
  make good any amount by which the consideration received is less than
  the fair equivalent of the money that the bank would have received if
  the share, membership share or subordinated indebtedness had been
  issued for money on the date of the resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Further liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Directors of a bank who vote for or consent to a
  resolution of the directors authorizing any of the following are
  jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable to restore to the bank
  any amounts so distributed or paid and not otherwise recovered by the
  bank and any amounts in relation to any loss suffered by the bank:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a redemption or purchase of shares or membership
    shares contrary to section 71;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a reduction of capital contrary to section 75;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a payment of a dividend or patronage allocation
    contrary to section 79;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a payment of an indemnity contrary to section 212;
    or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any transaction contrary to Part XI.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 207
- 2005, c. 54, s. 42(E)
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1992
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-207-20060427.html "Link to previous version of section 207"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution

- **[[208]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-208 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who has satisfied a judgment in relation to the director's
  liability under section 207 is entitled to contribution from the other
  directors who voted for or consented to the unlawful act on which the
  judgment was founded.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director who is liable under section 207 is
  entitled to apply to a court for an order compelling a shareholder,
  member or other person to pay or deliver to the director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any money or property that was paid or distributed
    to the shareholder, member or other person contrary to section 71,
    75, 79 or 212; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an amount equal to the value of the loss suffered
    by the bank as a result of any transaction contrary to Part XI.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court order

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an application is made to a court under
  subsection (2), the court may, where it is satisfied that it is
  equitable to do so,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} order a shareholder, member or other person to pay
    or deliver to a director any money or property that was paid or
    distributed to the shareholder, member or other person contrary to
    section 71, 75, 79 or 212 or any amount referred to in paragraph
    (2)(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} order a bank to return or issue shares or
    membership shares to a person from whom the bank has purchased,
    redeemed or otherwise acquired shares or membership shares; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make any further order it thinks fit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 208
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1993
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-208-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 208"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

**[[209]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-209 .sectionLabel}** An action to enforce a
liability imposed by section 207 may not be commenced after two years
from the date of the resolution authorizing the action complained of.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors liable for wages

- **[[210]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-210
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  the directors of a bank are jointly and severally, or solidarily,
  liable to each employee of the bank for all debts not exceeding six
  months wages payable to the employee for services performed for the
  bank while they are directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions precedent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director is not liable under subsection (1) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the bank has been sued for the debt within six
    months after it has become due and execution has been returned
    unsatisfied in whole or in part;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the bank has commenced liquidation and dissolution
    proceedings or has been dissolved and a claim for the debt has been
    proven within six months after the earlier of the date of
    commencement of the liquidation and dissolution proceedings and the
    date of dissolution; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a winding-up order has been issued in respect of
    the bank under the [Winding-up and Restructuring
    Act](/eng/acts/W-11) and a claim for the debt has been allowed or
    proven within six months after the issue of the winding-up order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director is not liable under subsection (1) unless
  the director is sued for a debt referred to in that subsection while a
  director or within two years after the director has ceased to be a
  director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amount due after execution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where execution referred to in paragraph (2)(a) has
  issued, the amount recoverable from a director is the amount remaining
  unsatisfied after execution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subrogation of director

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a director of a bank pays a debt referred to in
  subsection (1) that is proven in liquidation and dissolution or
  winding-up proceedings, the director is entitled to any preference
  that the employee would have been entitled to and, where a judgment
  has been obtained, the director is entitled to an assignment of the
  judgment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution entitlement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A director of a bank who has satisfied a claim under
  this section is entitled to a contribution from the other directors of
  the bank who are liable for the claim.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 210
- 1996, c. 6, s. 167
- 2005, c. 54, s. 43(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-210-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 210"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Defence --- due diligence

- **[[211]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-211 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director, officer or employee of a bank is not liable under section
  207 or 210 or subsection 506(1) and has fulfilled their duty under
  subsection 158(2) if they exercised the care, diligence and skill that
  a reasonably prudent person would have exercised in comparable
  circumstances, including reliance in good faith on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the bank that were
    represented to them by an officer of the bank or in a written report
    of the auditor or auditors of the bank fairly to reflect the
    financial condition of the bank; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report of a person whose profession lends
    credibility to a statement made by them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Defence --- good faith

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director or officer of a bank has fulfilled their
  duty under subsection 158(1) if they relied in good faith on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the bank that were
    represented to them by an officer of the bank or in a written report
    of the auditor or auditors of the bank fairly to reflect the
    financial condition of the bank; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report of a person whose profession lends
    credibility to a statement made by them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 211
- 2001, c. 9, s. 78
- 2005, c. 54, s. 44
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-211-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 211"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Indemnification

- **[[212]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-212 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank may indemnify a director or officer of the bank, a former
  director or officer of the bank or another person who acts or acted,
  at the bank's request, as a director or officer of or in a similar
  capacity for another entity against all costs, charges and expenses,
  including an amount paid to settle an action or satisfy a judgment,
  reasonably incurred by them in respect of any civil, criminal,
  administrative, investigative or other proceeding in which they are
  involved because of that association with the bank or other entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advances

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank may advance amounts to the director, officer
  or other person for the costs, charges and expenses of a proceeding
  referred to in subsection (1). They shall repay the amounts if they do
  not fulfil the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No indemnification

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A bank may not indemnify a person under
  subsection (1) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person acted honestly and in good faith with a
    view to the best interests of, as the case may be, the bank or the
    other entity for which they acted at the bank's request as a
    director or officer or in a similar capacity; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a criminal or administrative action
    or proceeding that is enforced by a monetary penalty, the person had
    reasonable grounds for believing that their conduct was lawful.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Indemnification --- derivative actions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A bank may with the approval of a court indemnify a
  person referred to in subsection (1) or advance amounts to them under
  subsection (2) --- in respect of an action by or on behalf of the bank
  or other entity to procure a judgment in its favour to which the
  person is made a party because of the association referred to in
  subsection (1) with the bank or other entity --- against all costs,
  charges and expenses reasonably incurred by them in connection with
  that action if they fulfil the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to indemnity

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person referred to in that
  subsection is entitled to be indemnified by the bank in respect of all
  costs, charges and expenses reasonably incurred by them in connection
  with the defence of any civil, criminal, administrative, investigative
  or other proceeding to which the person is subject because of the
  association referred to in subsection (1) with the bank or other
  entity described in that subsection if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was not judged by the court or other competent
    authority to have committed any fault or omitted to do anything that
    they ought to have done; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fulfils the conditions set out in subsection (3).
