[Previous
Version](section-482-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 482"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

**[[483]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-483 .sectionLabel}** Nothing in this Part
requires

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the termination of a loan made before February 7,
  2001;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the termination of a loan made after that date as a
  result of a commitment made before that date;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the disposal of an investment made before that date;
  or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the disposal of an investment made after that date as
  a result of a commitment made before that date.

But if the loan or investment would be precluded or limited by this
Part, the amount of the loan or investment may not, except as provided
in subsections 471(2), 472(3) and 473(3), be increased after that date.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 483
- 2001, c. 9, s. 127
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Saving

**[[484]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-484 .sectionLabel}** A loan or investment
referred to in section 483 is deemed not to be prohibited by the
provisions of this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 484
- 2001, c. 9, s. 127
:::

## [PART X]{.HLabel1}[Capital, Liquidity and Capacity to Absorb Losses]{.HTitleText1} {#h-16857 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Domestic systemically important bank

- **[[484.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-484.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order,
  designate a bank as a domestic systemically important bank unless the
  Minister advises the Superintendent that the Minister is of the
  opinion that it is not in the public interest to do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order, revoke the
  designation unless the Minister advises the Superintendent that the
  Minister is of the opinion that it is not in the public interest to do
  so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Factors

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In making the designation or revoking it, the
  Superintendent shall take into account all factors that he or she
  considers relevant, including whether the distress or failure of the
  bank could have a significant adverse impact on the financial system
  in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice and publication

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a designation is made or revoked, the
  Superintendent shall, as soon as feasible, cause a notice of the
  designation or revocation, as the case may be, to be published in the
  [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and on the website of the
  Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2016, c. 7, s. 159
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adequacy of capital and liquidity

- **[[485]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-485 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall, in relation to its operations, maintain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} adequate capital, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} adequate and appropriate forms of liquidity,

  and shall comply with any regulations in relation thereto.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Domestic systemically important banks

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If the bank is a domestic systemically important
  bank, it shall also maintain the minimum capacity to absorb losses
  that is provided for under subsection (1.2) and shall comply with any
  regulations in relation to that requirement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent's order

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} For each domestic systemically important bank, the
  Superintendent shall, by order made after consulting with the other
  members of the committee established under subsection 18(1) of the
  [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
  Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), provide for the amount that constitutes the
  bank's minimum capacity to absorb losses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amount --- subsection (1.2)

  [(1.21)]{.lawlabel} The amount set under subsection (1.2) consists of
  capital, prescribed shares and prescribed liabilities, which have the
  value determined in accordance with any criteria the Superintendent
  considers appropriate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public interest

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1.2), if, before the order is
  made, the Minister advises the Superintendent that the Minister is of
  the opinion that the amount provided for by the Superintendent is not
  in the public interest, the Superintendent shall provide for another
  amount in accordance with that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice and publication

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} If an order is made under subsection (1.2), the
  Superintendent shall, in writing and without delay, inform the bank
  that is subject to the order and shall, as soon as feasible, cause the
  order to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and on the website of the Office
  of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations and guidelines

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations and the
  Superintendent may make guidelines respecting the maintenance by banks
  of adequate capital and adequate and appropriate forms of liquidity
  and the maintenance by domestic systemically important banks of the
  minimum capacity to absorb losses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directives

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding that a bank is complying with
  regulations or guidelines made under subsection (2), the
  Superintendent may, by order, direct the bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to increase its capital; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to provide additional liquidity in such forms and
    amounts as the Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Orders to limit or prohibit

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent becomes aware that a domestic
  systemically important bank is not maintaining its minimum capacity to
  absorb losses, the Superintendent shall notify the other members of
  the committee established under subsection 18(1) of the [Office of the
  Superintendent of Financial Institutions Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7) and
  may, by order, take any measures that he or she considers appropriate,
  including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} limiting the growth of the bank's total assets;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} limiting or prohibiting acquisitions of assets by
    the bank;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} limiting or prohibiting discretionary payments in
    respect of the bank's shares or subordinated indebtedness;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} limiting or prohibiting purchases by the bank, or
    redemptions, of the bank's shares, subordinated indebtedness or
    prescribed liabilities;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} limiting or prohibiting reductions of the bank's
    stated capital; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} limiting or prohibiting the opening of new branches
    by the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consultation

  [(3.2)]{.lawlabel} Before making an order under subsection (3.1) or
  varying or revoking such an order, the Superintendent shall consult
  with the other members of the committee established under subsection
  18(1) of the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
  Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A bank shall comply with an order made under
  subsection (3) or (3.1) within the time that is specified in the
  order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of value

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where an appraisal of any asset held by a bank or any
  of its subsidiaries has been made by the Superintendent and the value
  determined by the Superintendent to be the appropriate value of the
  asset varies materially from the value placed by the bank or
  subsidiary on the asset, the Superintendent shall send to the bank,
  the auditor or auditors of the bank and the audit committee of the
  bank a written notice of the appropriate value of the asset as
  determined by the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 485
- 1996, c. 6, s. 7
- 2016, c. 7, s. 160
- 2017, c. 20, s. 111
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-485-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 485"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prescribed conditions

**[[485.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-485.01 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations respecting the conditions that domestic
systemically important banks must meet in issuing, originating or
amending prescribed shares or liabilities.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2016, c. 7, s. 161
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations and guidelines --- disclosure
of information

**[[485.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-485.02 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations and the Superintendent may make guidelines
respecting the disclosure by domestic systemically important banks of
information in relation to their capacity to absorb losses.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2016, c. 7, s. 162
:::

## [PART XI]{.HLabel1}[Self-dealing]{.HTitleText1} {#h-16915 .Part}

### [Interpretation and Application]{.HTitleText2} {#h-16916 .Subheading}

Definition of [[senior officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[485.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-485.1 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes of
this Part, a [[senior officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a body corporate
is a person who is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a director of the body corporate who is a full-time
  employee of the body corporate;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the chief executive officer, chief operating officer,
  president, secretary, treasurer, controller, chief financial officer,
  chief accountant, chief auditor or chief actuary of the body
  corporate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a natural person who performs functions for the body
  corporate similar to those performed by a person referred to in
  paragraph (b);

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the head of the strategic planning unit of the body
  corporate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the head of the unit of the body corporate that
  provides legal services or human resources services to the body
  corporate; or

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} any other officer reporting directly to the body
  corporate's board of directors, chief executive officer or chief
  operating officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 67
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Related party of bank

- **[[486]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-486 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purposes of this Part, a person is a related party of a bank where
  the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a person who has a significant interest in a
    class of shares or in membership shares of the bank;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a director or senior officer of the bank or of a
    body corporate that controls the bank or is acting in a similar
    capacity in respect of an unincorporated entity that controls the
    bank;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is the spouse or common-law partner, or a child who
    is less than eighteen years of age, of a person described in
    paragraph (a) or (b);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} is an entity that is controlled by a person
    referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (c);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} is an entity in which a person who controls the
    bank has a substantial investment;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} is an entity in which the spouse or common-law
    partner, or a child who is less than eighteen years of age, of a
    person who controls the bank has a substantial investment; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} is a person, or forms part of a class of persons,
    designated under subsection (3) or (4) as, or deemed under
    subsection (5) to be, a related party of the bank.

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 68\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- subsidiaries and
  substantial investments of banks

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an entity in which a bank has a substantial
  investment would, but for this subsection, be a related party of the
  bank only because a person who controls the bank controls the entity
  or has a substantial investment in the entity, and the person does not
  control the entity or have a substantial investment in the entity
  otherwise than through the person's controlling interest in the bank,
  the entity is not a related party of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designated related party

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the Superintendent
  may, with respect to a particular bank, designate as a related party
  of the bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any person or class of persons whose direct or
    indirect interest in or relationship with the bank or a related
    party of the bank might reasonably be expected to affect the
    exercise of the best judgment of the bank in respect of a
    transaction; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any person who is a party to any agreement,
    commitment or understanding referred to in section 9 if the bank
    referred to in that section is the particular bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a person is designated as a related party of a
  bank pursuant to subsection (3), the Superintendent may also designate
  any entity in which the person has a substantial investment and any
  entity controlled by such an entity to be a related party of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed related party

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where, in contemplation of a person becoming a
  related party of a bank, the bank enters into a transaction with the
  person, the person is deemed for the purposes of this Part to be a
  related party of the bank in respect of that transaction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Holders of exempted shares

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order, designate a class
  of non-voting shares of a bank for the purpose of this subsection. If
  a class of non-voting shares of a bank is so designated, a person is
  deemed, notwithstanding paragraph (1)(a), not to be a related party of
  the bank if the person would otherwise be a related party of the bank
  only because the person has a significant interest in that class.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of substantial investment

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of determining whether an entity or a
  person has a substantial investment for the purposes of paragraph
  (1)(e) or (f), the references to "control" and "controlled" in section
  10 shall be construed as references to "control, within the meaning of
  section 3, determined without regard to paragraph 3(1)(d)" and
  "controlled, within the meaning of section 3, determined without
  regard to paragraph 3(1)(d)", respectively.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of control

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d),
  [[controlled]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means "controlled, within the
  meaning of section 3, determined without regard to paragraph 3(1)(d)".

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 486
- 1997, c. 15, s. 68
- 2000, c. 12, s. 7
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2078
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-486-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 486"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application of Part

- **[[487]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-487 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This
  Part does not apply in respect of any transaction entered into prior
  to the coming into force of this Part but, after the coming into force
  of this Part, any modification of, addition to, or renewal or
  extension of a prior transaction is subject to this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} This Part does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the issue of shares of any class of shares, or of
    membership shares, of a bank when fully paid for in money or when
    issued

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with any provisions for the
      conversion of other issued and outstanding membership shares or
      securities of the bank into shares of that class of shares, or
      into membership shares,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} as a share or membership share dividend,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in exchange for shares, or membership shares,
      however designated, of a body corporate that has been continued as
      a bank under Part III,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the terms of an amalgamation
      or conversion under Part VI,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} by way of consideration in accordance with the
      terms of a sale agreement under Part VI, or

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} with the approval in writing of the
      Superintendent, in exchange for shares of another body corporate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the payment of dividends or patronage allocations
    by a bank;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} transactions that consist of the payment or
    provision by a bank to persons who are related parties of the bank
    of salaries, fees, stock options, pension benefits, incentive
    benefits or other benefits or remuneration in their capacity as
    directors, officers or employees of the bank;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} transactions approved by the Minister under
    subsection 678(1) of this Act or subsection 715(1) of the [Insurance
    Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8); or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if a bank is controlled by a widely held bank
    holding company or a widely held insurance holding company,
    transactions approved by the Superintendent that are entered as part
    of, or in the course of, a restructuring of the holding company or
    of any entity controlled by it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in paragraph (2)(c) exempts from the
  application of this Part the payment by a bank of fees or other
  remuneration to a person for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the provision of services referred to in paragraph
    495(1)(a); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} duties outside the ordinary course of business of
    the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception for holding body corporate

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A holding body corporate of a bank is not a related
  party of the bank if the holding body corporate is a Canadian
  financial institution that is referred to in any of paragraphs (a)
  to (d) of the definition [[financial institution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  in section 2.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Substantial investment --- related
  party exception

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a holding body corporate of a bank is, because
  of subsection (4), not a related party of the bank, any entity in
  which the holding body corporate has a substantial investment is not a
  related party of the bank if no related party of the bank has a
  substantial investment in the entity otherwise than through the
  control of the holding body corporate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 487, c. 48, s. 494
- 1997, c. 15, s. 69
- 2001, c. 9, s. 128
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2079
- 2012, c. 5, s. 223
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-487-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 487"){.PITLink}
:::

Meaning of [[transaction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[488]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-488 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purposes of this Part, entering into a transaction with a related
  party of a bank includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} making a guarantee on behalf of the related party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} making an investment in any securities of the
    related party;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} taking an assignment of or otherwise acquiring a
    loan made by a third party to the related party; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} taking a security interest in the securities of the
    related party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interpretation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the fulfilment of an
  obligation under the terms of any transaction, including the payment
  of interest on a loan or deposit, is part of the transaction, and not
  a separate transaction.

- Meaning of [[loan]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part,
  [[loan]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes a deposit, a financial lease, a
  conditional sales contract, a repurchase agreement and any other
  similar arrangement for obtaining funds or credit, but does not
  include investments in securities or the making of an acceptance,
  endorsement or other guarantee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Security of a related party

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part,
  [[security]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a related party includes an
  option, transferable by delivery, to demand delivery of a specified
  number or amount of shares of the related party at a fixed price
  within a specified time.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 488
- 2007, c. 6, s. 44
:::

[Previous
Version](section-488-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 488"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Prohibited Related Party Transactions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-16997 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibited transactions

- **[[489]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-489
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in this Part, a
  bank shall not, directly or indirectly, enter into any transaction
  with a related party of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transaction of entity

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), a
  bank is deemed to have indirectly entered into a transaction in
  respect of which this Part applies where the transaction is entered
  into by an entity that is controlled by the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply where an entity that is
  controlled by a bank is a financial institution incorporated or formed
  under the laws of a province and is subject to regulation and
  supervision, satisfactory to the Minister, regarding transactions with
  related parties of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of
  transactions entered into by an entity that is controlled by a bank if
  the transaction is a prescribed transaction or is one of a class of
  prescribed transactions.

### [Permitted Related Party Transactions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-17007 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nominal value transactions

**[[490]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-490 .sectionLabel}** Notwithstanding
anything in this Part, a bank may enter into a transaction with a
related party of the bank if the value of the transaction is nominal or
immaterial to the bank when measured by criteria that have been
established by the conduct review committee of the bank and approved in
writing by the Superintendent.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Secured loans

**[[491]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-491 .sectionLabel}** A bank may make a loan
to or a guarantee on behalf of a related party of the bank or take an
assignment of or otherwise acquire a loan to a related party of the bank
if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the loan or guarantee is fully secured by securities
  of or guaranteed by the Government of Canada or the government of a
  province; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the loan is a loan permitted by section 418 made to a
  related party who is a natural person on the security of a mortgage of
  the principal residence of that related party.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deposits

**[[492]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-492 .sectionLabel}** A bank may enter into a
transaction with a related party of the bank if the transaction consists
of a deposit by the bank with a financial institution that is a direct
clearer or a member of a clearing group under the by-laws of the
Canadian Payments Association and the deposit is made for clearing
purposes.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Borrowing, etc., from related party

**[[493]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-493 .sectionLabel}** A bank may borrow money
from, take deposits from, or issue debt obligations to, a related party
of the bank.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Acquisition of assets

- **[[494]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-494 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank may purchase or otherwise acquire from a related party of the
  bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} securities of, or securities guaranteed by, the
    Government of Canada or the government of a province;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} assets fully secured by securities of, or
    securities guaranteed by, the Government of Canada or the government
    of a province; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} goods for use in the ordinary course of business.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sale of assets

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 482, a bank may sell any assets of
  the bank to a related party of the bank if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the consideration for the assets is fully paid in
    money; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there is an active market for those assets.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Asset transactions with financial
  institutions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any of the provisions of
  subsections (1) and (2), a bank may, in the normal course of business
  and pursuant to arrangements that have been approved by the
  Superintendent in writing, acquire or dispose of any assets, other
  than real property, from or to a related party of the bank that is a
  financial institution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Asset transactions in restructuring

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any of the provisions of
  subsections (1) and (2), a bank may acquire any assets from, or
  dispose of any assets to, a related party of the bank as part of, or
  in the course of, a restructuring, if the acquisition or disposition
  has been approved in writing by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Goods or space for use in business

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A bank may lease assets

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from a related party of the bank for use in the
    ordinary course of business of the bank, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to a related party of the bank

  if the lease payments are made in money.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval under section 236

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A bank may acquire any assets from, or dispose of any
  assets to, a related party of the bank under a sale agreement that is
  approved by the Minister under section 236.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 494
- 2007, c. 6, s. 45
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-494-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 494"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Services

- **[[495]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-495 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank may enter into a transaction with a related party of the bank if
  the transaction

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (2), consists of a written
    contract for the purchase by the bank of services used in the
    ordinary course of business;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (4), involves the provision
    of services normally offered to the public by the bank in the
    ordinary course of business;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} consists of a written contract with a financial
    institution or an entity in which the bank is permitted to have a
    substantial investment pursuant to section 468 that is a related
    party of the bank

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the networking of any services provided by
      the bank or the financial institution or entity, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the referral of any person by the bank to
      the financial institution or entity, or for the referral of any
      person by the financial institution or entity to the bank;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} consists of a written contract for such pension or
    benefit plans or their management or administration as are
    incidental to directorships or to the employment of officers or
    employees of the bank or its subsidiaries; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} involves the provision by the bank of management,
    advisory, accounting, information processing or other services in
    relation to any business of the related party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order concerning management by
  employees

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a bank has entered into a contract pursuant to
  paragraph (1)(a) and the contract, when taken together with all other
  such contracts entered into by the bank, results in all or
  substantially all of the management functions of the bank being
  exercised by persons who are not employees of the bank, the
  Superintendent may, by order, if the Superintendent considers that
  result to be inappropriate, require the bank, within such time as may
  be specified in the order, to take all steps necessary to ensure that
  management functions that are integral to the carrying on of business
  by the bank are exercised by employees of the bank to the extent
  specified in the order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection 489(2), a bank is deemed not to
  have indirectly entered into a transaction in respect of which this
  Part applies if the transaction is entered into by an entity that is
  controlled by the bank and the business of which is limited to the
  activity referred to in paragraph 468(2)(c) and the transaction is on
  terms and conditions at least as favourable to the bank as market
  terms and conditions, as defined in subsection 501(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Services

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The provision of services, for the purposes of
  paragraph (1)(b), does not include the making of loans or guarantees.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 495
- 1997, c. 15, s. 70
- 2007, c. 6, s. 46
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-495-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 495"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transactions with holding companies

- **[[495.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-495.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2) and
  sections 495.2 and 495.3, if a widely held bank holding company or a
  widely held insurance holding company has a significant interest in
  any class of shares of a bank, the bank may enter into any transaction
  with the holding company or with any other related party of the bank
  that is an entity in which the holding company has a substantial
  investment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policies and procedures

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The bank shall adhere to policies and procedures
  established under subsection 195(3) when entering into the
  transaction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 129
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

- **[[495.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-495.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a bank enters into a transaction
  with a related party of the bank with whom the bank may enter into
  transactions under subsection 495.1(1) and that is not a federal
  financial institution, the bank shall not directly or indirectly make,
  take an assignment of or otherwise acquire a loan to the related
  party, make an acceptance, endorsement or other guarantee on behalf of
  the related party or make an investment in the securities of the
  related party if, immediately following the transaction, the aggregate
  financial exposure, as that expression is defined by the regulations,
  of the bank would exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of all transactions of the bank with the
    related party, the prescribed percentage of the bank's regulatory
    capital or, if no percentage is prescribed, five per cent of the
    bank's regulatory capital; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in respect of all transactions of the bank with
    such related parties of the bank, the prescribed percentage of the
    bank's regulatory capital or, if no percentage is prescribed, ten
    per cent of the bank's regulatory capital.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that it is
  necessary for the protection of the interests of the depositors and
  creditors of a bank, the Superintendent may, by order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} reduce the limit in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) that
    would otherwise apply to the bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} impose limits on transactions by the bank with
    related parties with whom the bank may enter into transactions under
    subsection 495.1(1) that are federal financial institutions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order, increase the limit
  in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) that would otherwise apply to a bank on
  transactions by the bank with related parties that are financial
  institutions that are regulated in a manner acceptable to the
  Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 129
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assets transactions

- **[[495.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-495.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection 494(3), a bank
  shall not, without the approval of the Superintendent and its conduct
  review committee, directly or indirectly acquire assets from a related
  party of the bank with whom the bank may enter into transactions under
  subsection 495.1(1) that is not a federal financial institution, or
  directly or indirectly transfer assets to such a related party if

  ::: {#17082 .Subsection}
  A + B \> C

  where

  [A]{.dfn}
  :   is the value of the assets;

  [B]{.dfn}
  :   is the total value of all assets that the bank directly or
      indirectly acquired from, or directly or indirectly transferred
      to, that related party in the 12 months ending immediately before
      the acquisition or transfer, other than assets acquired by or
      transferred to the bank under transactions permitted by section
      490; and

  [C]{.dfn}
  :   is five per cent, or the percentage that may be prescribed, of the
      total value of the assets of the bank, as shown in the last annual
      statement of the bank prepared before the acquisition or transfer.
  :::

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The prohibition in subsection (1) does not apply in
  respect of assets purchased or otherwise acquired under subsection
  494(1), assets sold under subsection 494(2) or any other assets as may
  be prescribed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The approval of the Superintendent is not required if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the bank purchases or sells assets under a sale
    agreement that is approved by the Minister under section 236; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the bank or its subsidiary acquires shares of, or
    ownership interests in, an entity for which the approval of the
    Minister under Part VII or subsection 468(5) is required or the
    approval of the Superintendent under subsection 468(6) is required.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Value of assets

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of "A" in subsection (1), the value
  of the assets is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of assets that are acquired, the
    purchase price of the assets or, if the assets are shares of, or
    ownership interests in, an entity the assets of which will be
    included in the annual statement of the bank after the acquisition,
    the fair market value of the assets; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of assets that are transferred, the
    book value of the assets as stated in the last annual statement of
    the bank prepared before the transfer or, if the assets are shares
    of, or ownership interests in, an entity the assets of which were
    included in the last annual statement of the bank before the
    transfer, the value of the assets as stated in the annual statement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Total value of all assets

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the total value
  of all assets that the bank or any of its subsidiaries has acquired
  during the period of twelve months referred to in subsection (1) is
  the purchase price of the assets or, if the assets are shares of, or
  ownership interests in, an entity the assets of which immediately
  after the acquisition were included in the annual statement of the
  bank, the fair market value of the assets of the entity at the date of
  the acquisition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Total value of all assets

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the total value
  of all assets that the bank or any of its subsidiaries has transferred
  during the period of twelve months referred to in subsection (1) is
  the book value of the assets as stated in the last annual statement of
  the bank prepared before the transfer or, if the assets are shares of,
  or ownership interests in, an entity the assets of which were included
  in the last annual statement of the bank before the transfer, the
  value of the assets of the entity as stated in the annual statement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 129
- 2007, c. 6, s. 47
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-495.3-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 495.3"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors and officers and their
interests

- **[[496]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-496
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2) and
  sections 497 and 498, a bank may enter into any transaction with a
  related party of the bank if the related party is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a natural person who is a related party of the bank
    only because the person is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a director or a senior officer of the bank or of
      an entity that controls the bank, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the spouse or common-law partner, or a child who
      is less than eighteen years of age, of a director or senior
      officer of the bank or of an entity that controls the bank; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an entity that is a related party of the bank only
    because the entity is controlled by

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a director or senior officer of the bank or of an
      entity that controls the bank, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the spouse or common-law partner, or a child who
      is less than eighteen years of age, of a director or senior
      officer referred to in subparagraph (i).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loans to full-time officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank may, with respect to a related party of the
  bank referred to in subsection (1) who is a full-time senior officer
  of the bank, make, take an assignment of or otherwise acquire a loan
  to the related party only if the aggregate principal amount of all
  outstanding loans to the related party that are held by the bank and
  its subsidiaries, together with the principal amount of the proposed
  loan, does not exceed the greater of twice the annual salary of the
  related party and \$100,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} loans referred to in paragraph 491(b), and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} margin loans referred to in section 498,

  and the amount of any such loans to a related party of a bank shall
  not be included in determining, for the purposes of subsection (2),
  the aggregate principal amount of all outstanding loans made by the
  bank to the related party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preferred terms --- loan to officer

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding section 501, a bank may make a loan,
  other than a margin loan, to a senior officer of the bank on terms and
  conditions more favourable to the officer than those offered to the
  public by the bank if those terms and conditions have been approved by
  the conduct review committee of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preferred terms --- loan to spouse or
  common-law partner

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding section 501, a bank may make a loan
  referred to in paragraph 491(b) to the spouse or common-law partner of
  a senior officer of the bank on terms and conditions more favourable
  than those offered to the public by the bank if those terms and
  conditions have been approved by the conduct review committee of the
  bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preferred terms --- other financial
  services

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding section 501, a bank may offer
  financial services, other than loans or guarantees, to a senior
  officer of the bank, or to the spouse or common-law partner, or a
  child who is less than eighteen years of age, of a senior officer of
  the bank, on terms and conditions more favourable than those offered
  to the public by the bank if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the financial services are offered by the bank to
    employees of the bank on those favourable terms and conditions; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the conduct review committee of the bank has
    approved the practice of making those financial services available
    on those favourable terms and conditions to senior officers of the
    bank or to the spouses or common-law partners, or the children under
    eighteen years of age, of senior officers of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 496
- 1997, c. 15, s. 71
- 2000, c. 12, ss. 5, 7
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Board approval required

- **[[497]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-497
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except with the concurrence of at
  least two thirds of the directors present at a meeting of the board of
  directors of the bank, a bank shall not, with respect to a related
  party of the bank referred to in subsection 496(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} make, take an assignment of or otherwise acquire a
    loan to the related party, including a margin loan referred to in
    section 498,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a guarantee on behalf of the related party, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make an investment in the securities of the related
    party

  if, immediately following the transaction, the aggregate of

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the principal amount of all outstanding loans to
    the related party that are held by the bank and its subsidiaries,
    other than

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} loans referred to in paragraph 491(b), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the related party is a full-time senior
      officer of the bank, loans to the related party that are permitted
      by subsection 496(2),

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the sum of all outstanding amounts guaranteed by
    the bank and its subsidiaries on behalf of the related party, and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} where the related party is an entity, the book
    value of all investments by the bank and its subsidiaries in the
    securities of the entity

  would exceed 2 per cent of the regulatory capital of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on transactions with directors,
  officers and their interests

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank shall not, with respect to a related party of
  the bank referred to in subsection 496(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} make, take an assignment of or otherwise acquire a
    loan to the related party, including a margin loan referred to in
    section 498,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a guarantee on behalf of the related party, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make an investment in the securities of the related
    party

  if, immediately following the transaction, the aggregate of

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the principal amount of all outstanding loans to
    all related parties of the bank referred to in subsection 496(1)
    that are held by the bank and its subsidiaries, other than

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} loans referred to in section 491, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} loans permitted by subsection 496(2),

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the sum of all outstanding amounts guaranteed by
    the bank and its subsidiaries on behalf of all related parties of
    the bank referred to in subsection 496(1), and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the book value of all investments by the bank and
    its subsidiaries in the securities of all entities that are related
    parties of the bank referred to in subsection 496(1)

  would exceed 50 per cent of the regulatory capital of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion of *de minimus* transactions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Loans, guarantees and investments that are referred
  to in section 490 shall not be included in calculating the aggregate
  of loans, guarantees and investments referred to in subsections (1)
  and (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 497
- 1997, c. 15, s. 72
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Margin loans

**[[498]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-498 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may
establish terms and conditions with respect to the making by a bank of
margin loans to a director or senior officer of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 498
- 1997, c. 15, s. 73
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by order

- **[[499]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-499 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank may enter into a transaction with a related party of the bank if
  the Superintendent, by order, has exempted the transaction from the
  provisions of section 489.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions for order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall not make an order referred
  to in subsection (1) unless the Superintendent is satisfied that the
  decision of the bank to enter into the transaction has not been and is
  not likely to be influenced in any significant way by a related party
  of the bank and does not involve in any significant way the interests
  of a related party of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 499
- 1996, c. 6, s. 8
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prescribed transactions

**[[500]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-500 .sectionLabel}** A bank may enter into a
transaction with a related party of the bank if the transaction is a
prescribed transaction or one of a class of prescribed transactions.

### [Restrictions on Permitted Transactions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-17171 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Market terms and conditions

- **[[501]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-501
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsections
  496(4) to (6), any transaction entered into with a related party of
  the bank shall be on terms and conditions that are at least as
  favourable to the bank as market terms and conditions.

- Meaning of [[market terms and conditions]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), [[market terms
  and conditions]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a service or a loan facility or a
    deposit facility offered to the public by the bank in the ordinary
    course of business, terms and conditions that are no more or less
    favourable than those offered to the public by the bank in the
    ordinary course of business; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in respect of any other transaction,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} terms and conditions, including those relating to
      price, rent or interest rate, that might reasonably be expected to
      apply in a similar transaction in an open market under conditions
      requisite to a fair transaction between parties who are at arm's
      length and who are acting prudently, knowledgeably and willingly,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the transaction is one that would not
      reasonably be expected to occur in an open market between parties
      who are at arm's length, terms and conditions, including those
      relating to price, rent or interest rate, that would reasonably be
      expected to provide the bank with fair value, having regard to all
      the circumstances of the transaction, and that would be consistent
      with the parties to the transaction acting prudently,
      knowledgeably and willingly.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 501
- 2001, c. 9, s. 130
:::

**[[502 and 503]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-502_and_503
.sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 74\]]{.Repealed}

### [Disclosure]{.HTitleText2} {#h-17184 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bank obligation

- **[[504]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-504
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where, in respect of any proposed
  transaction permitted by this Part, other than those referred to in
  section 490, a bank has reason to believe that the other party to the
  transaction is a related party of the bank, the bank shall take all
  reasonable steps to obtain from the other party full disclosure, in
  writing, of any interest or relationship, direct or indirect, that
  would make the other party a related party of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reliance on information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank and any person who is a director or an
  officer, employee or agent of the bank may rely on any information
  contained in any disclosure received by the bank pursuant to
  subsection (1) or any information otherwise acquired in respect of any
  matter that might be the subject of such a disclosure and no action
  lies against the bank or any such person for anything done or omitted
  in good faith in reliance on any such information.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

**[[505]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-505 .sectionLabel}** Where a bank has
entered into a transaction that the bank is prohibited by this Part from
entering into or where a bank has entered into a transaction for which
approval is required under subsection 497(1) without having obtained the
approval, the bank shall, on becoming aware of that fact, notify the
Superintendent without delay.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 505
- 1997, c. 15, s. 75
:::

### [Remedial Actions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-17194 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order to void contract or to grant other
remedy

- **[[506]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-506 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  bank enters into a transaction that it is prohibited from entering
  into by this Part, the bank or the Superintendent may apply to a court
  for an order setting aside the transaction or for any other
  appropriate remedy, including an order directing that the related
  party of the bank involved in the transaction account to the bank for
  any profit or gain realized or that any director or senior officer of
  the bank who authorized the transaction compensate the bank for any
  loss or damage incurred by the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time limit

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (1) in respect of a
  particular transaction may only be made within the period of three
  months following the day the notice referred to in section 505 in
  respect of the transaction is given to the Superintendent or, if no
  such notice is given, the day the Superintendent becomes aware of the
  transaction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (2), a document
  purporting to have been issued by the Superintendent, certifying the
  day on which the Superintendent became aware of the transaction,
  shall, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, be received in
  evidence as conclusive proof of that fact without proof of the
  signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have
  signed the document and without further proof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 46, s. 506
- 2001, c. 9, s. 131
:::

## [PART XII]{.HLabel1}[Foreign Banks]{.HTitleText1} {#h-17204 .Part}

### [DIVISION 1]{.HLabel2}[Interpretation and Application]{.HTitleText2} {#h-17205 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[507]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  following definitions apply in this Part.

  [[business growth fund]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[business growth fund]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means Canadian
      Business Growth Fund (GP) Inc., a corporation incorporated under
      the [Canada Business Corporations Act](/eng/acts/C-44). ([fonds de
      croissance des entreprises]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[designated foreign bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[designated foreign bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      2007, c. 6, s. 48\]]{.Repealed}

  [[designation order]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[designation order]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2007, c.
      6, s. 48\]]{.Repealed}

  [[exemption order]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[exemption order]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s.
      48\]]{.Repealed}

  [[finance entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[finance entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a Canadian entity
      that is a finance entity as defined in the regulations. ([entité
      s'occupant de financement]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[financial leasing entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[financial leasing entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a Canadian
      entity that is a financial leasing entity as defined in subsection
      464(1). ([entité s'occupant de crédit-bail]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[financial services entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[financial services entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an entity,
      other than an entity referred to in any of paragraphs 468(1)(a)
      to (i) or a leasing entity, that engages in activities at least
      the prescribed portion --- or if no portion is prescribed, 10 per
      cent --- of which, determined in the prescribed manner, consists
      of one or more of the following activities:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} providing any financial service;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} acting as a financial agent;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} providing investment counselling and portfolio
        management services;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} issuing payment, credit or charge cards and, in
        cooperation with others, including other financial institutions,
        operating a payment, credit or charge card plan;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} engaging in the activities referred to in the
        definition [[closed-end fund]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, [[mutual
        fund distribution entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} or [[mutual
        fund entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection 464(1);

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} engaging in prescribed activities, under
        prescribed terms and conditions, if any are prescribed;

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} engaging in any activity referred to in
        paragraphs (a) to (f) as an agent for another entity referred to
        in any of those paragraphs or in any of paragraphs 468(1)(a) to
        (j); or

      - [(h)]{.lawlabel} acquiring or holding control of, or becoming a
        major owner of, an entity referred to in any of paragraphs (a)
        to (g) or any of paragraphs 468(1)(a) to (j). ([entité
        s'occupant de services financiers]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[foreign cooperative credit society]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[foreign cooperative credit society]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
      an entity that is incorporated or formed, and regulated, otherwise
      than by or under an Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a
      province, and that, outside Canada, engages in or carries on the
      business of a cooperative credit society. ([société coopérative de
      crédit étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[foreign insurance company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[foreign insurance company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a foreign
      company as defined in subsection 2(1) of the [Insurance Companies
      Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8). ([société d'assurances
      étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[foreign securities dealer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[foreign securities dealer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an entity
      that is incorporated or formed, and regulated, otherwise than by
      or under an Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province,
      and that, outside Canada, engages in or carries on the business of
      dealing in securities. ([courtier de valeurs mobilières
      étranger]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[leasing activities]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[leasing activities]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the financial leasing of personal property and
        the related activities that a financial leasing entity may
        engage in; and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all other leasing of personal
        property. ([activités de location]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[leasing entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[leasing entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an entity that
      engages in only

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} leasing activities; or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} leasing activities and activities other than
        those described in paragraphs (a) to (h) of the definition
        [[financial services entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}. ([entité
        s'occupant de location]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[limited commercial entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[limited commercial entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a Canadian
      entity that a foreign bank or an entity associated with a foreign
      bank may control in accordance with subsection 522.09(1) or (2),
      or in which a foreign bank or an entity associated with a foreign
      bank is permitted to acquire a substantial investment in
      accordance with that subsection. ([entité à activités commerciales
      restreintes]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[non-bank affiliate of a foreign bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[non-bank affiliate of a foreign bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
      a Canadian entity, other than a bank,

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in which a foreign bank or an entity associated
        with a foreign bank holds a substantial investment, or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is controlled by a foreign bank or an
        entity associated with a foreign bank,

      but a Canadian entity is not a non-bank affiliate of a foreign
      bank by reason only that a bank that is a subsidiary of the
      foreign bank or of the entity associated with a foreign bank
      controls, or holds a substantial investment in, the Canadian
      entity. ([établissement affilié à une banque
      étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[permitted Canadian entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[permitted Canadian entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a Canadian
      entity that a foreign bank or an entity associated with a foreign
      bank may control in accordance with section 522.08, or in which a
      foreign bank or an entity associated with a foreign bank is
      permitted to acquire a substantial investment in accordance with
      that section. ([entité canadienne admissible]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[representative office]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[representative office]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an office
      established to represent a foreign bank in Canada that is not
      subject to the direction of, or management by, an entity
      incorporated or formed by or under an Act of Parliament or of the
      legislature of a province, and the personnel of which are employed
      directly or indirectly by the foreign bank. ([bureau de
      représentation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[specialized financing entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[specialized financing entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
      Canadian entity that is a specialized financing entity as defined
      in the regulations. ([entité s'occupant de financement
      spécial]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entity associated with foreign bank

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an entity is associated with a foreign bank if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the entity controls, or is controlled by, the
      foreign bank, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the entity and the foreign bank are controlled
      by the same person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an entity may be associated with more than one
    foreign bank; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a foreign bank may be associated with another
    foreign bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entity deemed to be associated with a
  foreign bank

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the Minister may deem
  an entity to be associated with a foreign bank if, in the opinion of
  the Minister, it is reasonable to conclude that under any agreement,
  commitment or understanding, whether formal or informal, verbal or
  written,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the foreign bank is acting, jointly or in concert,
    in relation to the shares or ownership interests of the entity, with
    one or more other persons such that, if they were one person, they
    would control the entity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entity is acting, jointly or in concert, in
    relation to the shares or ownership interests of the foreign bank,
    with one or more other persons such that, if they were one person,
    they would control the foreign bank;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} another entity that is associated with the foreign
    bank is acting, jointly or in concert, in relation to the shares or
    ownership interests of the entity, with one or more other persons
    such that, if they were one person, they would control the entity;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who controls the entity is acting, jointly
    or in concert, in relation to the shares or ownership interests of
    the foreign bank, with one or more other persons, such that, if they
    were one person, they would control the foreign bank;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a person who controls the foreign bank is acting,
    jointly or in concert, in relation to the shares or ownership
    interests of the entity, with one or more other persons, such that,
    if they were one person, they would control the entity; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} two or more persons are acting, jointly or in
    concert, in relation to the shares or ownership interests of the
    entity and the foreign bank such that, if they were one person, they
    would control the entity and the foreign bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed substantial investment by
  foreign bank

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, a foreign bank is
  deemed to hold a substantial investment in a Canadian entity if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the foreign bank and one or more entities
    associated with the foreign bank, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two or more entities associated with the foreign
    bank

  would, if they were one person, hold a substantial investment in the
  Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed substantial investment by entity
  associated

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, an entity associated
  with a foreign bank is deemed to hold a substantial investment in a
  Canadian entity if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the entity and the foreign bank, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entity and one or more other entities
    associated with the foreign bank

  would, if they were one person, hold a substantial investment in the
  Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed control by foreign bank

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, a foreign bank is
  deemed to control a Canadian entity if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the foreign bank and one or more entities
    associated with the foreign bank, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two or more entities associated with the foreign
    bank

  would, if they were one person, control the Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed control by entity associated

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, an entity associated
  with a foreign bank is deemed to control a Canadian entity if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the entity and the foreign bank, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entity and one or more other entities
    associated with the foreign bank

  would, if they were one person, control the Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person is a major owner

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, a person, other than a
  foreign bank or an entity associated with a foreign bank,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a major owner of an unincorporated Canadian
    entity if the aggregate of any ownership interests, however
    designated, into which the unincorporated Canadian entity is divided
    that are beneficially owned by the person and that are beneficially
    owned by any entities controlled by the person is more than 35 per
    cent of all of the ownership interests into which the unincorporated
    Canadian entity is divided; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a major owner of a Canadian entity that is a
    body corporate if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate of the shares of any class of
      voting shares of the Canadian entity that are beneficially owned
      by the person and that are beneficially owned by any entities
      controlled by the person is more than 20 per cent of the
      outstanding shares of that class of voting shares of the Canadian
      entity, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate of the shares of any class of
      non-voting shares of the Canadian entity that are beneficially
      owned by the person and that are beneficially owned by any
      entities controlled by the person is more than 30 per cent of the
      outstanding shares of that class of non-voting shares of the
      Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Foreign bank a major owner

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, a foreign bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a major owner of an unincorporated Canadian
    entity if the aggregate of any ownership interests, however
    designated, into which the unincorporated Canadian entity is divided
    that are beneficially owned by the foreign bank and that are
    beneficially owned by any entities associated with the foreign bank
    is more than 35 per cent of all of the ownership interests into
    which the unincorporated Canadian entity is divided; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a major owner of a Canadian entity that is a
    body corporate if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate of the shares of any class of
      voting shares of the Canadian entity that are beneficially owned
      by the foreign bank and that are beneficially owned by any
      entities associated with the foreign bank is more than 20 per cent
      of the outstanding shares of that class of voting shares of the
      Canadian entity, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate of the shares of any class of
      non-voting shares of the Canadian entity that are beneficially
      owned by the foreign bank and that are beneficially owned by any
      entities associated with the foreign bank is more than 30 per cent
      of the outstanding shares of that class of non-voting shares of
      the Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Associated entity a major owner

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, an entity associated
  with a foreign bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a major owner of an unincorporated Canadian
    entity if the aggregate of any ownership interests, however
    designated, into which the unincorporated Canadian entity is divided
    that are beneficially owned by the entity associated with the
    foreign bank, that are beneficially owned by the foreign bank and
    that are beneficially owned by any other entities associated with
    the foreign bank is more than 35 per cent of all of the ownership
    interests into which the unincorporated Canadian entity is divided;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a major owner of a Canadian entity that is a
    body corporate if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate of the shares of any class of
      voting shares of the Canadian entity that are beneficially owned
      by the entity associated with the foreign bank, that are
      beneficially owned by the foreign bank and that are beneficially
      owned by any other entities associated with the foreign bank is
      more than 20 per cent of the outstanding shares of that class of
      voting shares of the Canadian entity, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate of the shares of any class of
      non-voting shares of the Canadian entity that are beneficially
      owned by the entity associated with the foreign bank, that are
      beneficially owned by the foreign bank and that are beneficially
      owned by any other entities associated with the foreign bank is
      more than 30 per cent of the outstanding shares of that class of
      non-voting shares of the Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed major owner --- person

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the Minister may deem
  a person to be a major owner of a Canadian entity if, in the opinion
  of the Minister, it is reasonable to conclude that under any
  agreement, commitment or understanding, whether formal or informal,
  verbal or written, the person is acting, jointly or in concert, in
  relation to the shares or ownership interests of the Canadian entity,
  with one or more other persons such that, if they were one person,
  they would be a major owner of the Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed major owner --- foreign bank

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the Minister may deem
  a foreign bank to be a major owner of a Canadian entity if, in the
  opinion of the Minister, it is reasonable to conclude that under any
  agreement, commitment or understanding, whether formal or informal,
  verbal or written,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the foreign bank is acting, jointly or in concert,
    in relation to the shares or ownership interests of the Canadian
    entity, with one or more other persons such that, if they were one
    person, they would be a major owner of the Canadian entity; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two or more persons are acting, jointly or in
    concert in relation to the shares or ownership interests of the
    Canadian entity and in relation to the shares or ownership interests
    of the foreign bank such that, if they were one person, they would
    control the foreign bank and be a major owner of the Canadian
    entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed major owner --- entity
  associated with a foreign bank

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the Minister may deem
  an entity associated with a foreign bank to be a major owner of a
  Canadian entity if, in the opinion of the Minister, it is reasonable
  to conclude that under any agreement, commitment or understanding,
  whether formal or informal, verbal or written, the entity associated
  with the foreign bank is acting, jointly or in concert, in relation to
  the shares and ownership interests of the Canadian entity with one or
  more other persons, such that, if they were one person, they would be
  a major owner of the Canadian entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Member of foreign bank's group

  [(14)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, a member of a foreign
  bank's group is any of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an entity associated with the foreign bank;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an entity in which the foreign bank or an entity
    associated with the foreign bank holds a substantial investment; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a prescribed entity, in relation to the foreign
    bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Foreign bank that has a financial
  establishment in Canada

  [(15)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, a foreign bank has,
  or is deemed to have, a financial establishment in Canada if the
  foreign bank or any entity associated with the foreign bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is an authorized foreign bank;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a foreign insurance company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has received the approval of the Minister under
    paragraph 522.22(1)(f); or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} controls, or is a major owner of,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian entity referred to in any of
      paragraphs 468(1)(a) to (i), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian entity that is a financial services
      entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Associated entity that has a financial
  establishment in Canada

  [(16)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, an entity associated
  with a foreign bank has, or is deemed to have, a financial
  establishment in Canada if the entity, the foreign bank or any other
  entity associated with the foreign bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is an authorized foreign bank;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a foreign insurance company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has received the approval of the Minister under
    paragraph 522.22(1)(f); or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} controls, or is a major owner of,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian entity referred to in any of
      paragraphs 468(1)(a) to (i), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian entity that is a financial services
      entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations concerning exemption from
  associated status

  [(17)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the exemption, from the application of
    any provision of this Act, of any class or classes of entities
    associated with a foreign bank from the status of being associated
    with a foreign bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} authorizing the Minister, by order, and subject to
    any terms and conditions that the Minister considers appropriate, to
    deem, for the purposes of any provision of this Act, any entity not
    to be an entity associated with a foreign bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation or variation of order

  [(18)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, by further order, revoke or vary
  any order referred to in paragraph (17)(b) and any such revocation or
  variation comes into effect three months after the date the further
  order is made unless the Minister and the entity to which the order
  relates agree that the revocation or variation is to take effect at
  some other time agreed to by them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

  [(19)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister makes an order referred to in
  paragraph (17)(b) or subsection (18), the Minister shall publish in
  the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a notice of the making
  of the order.

::: HistoricalNote

- 2007, c. 6, s. 48
