### [DIVISION 2]{.HLabel2}[Fair and Equitable Dealings]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1369154 .Subheading}

#### [Responsible Business Conduct]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1369155 .Subheading}

##### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1369156 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Training

**[[627.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.02 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall ensure that its officers and employees in Canada, and any person
who offers or sells the institution's products or services in Canada,
are trained with respect to the policies and procedures that it has
established for complying with the consumer provisions.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369160){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369160.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}False or misleading information

**[[627.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.03 .sectionLabel}** No institution
shall communicate or otherwise provide false or misleading information
to a customer, the public or the Commissioner.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369164){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369164.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibited conduct

**[[627.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.04 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall not, in its dealings in Canada with its customers and the public,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} impose undue pressure on a person, or coerce a
  person, for any purpose, including to obtain a product or service from
  a particular person --- including the institution and any of its
  affiliates --- as a condition for obtaining another product or service
  from the institution;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} take advantage of a person; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} engage in any prescribed conduct.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369171){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369171.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}For greater certainty

- **[[627.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, an
  institution may offer a product or service to a person on more
  favourable terms or conditions than it would otherwise offer, if the
  more favourable terms and conditions are offered on the condition that
  the person obtain another product or service from any particular
  person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}For greater certainty

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, an affiliate of an institution
  may offer a product or service to a person on more favourable terms or
  conditions than the affiliate would otherwise offer, if the more
  favourable terms and conditions are offered on the condition that the
  person obtain another product or service from the institution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval by institution

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a product or service is obtained by a borrower
  from a particular person as security for a loan from an institution,
  the institution may require that the product or service meet with its
  approval. That approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369180){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369180.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policies and procedures --- appropriate
products or services

**[[627.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.06 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall establish and implement policies and procedures to ensure that the
products or services in Canada that it offers or sells to a natural
person other than for business purposes are appropriate for the person
having regard to their circumstances, including their financial needs.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369184){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369184.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration, payment or benefit

**[[627.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.07 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall ensure that the remuneration of its officers and employees in
Canada --- and of any person who offers or sells its products or
services in Canada --- as well as any payment or benefit that the
institution offers to them, does not interfere with the person's ability
to comply with the policies and procedures referred to in section
627.06.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369188){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369188.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No provision without express consent and
agreement

- **[[627.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to any regulations, an
  institution shall not provide a person with a product or service in
  Canada without first

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} obtaining the person's express consent to do so;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} entering into an agreement with the person for it
    to be provided; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} providing the person with a copy of the agreement,
    if the agreement is for a product or service to be provided on an
    ongoing basis.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Oral consent --- written confirmation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the consent is given orally, the institution shall
  provide the person with written confirmation of that consent without
  delay.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use not consent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Use by the person of the product or service does not
  constitute express consent for the purpose of subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369200){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369200.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obtaining express consent

**[[627.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.09 .sectionLabel}** Any communication
from an institution seeking a person's express consent shall be made in
a manner, and using language, that is clear, simple and not misleading.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369204){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369204.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cancellation periods --- products or
services

- **[[627.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (1.1), if an
  institution enters into an agreement with a person in respect of a
  product or service in Canada --- other than a prescribed product or
  service or a product or service referred to in section 627.11 --- to
  be provided on an ongoing basis, the institution shall allow the
  person to cancel the agreement,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if it was entered into by mail or orally by
    telephone, within the prescribed period or, if there is no
    prescribed period, until the end of the 14th business day after the
    day on which the agreement is entered into; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if it was entered into in any other manner, within
    the prescribed period or, if there is no prescribed period, until
    the end of the third business day after the day on which the
    agreement is entered into.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to a body corporate,
  trust or partnership if it is a business that is not an eligible
  enterprise.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligations of institution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person notifies an institution that they are
  cancelling an agreement within the applicable period referred to in
  subsection (1), the institution shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in writing and without delay, acknowledge receipt
    of the person's notice of cancellation and confirm what it intends
    to recover under subsection (3); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} without delay, refund to the person any amount that
    it received in respect of the provision of the product or service.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limited recovery

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the event of a cancellation within the applicable
  period referred to in subsection (1), an institution shall waive any
  cancellation charge and may recover only

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any amounts related to the person's use of the
    product or service prior to the cancellation;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any expense that the institution has reasonably
    incurred in providing the product or service; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed amount.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369222){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369222.html"}
- [2021, c. 23, s. 151](#1307106-1369223){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1307106-1369223.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cancellation --- certain products or
services

- **[[627.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If an institution enters into an
  agreement with a person in respect of a retail deposit account,
  deposit-type instrument, credit card account or any prescribed product
  or service in Canada, the institution shall allow the person to cancel
  the agreement in accordance with any prescribed requirements.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation of institution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the person cancels the agreement, the institution
  shall meet any prescribed requirements.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369230){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369230.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Imposition of charges or penalties

- **[[627.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not impose on a
  person a charge or penalty in relation to a product or service in
  Canada unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the institution has obtained from the person the
    express consent referred to in paragraph 627.08(1)(a);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the agreement in respect of the product or service
    provides for its imposition; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the institution discloses the charge or penalty in
    accordance with this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not preclude the institution from
  receiving an amount in relation to a product or service that is
  determined under an order of a court.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369240){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369240.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alert

- **[[627.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall, without delay,
  send to a natural person an alert, by electronic means,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the balance of the person's personal deposit
    account that is opened in Canada falls below any amount that the
    person communicates to the institution or, if the person does not
    communicate an amount, below the prescribed amount or, if there is
    no prescribed amount, \$100; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the amount of credit available on the person's
    line of credit that is extended --- or credit card account that is
    opened --- in Canada other than for business purposes falls below
    any amount that the person communicates to the institution or, if
    the person does not communicate an amount, below the prescribed
    amount or, if there is no prescribed amount, \$100.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has opted
  out, in writing, of receiving the alert or does not provide the
  contact information required to receive the alert.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Content

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The alert shall indicate that the balance of the
  personal deposit account, or the amount of credit available on the
  line of credit or credit card account, has fallen below the amount
  communicated to the institution, below the prescribed amount or below
  \$100, as the case may be, and that, in accordance with the agreement
  in respect of the product or service, charges or penalties may be
  imposed for the most recent transaction, or for any subsequent
  transaction, made on the account or line of credit. The alert shall
  also indicate what the person may do to avoid charges or penalties and
  the time within which it is to be done, and include any prescribed
  information.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369251){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369251.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advertisements

**[[627.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.14 .sectionLabel}** Any advertisement
in Canada that is made by an institution shall be accurate, clear and
not misleading.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369255){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369255.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Arrangements with affiliates, etc.

**[[627.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.15 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall not enter into any arrangement or otherwise cooperate with any of
its representatives, agents or other intermediaries, with any of its
affiliates that are controlled by a bank or a bank holding company and
that are a [[finance entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in
subsection 464(1) or other prescribed entity, or with any of the
representatives, agents or other intermediaries of such an affiliate, to
sell or further the sale of a product or service of the institution or
the affiliate unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the affiliate or the representative, agent or other
  intermediary of the institution or the affiliate, as the case may be,
  complies, with respect to the product or service, with the consumer
  provisions that apply to institutions, as if it were an institution,
  to the extent that those provisions are applicable to its activities;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the persons who request or receive the product or
  service have access to the institution's procedures established for
  dealing with complaints under paragraph 627.43(1)(a) as if the product
  or service had been requested or received from the institution;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the employees of the affiliate or the representative,
  agent or other intermediary of the institution or the affiliate, as
  the case may be,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} may report particulars under subsection 979.2(1) to
    the affiliate or the representative, agent or other intermediary of
    the institution or the affiliate as if they were an employee of a
    bank, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} have access to the procedures established under
    section 979.3; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the affiliate or the representative, agent or other
  intermediary of the institution or the affiliate, as the case may be,
  complies with section 979.4 as if it were a bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369265){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369265.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Intermediary for another entity

**[[627.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.16 .sectionLabel}** If an institution
is acting in the capacity of a representative, agent or other
intermediary for another entity in respect of a product or service
provided by the entity, the institution shall ensure that an agreement
in respect of that product or service complies with the prescribed
requirements.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369269){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369269.html"}
:::

##### [Access to Basic Banking Services]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1369270 .Subheading}

###### [Retail Deposit Accounts]{.HTitleText5} {#h-1369271 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opening

- **[[627.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a member
  bank shall, at any point of service or any branch in Canada at which
  it opens retail deposit accounts through natural persons, open a
  retail deposit account on the request, made there in person, of a
  natural person who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} presents to the member bank

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} two documents from a reliable source --- one of
      which indicates the person's name and address and the other the
      person's name and date of birth --- including

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} identification issued by the Government of
        Canada or the government of a province,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} recent notices of tax assessments issued by the
        Government of Canada or the government of a province or
        municipality,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} recent statements of benefits from the
        Government of Canada or the government of a province,

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} recent Canadian public utility bills,

      - [(E)]{.lawlabel} recent bank account or credit card statements,

      - [(F)]{.lawlabel} foreign passports, and

      - [(G)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed document, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any document from a reliable source that
      indicates the person's name and date of birth, if the person's
      identity is also confirmed by a customer in good standing with the
      member bank or by a natural person of good standing in the
      community where the point of service or branch is located;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank so requests, consents to the
    member bank's verifying whether any of the circumstances set out in
    paragraphs 627.18(1)(a) to (d) applies to the person, and to the
    member bank's verifying the documents presented by the person;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank --- based on its verification of
    the circumstances set out in paragraphs 627.18(1)(a) to (d) or of
    the documents presented by the person or based on any information
    provided by the person in connection with the request --- has
    reasonable grounds to suspect that the person is misrepresenting
    their identity, presents to the member bank one piece of
    identification issued by the Government of Canada or the government
    of a province that bears the person's photograph and signature;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank is a federal credit union and so
    requests, becomes a member of the bank; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} meets any prescribed condition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opening at another location

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a natural person who meets the conditions set out
  in subsection (1) requests the opening of a retail deposit account at
  a point of service at which the opening of such an account can only be
  initiated, the member bank is not required to open the account at that
  point of service; however, the bank shall open the account at another
  physical location.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Request made in other manner

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A member bank shall open a retail deposit account for
  any natural person who requests it in any prescribed manner and who
  meets any prescribed condition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No minimum deposit or balance required

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A member bank shall not require the natural person to
  make an initial minimum deposit or maintain a minimum balance.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369296){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369296.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

- **[[627.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 627.17(1) to (3) do not
  apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank has reasonable grounds to
    believe that the retail deposit account will be used for illegal or
    fraudulent purposes;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the natural person has a history of illegal or
    fraudulent activity in relation to providers of financial services
    and the most recent instance of such an activity occurred less than
    seven years before the day on which the request to open a retail
    deposit account is made;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank has reasonable grounds to
    believe that the natural person, for the purpose of opening the
    retail deposit account, knowingly made a material misrepresentation
    in the information provided to the member bank;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank has reasonable grounds to
    believe that it is necessary to refuse to open the retail deposit
    account in order to protect the customers or employees of the member
    bank from physical harm, harassment or other abuse;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if the request is made at a branch or point of
    service of a member bank at which the only retail deposit accounts
    offered are those that are linked to an account at another financial
    institution; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in any prescribed circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bankruptcy

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty and for the purpose of
  paragraph (1)(a), the fact that the natural person is or has been a
  bankrupt does not, by itself without any evidence of fraud or any
  other illegal activity in relation to the bankruptcy, constitute
  reasonable grounds for a member bank to believe that an account for
  the person will be used for illegal or fraudulent purposes.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369309){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369309.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refusal to open

**[[627.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.19 .sectionLabel}** A member bank
that refuses to open a retail deposit account for a natural person shall
provide the person with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written statement that indicates that it will not
  be opening the account; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs 627.65(a)
  to (c).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369315){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369315.html"}
:::

###### [Funds]{.HTitleText5} {#h-1369316 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

**[[627.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.2 .sectionLabel}** Sections 627.21 and
627.22 apply only with respect to paper-based cheques or other
paper-based instruments deposited in Canada that are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} encoded with magnetic ink to allow for character
  recognition;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} not damaged or mutilated to the extent that they are
  unreadable by cheque-clearing systems;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} drawn on an institution's branch in Canada; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} issued in Canadian dollars.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369324){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369324.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Availability

**[[627.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.21 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall make available for withdrawal any funds deposited by cheque or
other instrument into a retail deposit account or into a deposit account
held by an eligible enterprise

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a cheque or other instrument in an
  amount that is not greater than the prescribed amount,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the deposit is made in person with an employee
    at one of the institution's branches or points of service, within
    the prescribed period or, if there is no prescribed period, no later
    than four business days after the day of the deposit, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the deposit is made in any other manner, within
    the prescribed period or, if there is no prescribed period, no later
    than five business days after the day of the deposit; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a cheque or other instrument in an
  amount that is greater than the prescribed amount,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the deposit is made in person with an employee
    at one of the institution's branches or points of service, within
    the prescribed period or, if there is no prescribed period, no later
    than seven business days after the day of the deposit, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the deposit is made in any other manner, within
    the prescribed period or, if there is no prescribed period, no later
    than eight business days after the day of the deposit.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369334){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369334.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}First amount available

**[[627.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.22 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall make the prescribed amount of funds deposited or, if there is no
prescribed amount, the first \$100 of all funds deposited by a cheque or
other instrument into a retail deposit account available for withdrawal

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately, if the deposit is made in person with an
  employee at one of the institution's branches or points of service; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} on the business day following the day of the deposit,
  if the deposit is made in any other manner.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369340){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369340.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

**[[627.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.23 .sectionLabel}** Section 627.21
does not apply in respect of a deposit that is made by an eligible
enterprise if the institution has reasonable grounds to believe that
there is a material increased credit risk, having regard to the
following factors, among others:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an escalating overdraft balance that is not being
  reduced by deposits received;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a negative change in the credit score or other
  behaviour scores that may impact the enterprise's credit risk;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an unexplained change in the history of cheques or
  other instruments deposited into the account;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a high number of cheques or other instruments
  deposited that are returned as dishonoured items from other
  institutions, which may impact the available balance in the account;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} notice of bankruptcy or of creditor action against
  the enterprise; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed factor.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369350){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369350.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

- **[[627.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 627.21 and 627.22 do not
  apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the institution has reasonable grounds to
    believe that the deposit is being made for illegal or fraudulent
    purposes in relation to the depositor's account;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the account has been open for fewer than 90
    days;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the cheque or other instrument has been endorsed
    more than once;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the cheque or other instrument is deposited at
    least six months after the date of the cheque or other instrument;
    or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in any prescribed circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refusal to make funds available

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An institution that relies on subsection (1) as
  grounds for not complying with section 627.21 or 627.22 shall ---
  immediately, if the deposit is made in person with an employee at one
  of the institution's branches or points of service or on request of
  the depositor if the deposit is made in any other manner --- provide
  the depositor with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written statement that indicates that it will not
    be making the funds available; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs 627.65(a)
    to (c).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369364){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369364.html"}
:::

###### [Cashing Government Cheques or Other Instruments]{.HTitleText5} {#h-1369365 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cashing

- **[[627.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A member bank shall, at any branch
  in Canada at which it, through natural persons, opens retail deposit
  accounts and disburses cash to customers, cash a cheque or other
  instrument on the request of a natural person made there in person if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cheque or other instrument is drawn on the
    Receiver General or on the Receiver General's account in the Bank of
    Canada or in any bank or other deposit-taking Canadian financial
    institution incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament, or is any
    other instrument issued as authority for the payment of money out of
    the Consolidated Revenue Fund;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person presents to the member bank

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the documents referred to in subparagraph
      627.17(1)(a)(i),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one piece of identification that is issued by
      the Government of Canada or the government of a province and that
      bears the person's signature and photograph, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any document from a reliable source that
      indicates the person's name and date of birth, if the person's
      identity is also confirmed by a customer in good standing with the
      member bank or by a natural person of good standing in the
      community where the branch is located;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amount of the cheque or other instrument is not
    greater than the prescribed amount; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed condition is met.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if there is evidence that the cheque or other
    instrument has been altered in any way or is counterfeit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the member bank has reasonable grounds to
    believe that there has been illegal or fraudulent activity in
    relation to the cheque or other instrument; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in any prescribed circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refusal to cash

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A member bank that refuses to cash for a natural
  person a cheque or other instrument that meets the conditions set out
  in paragraphs (1)(a), (c) and (d) shall provide the person with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written statement that indicates that it will not
    be cashing the cheque or other instrument; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs 627.65(a)
    to (c).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369386){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369386.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No charges

- **[[627.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not impose a
  charge

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for cashing a cheque or other instrument drawn on
    the Receiver General or on the Receiver General's account in the
    Bank of Canada, in any bank or other deposit-taking Canadian
    financial institution incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament
    or in any authorized foreign bank that is not subject to the
    restrictions and requirements referred to in subsection 524(2), in
    respect of its business in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for cashing any other instrument issued as
    authority for the payment of money out of the Consolidated Revenue
    Fund; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in respect of any cheque or other instrument that
    is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} drawn in favour of the Receiver General, the
      Government of Canada or any department of it or any public officer
      acting in the capacity of a public officer, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} tendered for deposit to the credit of the
      Receiver General.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deposits of Government of Canada

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) precludes any arrangement
  between the Government of Canada and an institution concerning

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} compensation for services performed by the
    institution for the Government of Canada; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} interest to be paid on any or all deposits of the
    Government of Canada with the institution.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369400){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369400.html"}
:::

###### [Documents]{.HTitleText5} {#h-1369401 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}General

- **[[627.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, any documents
  required to be presented by a natural person under any of sections
  627.17 to 627.26 and subsection (2) shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} original, valid and not substantially defaced; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a piece of identification issued by
    the government of a province, usable for identification purposes
    under the law of the province.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Different names

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If any document presented by a natural person bears a
  former name of the person, the person shall present a certificate
  evidencing the change of name that has occurred or a certified copy of
  that certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369410){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369410.html"}
:::

##### [Credit]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1369411 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prepayment

- **[[627.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.28
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not make a loan
  to a natural person that is repayable in Canada, the terms of which
  prohibit prepayment of the money advanced or any instalment on the
  money advanced before its due date.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a loan
  that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is secured by a mortgage on real property; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is made for business purposes and has a principal
    amount of more than the prescribed amount or, if there is no
    prescribed amount, \$100,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prepayment of certain loans

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an institution enters into a credit agreement with
  a natural person other than for business purposes, the institution
  shall allow the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a loan for a fixed amount, other
    than a loan that is secured by a mortgage on real property,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to prepay the outstanding balance under the
      agreement, at any time, without incurring any charge or penalty
      for making the prepayment, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} to prepay a part of the outstanding balance

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} on the date of any scheduled payment, if
        payments are scheduled once a month or more often, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} at any time but only once a month, in any other
        case; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any prescribed credit agreement, to
    prepay any prescribed amount at any prescribed time if the person
    meets any prescribed requirements.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refund or credit

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a person makes a prepayment referred to in
  paragraph (3)(a) or (b), the institution shall refund or credit to the
  person the prescribed amount of any prescribed charge other than any
  interest or discount applicable to the loan.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369430){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369430.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No minimum credit balance without express
consent

**[[627.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.29 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall not make a loan or advance in Canada to a natural person subject
to the condition that the person maintain a minimum credit balance with
the institution without first obtaining the person's express consent to
do so.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369434){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369434.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Default charges

**[[627.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.3 .sectionLabel}** If a natural person
fails to make a payment when it becomes due under a credit agreement
that the person entered into other than for business purposes or fails
to comply with any other obligation in the agreement an institution may
impose, in addition to interest, other charges for the sole purpose of
recovering the costs reasonably incurred

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} for legal services retained to collect or attempt to
  collect the payment;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in realizing on any security interest taken under the
  credit agreement or in protecting such a security interest, including
  the cost of legal services retained for that purpose;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in processing a cheque or other instrument that the
  person used to make a payment under the loan but that was dishonoured;
  or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} for any prescribed purpose.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369442){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369442.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Renewal of mortgages

**[[627.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.31 .sectionLabel}** If a natural
person enters into a credit agreement other than for business purposes
with an institution for a loan that is secured by a mortgage on real
property and that is to be renewed on a specified day,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the institution shall not, during any prescribed
  period, make a change to the agreement that increases the cost of
  borrowing; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person's rights under the agreement continue, and
  the renewal does not take effect, until the prescribed day.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369448){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369448.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No increase or provision without express
consent

- **[[627.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.32
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to any regulations, an
  institution shall not

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} increase the credit limit on a line of credit that
    is extended --- or a credit card account that is opened --- in
    Canada for a natural person other than for business purposes without
    first obtaining the person's express consent to do so; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide cheques that are issued on a credit card
    account that is opened in Canada for a natural person other than for
    business purposes without first obtaining the person's express
    consent to do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Oral consent --- written confirmation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the consent is given orally, the institution shall
  provide the person with written confirmation of the consent not later
  than the date of the first statement of account that is provided after
  the date of that consent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use not consent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Use by the person of the line of credit or the credit
  card account, or of any service related to the line of credit or
  credit card account, does not constitute express consent for the
  purpose of subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369459){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369459.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liability for unauthorized use

- **[[627.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.33
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The maximum liability of a borrower
  for the unauthorized use of a credit card issued to them in Canada,
  the account information of the credit card or the personal
  authentication information created or adopted in relation to the
  credit card or credit card account is \$50, unless the borrower has
  demonstrated gross negligence or, in Quebec, gross fault, in
  safeguarding the credit card, the account information or the personal
  authentication information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of unauthorized use

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a borrower reports to an institution that a credit
  card issued to them in Canada, the account information of the credit
  card or the personal authentication information created or adopted in
  relation to the credit card or credit card account has been lost or
  stolen or is otherwise at risk of being used in an unauthorized
  manner, the borrower shall not be liable for any unauthorized use of
  the credit card, the account information or the personal
  authentication information after the report is received.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Personal authentication information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The unauthorized use of a credit card issued to a
  borrower in Canada, or of account information of the credit card, by
  means of the personal authentication information created or adopted in
  relation to the credit card or credit card account does not by itself
  establish that the borrower demonstrated gross negligence or, in
  Quebec, gross fault, in safeguarding the personal authentication
  information.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369468){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369468.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Credit card statement

- **[[627.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to any regulations, an
  institution shall, for a credit card issued in Canada to a natural
  person other than for business purposes, send a statement of account
  in respect of each billing cycle to the person. The statement is to be
  sent without delay after the last day of the billing cycle.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum payment --- due date

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not require a minimum payment in
  respect of the outstanding balance owing for a particular billing
  cycle on the credit card account to be made by the person less than 21
  days after the last day of that billing cycle.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-business day

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the due date for a minimum payment in respect of
  the outstanding balance owing on the credit card account does not fall
  on a business day, the institution shall consider a payment made on
  the next business day as being made on time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No interest if balance paid in full

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not impose interest on purchases
  of goods or services made during a particular billing cycle on the
  credit card account if the person pays the outstanding balance owing
  on the credit card account in full on or before the due date.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369479){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369479.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Different interest rates --- allocation
of payment

- **[[627.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.35
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If different interest rates apply to
  different amounts owing for a particular billing cycle on a credit
  card account that is opened in Canada by a natural person other than
  for business purposes, the institution shall allocate any payment made
  by the person that is greater than the required minimum payment for
  that billing cycle among those amounts using one of the following
  methods:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by allocating that payment first to the amount with
    the highest interest rate and then allocating any remaining portion
    of the payment to the other amounts in descending order, based on
    their applicable interest rates; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by allocating that payment among those amounts in
    the same proportion as each amount bears to the outstanding balance
    owing on the credit card account.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rounding and adjustments

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of paragraph (1)(b), if the payment
  that the institution allocates to an amount owing on a credit card
  account contains a fraction of a dollar, the institution may round up
  that amount to the nearest dollar if the fraction of the dollar is
  equal to or greater than 50 cents, round down that amount to the
  nearest dollar if the fraction is less than 50 cents and, if
  necessary, make corresponding adjustments to the other amounts that
  are being allocated.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369488){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369488.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No charge --- holds

- **[[627.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.36
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not impose a
  charge on a natural person for exceeding their credit limit as a
  result of a hold on a credit card that was issued in Canada to the
  person other than for business purposes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if the person would, in
  any case, have exceeded their credit limit during the period in which
  the hold was in effect.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369495){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369495.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Debt recovery

**[[627.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.37 .sectionLabel}** In its dealings
with a natural person who owes it a debt under a credit agreement
entered into other than for business purposes, an institution

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall not communicate or attempt to communicate with
  the person, any member of the person's family or household, any
  relative, neighbour, friend or acquaintance of the person or the
  person's employer by any means that constitutes harassment, in a
  manner that constitutes harassment or with a frequency that
  constitutes harassment, including by

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} using threatening, profane, intimidating or
    coercive language,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} using undue pressure, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} making public, or threatening to make public, the
    person's failure to pay; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall comply with any other prescribed debt
  collection practices.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369504){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369504.html"}
:::

##### [Prepaid Payment Products]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1369505 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No expiry unless promotional product

**[[627.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.38 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall not impose an expiry date on the right of a person with whom it
entered into an agreement for the issuance of a prepaid payment product
to use the funds that are loaded on the product unless it is a
promotional product.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369509){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369509.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maintenance charges

**[[627.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.39 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall not impose any maintenance charges in respect of a prepaid payment
product for the period of 12 months after the day on which the product
is activated unless it is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a promotional product; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a reloadable product for which the institution has
  obtained the express consent of the person with whom it entered into
  an agreement for the issuance of the product to the imposition of the
  charge.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369515){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369515.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No overdraft charges without express
consent

- **[[627.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not impose any
  overdraft charges in respect of a prepaid payment product without
  first obtaining the express consent of the person with whom it entered
  into an agreement for the issuance of the product.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use not consent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Use by the person of the prepaid payment product does
  not constitute express consent for the purpose of subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369522){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369522.html"}
:::

##### [Optional Products or Services]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1369523 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Independent agreement

**[[627.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.41 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall not provide an optional product or service to a natural person ---
other than for business purposes --- in an agreement in respect of
another product or service.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369527){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369527.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Express consent --- temporary offer

- **[[627.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.42
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If an optional product or service,
  or a product or service that would have been an optional product or
  service if it had been provided for an additional charge, is provided
  to a natural person --- other than for business purposes --- under a
  promotional, preferential, introductory or special offer other than an
  offer referred to in subsection (2), an institution shall not impose
  any charges for the use of the product or service as of the day on
  which the person will no longer benefit from the offer without
  obtaining, within five business days before that day, the person's
  express consent to impose that charge.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Express consent --- number of uses

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an optional product or service, or a product or
  service that would have been an optional product or service if it had
  been provided for an additional charge, is provided to a natural
  person --- other than for business purposes --- under a promotional,
  preferential, introductory or special offer based on a specified
  number of uses, an institution shall not impose any charges after the
  last use of the product or service without obtaining, immediately
  after the last use, the person's express consent to impose that
  charge.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use not consent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Use by the person of the product or service does not
  constitute express consent for the purpose of subsections (1) and (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369536){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369536.html"}
:::

#### [Complaints Process]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1369537 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedures for dealing with complaints

- **[[627.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.43
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish procedures that are satisfactory to the
    Commissioner for dealing, within the prescribed period, with
    complaints;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} designate one of its officers or employees in
    Canada to be responsible for implementing those procedures; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} designate one or more of its officers or employees
    in Canada to receive and deal with those complaints.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Misleading terms

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall not use any misleading term with
  respect to its procedures or designated officers or employees,
  including any term that suggests that the procedures, officers or
  employees are independent of the institution --- such as the term
  "ombudsman" or any other term with a similar meaning --- or any
  prescribed term.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing with Commissioner

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall file a copy of its procedures as
  amended from time to time with the Commissioner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information regarding complaint
  procedure

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An institution shall provide a person who makes a
  complaint with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written acknowledgment of the date on which it
    received the complaint;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs 627.65(a)
    to (c); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any information that is necessary to enable them to
    meet the requirements of the procedures referred to in paragraph
    627.65(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369554){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369554.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record of complaint

**[[627.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.44 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall make, with respect to a complaint referred to in paragraph
627.43(1)(a), a record that is to be retained for a period of at least
seven years and that contains

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the complaint was made in writing, the original
  version of the complaint;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the complaint was made orally,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the recording or a transcript of the recording if
    the complaint was recorded, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the details of the complaint if the complaint was
    not recorded;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person who made the complaint;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person who requested or received from
  the institution the product or service to which the complaint relates;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the contact information provided by the person who
  made the complaint;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the institution received the
  complaint;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a description of the nature of the complaint and the
  product or service to which the complaint relates;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the complaint was resolved if, in
  the institution's opinion, it was resolved to the satisfaction of the
  person who made the complaint;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of any actions that were taken by the
  institution to attempt to resolve the complaint;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} a description of any compensation provided to the
  persons referred to in paragraph (c) or (d);

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} confirmation that the institution provided the
  information referred to in paragraphs 627.65(a) to (c) to the person
  who made the complaint, if the institution did so; and

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed information.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369572){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369572.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to Commissioner

**[[627.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.45 .sectionLabel}** The institution
shall ensure that the record retained under section 627.44 is accessible
to the Commissioner.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369576){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369576.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report to Commissioner

**[[627.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.46 .sectionLabel}** Within 60 days
after the end of each quarter, an institution shall submit to the
Commissioner in a form satisfactory to him or her, with respect to each
complaint received by an officer or employee referred to in paragraph
627.43(1)(c) during that quarter,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the record retained under section 627.44,
  except the contact information referred to in paragraph 627.44(e)
  other than the postal code; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed information.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369582){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369582.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Annual information

**[[627.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.47 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall, free of charge and within 135 days after the end of each
financial year, make available the following information for that year
on each of its websites through which it offers products or services in
Canada and provide the information in writing to any person who requests
it:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number and nature of any complaints that were
  dealt with by the officer or employee designated by the institution to
  deal with complaints who holds the most senior position identified for
  that purpose in the procedures established by the institution;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the average length of time taken to deal with the
  complaints received by that officer or employee;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number of complaints that, in the institution's
  opinion, were resolved by that officer or employee to the satisfaction
  of the persons who made them; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed information.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369590){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369590.html"}
:::

#### [External Complaints Body]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1415283 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purpose

**[[627.471]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.471 .sectionLabel}** The purpose of
sections 627.48 to 627.54 is to enhance the process for dealing with
complaints by establishing a regime comprised of a sole external
complaints body that discharges its functions and performs its
activities in a transparent, effective, timely and fair manner based on
the principles of accessibility, accountability, impartiality and
independence.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2023, c. 26, s. 129](#1409379-1415287){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409379-1415287.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation of body corporate

- **[[627.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.48
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, on the
  recommendation of the Commissioner, designate a body corporate
  incorporated under the [Canada Not-for-profit Corporations
  Act](/eng/acts/C-7.75) or under a provincial statute equivalent to
  that Act to be the external complaints body to deal with complaints
  referred to in paragraph 627.43(1)(a) that have not been resolved by
  its member institutions to the satisfaction of the persons who made
  the complaints or that have not been dealt with within the prescribed
  period referred to in that paragraph.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters for consideration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before designating a body corporate, the Minister
  shall take into account all matters that the Minister considers
  relevant, including whether the body corporate has

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the reputation required under paragraph 627.49(a);
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} policies and procedures and terms of reference that
    would enable it to discharge its functions and perform its
    activities in a manner that is consistent with the purpose set out
    in section 627.471 and to comply with paragraphs 627.49(b) to (m).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to be member

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every institution shall be a member of the external
  complaints body.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not an agent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The external complaints body is not an agent of His
  Majesty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation to be published

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A designation made under subsection (1) shall be
  published in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369607){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369607.html"}
- [2023, c. 26, s. 129](#1409379-1415301){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409379-1415301.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-627.48-20220630.html "Link to previous version of section 627.48"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirements

**[[627.49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.49 .sectionLabel}** The external
complaints body shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain a reputation for being operated in a manner
  that is consistent with the standards of good character and integrity;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} make its services available across Canada in both
  official languages and offer those services free of charge to persons
  who make complaints to it;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish policies, procedures and terms of reference
  that are satisfactory to the Commissioner pertaining to, among other
  things, dealing with complaints and the consultation, at least once a
  year, of its member institutions and consumers for the purpose of
  raising concerns about the external complaints body;

- [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} establish the manner of calculating, to the
  satisfaction of the Commissioner, the fees it charges to each of its
  member institutions for its services;

- [(c.2)]{.lawlabel} make information available to consumers about their
  rights and responsibilities in relation to the external complaints
  handling regime, respond to their inquiries and requests for
  information and offer them assistance in making a complaint;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} inform the Commissioner in writing within 30 days
  after the day on which it determines that a complaint raises a
  potential systemic issue;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} if it determines that all or part of a complaint is
  not within its terms of reference, provide the person who made the
  complaint with written reasons for that determination, and the name of
  any entity to whom the person may make a complaint, within 30 days
  after the day on which it receives the complaint;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} obtain confirmation from a member institution to
  which a complaint relates regarding whether the period referred to in
  paragraph 627.43(1)(a) has ended, unless the person who made the
  complaint has provided it with the written acknowledgment referred to
  in paragraph 627.43(4)(a);

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} impartially deal with complaints referred to in
  paragraph 627.43(1)(a) that have not been resolved by its member
  institutions to the satisfaction of the persons who made the
  complaints or that have not been dealt with within the prescribed
  period referred to in that paragraph;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} no later than 120 days after the day on which it has
  all of the information that it requires to deal with a complaint, make
  a final written recommendation to the parties;

- [(h.1)]{.lawlabel} without delay, inform the Commissioner in writing
  of cases in which an institution does not comply with a final
  recommendation;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} within 90 days after making a final recommendation,
  make a summary of the final recommendation available on its website
  free of charge, which summary is to include

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the nature of the complaint that
    is the subject of the final recommendation,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the name of the institution that received the
    complaint,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of any compensation provided to the
    persons referred to in paragraph 627.44(c) or (d),

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the reasons for the final recommendation, and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed information;

- [(i.1)]{.lawlabel} within 60 days after the end of each quarter,
  submit to the Commissioner, in a form satisfactory to the
  Commissioner,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in relation to all investigations completed during
    the quarter, a copy of the record of the complaint, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any prescribed information;

- [(i.2)]{.lawlabel} within 60 days after the end of each quarter, meet
  with the Commissioner to discuss, among other things, complaints,
  operations and market trends and issues with the potential to impact
  consumers;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} within 135 days after the end of each financial year,
  file a written report with the Commissioner on the performance of its
  functions and activities for that year, which report is to include

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} information about

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} its constitution, governance and terms of
      reference, and the identity of its member institutions,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} all sources of funding for its functions and
      activities, including the fees charged to each of its member
      institutions for its services and the manner in which those fees
      are calculated, and

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the results of the most recent evaluation
      referred to in paragraph (l),

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a summary of the results of any consultation with
    its member institutions and with persons who made complaints to it,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of each of its member institutions,
    the number and nature of complaints that it received, the number of
    complaints that it determined were within its terms of reference,
    the number of final recommendations that it made and the number of
    complaints that, in its opinion, were resolved to the satisfaction
    of the persons who made them,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the average length of time taken to deal with
    complaints,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the number of complaints that it determined were
    not within its terms of reference and the reasons for that
    determination,

  - [(v.1)]{.lawlabel} the number of complaints for which an institution
    did not comply with a final recommendation,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the number of final recommendations that it made
    in which compensation was recommended, and

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the average and total compensation provided with
    respect to complaints that it determined were within its terms of
    reference;

- [(j.1)]{.lawlabel} meet with the Commissioner annually;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} without delay after it is filed with the
  Commissioner, make the report available on its website free of charge
  and provide it to any person who requests it;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} submit, every five years, to an evaluation of the
  performance of its functions and activities that is conducted, at the
  discretion of the Commissioner, by the Commissioner or a third party
  in accordance with terms of reference that are established by the
  external complaints body in consultation with the Commissioner; and

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} meet any prescribed requirement.

::: HistoricalNote

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of information --- external
complaints body

**[[627.52]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627.52 .sectionLabel}** An institution
shall provide the external complaints body with all information in its
possession or control that relates to a complaint in respect of the
institution without delay after the external complaints body notifies it
that the complaint has been received.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 329](#1039564-1369662){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039564-1369662.html"}
- [2023, c. 26, s. 131](#1409414-1415326){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409414-1415326.html"}
:::
