## [PART XIII]{.HLabel1}[Regulation of Banks --- Superintendent]{.HTitleText1} {#h-19372 .Part}

### [Supervision]{.HTitleText2} {#h-19373 .Subheading}

#### [Returns]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19374 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required information

- **[[628]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-628 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall provide the Superintendent with such information, at such
  times and in such form as the Superintendent may require.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 86\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 36
:::

**[[629]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-629 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2007, c.
6, s. 102\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-629-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 629"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[630]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-630 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2007, c.
6, s. 102\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-630-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 630"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[631]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-631 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2007, c.
6, s. 102\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-631-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 631"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names of directors and auditors

- **[[632]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-632 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall, within thirty days after each annual meeting of the bank,
  provide the Superintendent with a return showing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name, residence and citizenship of each
    director holding office immediately following the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the mailing address of each director holding office
    immediately following the meeting;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the bodies corporate of which each director
    referred to in paragraph (a) is an officer or director and the firms
    of which each director is a member;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the affiliation, within the meaning of section 162,
    with the bank of each director referred to in paragraph (a);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the names of the directors referred to in
    paragraph (a) who are officers or employees of the bank or any
    affiliate of the bank, and the positions they occupy;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the name of each committee of the bank on which
    each director referred to in paragraph (a) serves;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the date of expiration of the term of each director
    referred to in paragraph (a); and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and date of appointment of the
    auditor or auditors of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Changes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any information relating to a director or an
    auditor of a bank shown in the latest return made to the
    Superintendent under subsection (1), other than information referred
    to in paragraph (1)(c) or (d), becomes inaccurate or incomplete,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a vacancy in the office of auditor of the bank
    occurs or is filled by another person, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a vacancy on the board of directors of the bank
    occurs or is filled,

  the bank shall forthwith provide the Superintendent with such
  information as is required to maintain the return in a complete and
  accurate form.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 38
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy of by-laws

**[[633]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-633 .sectionLabel}** A bank shall send to
the Superintendent, within thirty days after the coming into effect of a
by-law or an amendment to a by-law, a copy of the by-law or amendment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 38
- 2001, c. 9, s. 173
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Register of banks

- **[[634]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-634 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent shall, in respect of each bank for which an order
  approving the commencement and carrying on of business has been made,
  cause a register to be maintained containing a copy of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the incorporating instrument of the bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs
    632(1)(a), (c) and (e) to (h) contained in the latest return sent to
    the Superintendent under section 632.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The register may be maintained in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a bound or loose-leaf form or in a photographic
    film form; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a system of mechanical or electronic data
    processing or any other information storage device that is capable
    of reproducing any required information in intelligible written form
    within a reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Persons are entitled to reasonable access to the
  register and may make copies of or take extracts from the information
  in it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A statement containing information in the register
  and purporting to be certified by the Superintendent is admissible in
  evidence in all courts as proof, in the absence of evidence to the
  contrary, of the facts stated in the statement without proof of the
  appointment or signature of the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 39
- 2001, c. 9, s. 173
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate

**[[634.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-634.1 .sectionLabel}** On the application
of a bank that has been incorporated by a special Act of Parliament, the
Superintendent may issue a certificate stating that the bank was
incorporated by a special Act of Parliament, and may include with the
certificate any information in the Superintendent's possession that
relates to the bank's incorporation.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2012, c. 5, s. 75
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Production of information and documents

- **[[635]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-635 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent may, by order, direct a person who controls a bank or
  any entity that is affiliated with a bank to provide the
  Superintendent with any information or documents that may be specified
  in the order if the Superintendent believes that the production of the
  information or documents is necessary in order to be satisfied that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of this Act are being duly observed
    and that the bank is in a sound financial condition; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the bank has adequate policies and procedures to
    protect itself against threats to its integrity or security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any person to whom a direction has been issued under
  subsection (1) shall provide the information or documents specified in
  the order within the time specified in the order and, where the order
  does not specify a time, the person shall provide the information or
  documents within a reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an entity
  that controls a bank or is affiliated with a bank where that entity is
  a financial institution regulated

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by or under an Act of Parliament; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by or under an Act of the legislature of a province
    where the Superintendent has entered into an agreement with the
    appropriate official or public body responsible for the supervision
    of financial institutions in that province concerning the sharing of
    information on such financial institutions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 40
- [2023, c. 26, s. 555](#1410996-1415450){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1410996-1415450.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-635-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 635"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidential information

- **[[636]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-636
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 639, all
  information regarding the business or affairs of a bank or a foreign
  bank, or regarding a person dealing with a bank or a foreign bank,
  that is obtained by the Superintendent, or by any person acting under
  the direction of the Superintendent, as a result of the administration
  or enforcement of any Act of Parliament, and all information prepared
  from that information, is confidential and shall be treated
  accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure permitted

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) prevents the Superintendent
  from disclosing any information

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to any government agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision,

  - [(a.01)]{.lawlabel} to any other agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision,

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} to the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation for
    purposes related to its operation, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to the Deputy Minister of Finance or any officer of
    the Department of Finance authorized in writing by the Deputy
    Minister of Finance or to the Governor of the Bank of Canada or any
    officer of the Bank of Canada authorized in writing by the Governor
    of the Bank of Canada, for the purposes of policy analysis related
    to the regulation of financial institutions,

  if the Superintendent is satisfied that the information will be
  treated as confidential by the agency, body or person to whom it is
  disclosed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 41
- 2001, c. 9, s. 174
- 2007, c. 6, s. 103
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-636-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 636"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

**[[637]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-637 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may make regulations prohibiting, limiting or restricting the disclosure
by banks of prescribed supervisory information.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 42
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidentiary privilege

- **[[638]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-638
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Prescribed supervisory information
  shall not be used as evidence in any civil proceedings and is
  privileged for that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No testimony or production

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall by an order of any court, tribunal or
  other body be required in any civil proceedings to give oral testimony
  or to produce any document relating to any prescribed supervisory
  information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions to subsection (1)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Minister, the Superintendent or the Attorney
    General of Canada may, in accordance with the regulations, if any,
    use prescribed supervisory information as evidence in any
    proceedings; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a bank may, in accordance with the regulations, if
    any, use prescribed supervisory information as evidence in any
    proceedings in relation to the administration or enforcement of this
    Act or the [Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11) that
    are commenced by the bank, the Minister, the Superintendent or the
    Attorney General of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions to subsections (1) and (2)

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections (1) and (2) and section 39.1 of
  the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
  Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), a court, tribunal or other body may, by order,
  require the Minister, the Superintendent or a bank to give oral
  testimony or to produce any document relating to any prescribed
  supervisory information in any civil proceedings in relation to the
  administration or enforcement of this Act that are commenced by the
  Minister, the Superintendent, the Attorney General of Canada or the
  bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No waiver

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure of any prescribed supervisory
  information, other than under subsection (3) or (4), does not
  constitute a waiver of the privilege referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may, for the purposes of
  subsection (3), make regulations respecting the circumstances in which
  prescribed supervisory information may be used as evidence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 43
- 2007, c. 6, s. 104
- 2015, c. 36, s. 234
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-638-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 638"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No waiver

- **[[638.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-638.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, the
  disclosure by a bank --- or by a person who controls a bank or by an
  entity that is affiliated with a bank --- to the Superintendent of any
  information that is subject to a privilege under the law of evidence,
  solicitor-client privilege or the professional secrecy of advocates
  and notaries or to litigation privilege does not constitute a waiver
  of any of those privileges or that secrecy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No disclosure

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall not disclose any information
  referred to in subsection (1) to any person whose powers, duties or
  functions include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the investigation or prosecution of an offence
    under any Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the investigation of, or conduct of proceedings in
    respect of, a violation under an Act referred to in paragraph (a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 27, s. 170
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure by Superintendent

- **[[639]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-639 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent shall disclose, at such times and in such manner as the
  Minister may determine, such information obtained by the
  Superintendent under this Act as the Minister considers ought to be
  disclosed for the purposes of the analysis of the financial condition
  of a bank and that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is contained in returns filed pursuant to the
    Superintendent's financial regulatory reporting requirements in
    respect of banks; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has been obtained as a result of an industry-wide
    or sectoral survey conducted by the Superintendent in relation to an
    issue or circumstances that could have an impact on the financial
    condition of banks.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prior consultation required

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall consult with the Superintendent
  before making any determination under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 44
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure by a bank

- **[[640]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-640 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank shall make available to the public such information concerning

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the compensation of its executives, as that
    expression is defined by the regulations, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} its business and affairs for the purposes of the
    analysis of its financial condition,

  in such form and manner and at such times as may be required by or
  pursuant to such regulations as the Governor in Council may make for
  the purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by regulation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply to a bank that is
  within such class or classes of banks as may be prescribed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 44
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions to disclosure

**[[641]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-641 .sectionLabel}** Subject to any
regulations made under paragraph 627.998(n), no information obtained by
a bank regarding any of its customers shall be disclosed or made
available under subsection 639(1) or section 640.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 45
- [2018, c. 27, s. 330](#1039566-1370398){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039566-1370398.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-641-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 641"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report respecting disclosure

**[[642]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-642 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
shall prepare a report, to be included in the report referred to in
section 40 of the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial
Institutions Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), respecting the disclosure of
information by banks and describing the state of progress made in
enhancing the disclosure of information in the financial services
industry.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 46
- 2001, c. 9, s. 175
:::

#### [Inspection of Banks]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19506 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of banks

- **[[643]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-643 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent, from time to time, but at least once in each calendar
  year, shall make or cause to be made any examination and inquiry into
  the business and affairs of each bank that the Superintendent
  considers to be necessary or expedient to determine whether the bank
  is complying with the provisions of this Act, whether the bank is in a
  sound financial condition and whether the bank has adequate policies
  and procedures to protect itself against threats to its integrity or
  security. After the conclusion of each examination and inquiry, the
  Superintendent shall report on it to the Minister.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2023, c. 26, s. 556\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to records of bank

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent or a person acting under the
  Superintendent's direction

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a right of access to any records, cash, assets
    and security held by or on behalf of a bank; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may require the directors, officers and the auditor
    or auditors of a bank to provide information and explanations, to
    the extent that they are reasonably able to do so, in respect of the
    condition and affairs of the bank or any entity in which the bank
    has a substantial investment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 46
- 2001, c. 9, s. 176
- 2012, c. 5, s. 76
- [2023, c. 26, s. 556](#1410998-1415453){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1410998-1415453.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-643-20230622.html "Link to previous version of section 643"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power of Superintendent on inquiry

**[[644]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-644 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent has
all the powers of a person appointed as a commissioner under Part II of
the [Inquiries Act](/eng/acts/I-11) for the purpose of obtaining
evidence under oath, and may delegate those powers to any person acting
under the Superintendent's direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 46
:::

### [Remedial Powers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-19520 .Subheading}

#### [Prudential Agreements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19521 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prudential agreement

**[[644.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-644.1 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
may enter into an agreement, called a "prudential agreement", with a
bank for the purposes of implementing any measure designed to maintain
or improve its safety and soundness or establishing adequate policies
and procedures to protect it against threats to its integrity or
security.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 177
- [2023, c. 26, s. 557](#1411004-1415456){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411004-1415456.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-644.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 644.1"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Directions of Compliance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19526 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent's directions to bank

- **[[645]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-645
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where, in the opinion of the
  Superintendent, a bank, or a person with respect to a bank, is
  committing, or is about to commit, an act that is an unsafe or unsound
  practice in conducting the business of the bank, or is pursuing or is
  about to pursue any course of conduct that is an unsafe or unsound
  practice in conducting the business of the bank, the Superintendent
  may direct the bank or person to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} cease or refrain from committing the act or
    pursuing the course of conduct; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} perform such acts as in the opinion of the
    Superintendent are necessary to remedy the situation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directions --- policies and procedures

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, a bank
  does not have adequate policies and procedures to protect itself
  against threats to its integrity or security, the Superintendent may
  direct the bank to take any measures that in the opinion of the
  Superintendent are necessary to remedy the situation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opportunity for representations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no direction shall be
  issued to a bank or person under subsection (1) or (1.1) unless the
  bank or person is provided with a reasonable opportunity to make
  representations in respect of the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary direction

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the length
  of time required for representations to be made under subsection (2)
  might be prejudicial to the public interest, the Superintendent may
  make a temporary direction with respect to the matters referred to in
  paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) or subsection (1.1) having effect for a
  period of not more than 15 days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continued effect

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A temporary direction under subsection (3) continues
  to have effect after the expiration of the fifteen day period referred
  to in that subsection if no representations are made to the
  Superintendent within that period or, if representations have been
  made, the Superintendent notifies the bank or person that the
  Superintendent is not satisfied that there are sufficient grounds for
  revoking the direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 47
- [2023, c. 26, s. 558](#1411006-1415463){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411006-1415463.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-645-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 645"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement

- **[[646]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-646
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a bank or person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is contravening or has failed to comply with a
    prudential agreement entered into under section 644.1 or a direction
    of the Superintendent made under subsection 645(1), (1.1) or (3),

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is contravening this Act, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has omitted to do any thing under this Act that is
    required to be done by or on the part of the bank or person,

  the Superintendent may, in addition to any other action that may be
  taken under this Act, apply to a court for an order requiring the bank
  or person to comply with the prudential agreement or the direction,
  cease the contravention or do any thing that is required to be done,
  and on such application the court may so order and make any other
  order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from a decision of a court under
  subsection (1) lies in the same manner, and to the same court, as an
  appeal from any other order of the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 48
- 2001, c. 9, s. 178
- [2023, c. 26, s. 559](#1411008-1415465){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411008-1415465.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-646-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 646"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Disqualification and Removal of Directors or Senior Officers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19551 .Subheading}

Meaning of [[senior officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[646.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-646.1 .sectionLabel}** In sections 647 and
647.1, [[senior officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the chief executive
officer, secretary, treasurer or controller of a bank or any other
officer reporting directly to the bank's board of directors or chief
executive officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 179
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

- **[[647]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-647 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This
  section applies only in respect of a bank

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that has been notified by the Superintendent that
    this section applies to it where the bank is subject to measures
    designed to maintain or improve its safety and soundness, which
    measures

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} have been specified by the Superintendent by way
      of conditions or limitations in respect of the order approving the
      commencement and carrying on of the bank's business, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} are contained in a prudential agreement entered
      into under section 644.1 or an undertaking given by the bank to
      the Superintendent; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is the subject of a direction made under
    section 645 or an order made under subsection 485(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank shall provide the Superintendent with the name
  of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} each person who has been nominated for election or
    appointment as a member of its board of directors,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each person who has been selected by the bank for
    appointment as a senior officer, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each person who is newly elected as a director of
    the bank and who was not proposed for election by anyone involved in
    the management of the bank,

  together with such other information about the background, business
  record and experience of the person as the Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When information to be provided

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The information required by subsection (2) shall be
  provided to the Superintendent

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least thirty days prior to the date or proposed
    date of the election or appointment or within such shorter period as
    the Superintendent may allow; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person referred to in paragraph
    (2)(c), within fifteen days after the date of the election of the
    person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualification or removal

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that, on the
  basis of the competence, business record, experience, conduct or
  character of a person, he or she is not suitable to hold that
  position, the Superintendent may, by order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person referred to in paragraph
    (2)(a) or (b), disqualify the person from being elected or appointed
    as a director of a bank or from being appointed as a senior officer;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person referred to in paragraph
    (2)(c), remove the person from office as a director of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Risk of prejudice

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} In forming an opinion under subsection (4), the
  Superintendent must consider whether the interests of the depositors
  and creditors of the bank would likely be prejudiced if the person
  were to take office or continue to hold office, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations may be made

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must in writing notify the person
  concerned and the bank of any action that the Superintendent proposes
  to take under subsection (4) and must afford them an opportunity
  within 15 days after the date of the notice, or within any longer
  period that the Superintendent allows, to make representations to the
  Superintendent in relation to the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where an order has been made under subsection (4)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} disqualifying a person from being elected or
    appointed to a position, the person shall not be, and the bank shall
    not permit the person to be, elected or appointed to the position;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} removing a director from office, the person shall
    not continue to hold, and the bank shall not permit the person to
    continue to hold, office as a director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 49
- 2001, c. 9, s. 180
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2080
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-647-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 647"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of directors or senior officers

- **[[647.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-647.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order,
  remove a person from office as a director or senior officer of a bank
  if the Superintendent is of the opinion that the person is not
  suitable to hold that office

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on the basis of the competence, business record,
    experience, conduct or character of the person; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} because the person has contravened or, by action or
    negligence, has contributed to the contravention of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} this Act or the regulations made under it,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a direction made under section 645,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an order made under subsection 485(3),

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a condition or limitation in respect of the
      order approving the commencement and carrying on of the bank's
      business, or

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a prudential agreement entered into under section
      644.1 or an undertaking given by the bank to the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Risk of prejudice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In forming an opinion under subsection (1), the
  Superintendent must consider whether the interests of the depositors
  and creditors of the bank have been or are likely to be prejudiced by
  the person's holding office as a director or senior officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations may be made

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must in writing notify the person
  concerned and the bank of any removal order that the Superintendent
  proposes to make under subsection (1) and must afford them an
  opportunity within 15 days after the date of the notice, or within any
  longer period that the Superintendent allows, to make representations
  to the Superintendent in relation to the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Suspension

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that the
  public interest may be prejudiced by the director or senior officer
  continuing to exercise the powers or carry out the duties and
  functions of that office during the period for making representations,
  the Superintendent may make an order suspending the director or senior
  officer. The suspension may not extend beyond 10 days after the
  expiration of that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of order

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall, without delay, notify the
  director or senior officer, as the case may be, and the bank of a
  removal order or suspension order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consequences of removal order

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The director or senior officer, as the case may be,
  ceases to hold that office as of the date the removal order is made or
  any later date specified in the order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The director or senior officer, as the case may be,
  or the bank may, within 30 days after the date of receipt of notice of
  the removal order under subsection (5), or within any longer period
  that the Court allows, appeal the matter to the Federal Court.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of Federal Court

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The Federal Court, in the case of an appeal, may
  dismiss the appeal or set aside the removal order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order not stayed by appeal

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} A removal order is not stayed by an appeal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 181
:::

#### [Supervisory Intervention]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19615 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may take control

- **[[648]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-648
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, where any of
  the circumstances described in subsection (1.1) exist in respect of a
  bank, the Superintendent may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period not exceeding sixteen
    days, of the assets of the bank and the assets under its
    administration; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} unless the Minister advises the Superintendent that
    the Minister is of the opinion that it is not in the public interest
    to do so,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period exceeding sixteen
      days, of the assets of the bank and the assets under its
      administration,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where control of assets has been taken under
      paragraph (a), continue the control beyond the sixteen days
      referred to in that paragraph, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} take control of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circumstances for taking control

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under subsection (1)
  may be taken in respect of a bank where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the bank has failed to pay its liabilities or, in
    the opinion of the Superintendent, will not be able to pay its
    liabilities as they become due and payable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2001, c. 9, s. 182\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the assets of the bank are not, in the opinion of
    the Superintendent, sufficient to give adequate protection to the
    bank's depositors and creditors;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any asset appearing on the books or records of the
    bank or held under its administration is not, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, satisfactorily accounted for;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the regulatory capital of the bank has, in the
    opinion of the Superintendent, reached a level or is eroding in a
    manner that may detrimentally affect its depositors or creditors;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the bank has failed to comply with an order of the
    Superintendent under paragraph 485(3)(a);

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the bank's deposit insurance has been terminated by
    the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation;

  - [(g.1)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the bank's
    depositors and creditors may be detrimentally affected because all
    of the common shares or membership shares of the bank must be
    disposed of under a direction made by the Minister or because there
    is a prohibition under this Act in respect of the exercise of the
    right to vote attached to all of the common shares or membership
    shares of the bank;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, any other
    state of affairs exists in respect of the bank that may be
    materially prejudicial to the interests of the bank's depositors or
    creditors or the owners of any assets under the bank's
    administration, including where proceedings under a law relating to
    bankruptcy or insolvency have been commenced in Canada or elsewhere
    in respect of the holding body corporate of the bank;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the continued
    operation of the bank by the directors of the bank or by the
    officers of the bank responsible for its management would be
    materially prejudicial to its integrity or security; or

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the continued
    operation of the bank by the directors of the bank or by the
    officers of the bank responsible for its management would pose a
    risk to national security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister's powers

  [(1.11)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, the Minister may, for reasons
  related to national security, direct the Superintendent to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period not exceeding 16 days,
    of the assets of the bank and the assets under its administration;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period exceeding 16 days, of
    the assets of the bank and the assets under its administration;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if control of assets has been taken under paragraph
    (a), continue the control beyond the 16 days referred to in that
    paragraph; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} take control of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of proposed action

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must notify a bank of any action
  proposed to be taken in respect of it under paragraph (1)(b) and of
  its right to make written representations to the Superintendent within
  the time specified in the notice, not exceeding ten days after it
  receives the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- up to 16 days

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent takes control of the assets
  of the bank under paragraph (1.11)(a), the Superintendent shall notify
  the bank that control has been taken at the direction of the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- more than 16 days

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister is considering whether to exercise
  the powers under any of paragraphs (1.11)(b) to (d), the
  Superintendent shall notify the bank of the action that is being
  considered and of its right to make written representations to the
  Minister within the time specified in the notice, not exceeding 10
  days after it receives the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- Committee and Review Agency

  [(1.5)]{.lawlabel} Within 30 days after exercising any of the powers
  under subsection (1.11), the Minister shall notify

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the [[Committee]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined
    in section 2 of the [National Security and Intelligence Committee of
    Parliamentarians Act](/eng/acts/N-16.6); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the [[Review Agency]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as
    defined in section 2 of the [National Security and Intelligence
    Review Agency Act](/eng/acts/N-16.62).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Objectives of Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent has control under
  subsection (1) or (1.11) of the assets of a bank referred to in that
  subsection, the Superintendent may do all things necessary or
  expedient to protect the rights and interests of the depositors and
  creditors of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent has control under
  subsection (1) or (1.11) of the assets of a bank referred to in that
  subsection,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the bank shall not make, acquire or transfer any
    loan or make any purchase, sale or exchange of securities or any
    disbursement or transfer of cash of any kind without the prior
    approval of the Superintendent or a representative designated by the
    Superintendent; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no director, officer or employee of the bank shall
    have access to any cash or securities held by the bank unless

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a representative of the Superintendent
      accompanies the director, officer or employee, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the access is previously authorized by the
      Superintendent or the Superintendent's representative.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 50
- 2001, c. 9, s. 182
- [2023, c. 26, s. 560](#1411010-1415488){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411010-1415488.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-648-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 648"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers suspended

- **[[649]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-649 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Superintendent takes control of a bank under subparagraph
  648(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 648(1.11)(d), the powers, duties,
  functions, rights and privileges of the directors of the bank and of
  the officers of the bank responsible for its management are suspended.
  If the bank is a federal credit union, the powers of the members to
  make, amend or repeal by-laws are also suspended.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent to manage bank

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent takes control of a bank under
  subparagraph 648(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 648(1.11)(d), the
  Superintendent shall manage the business and affairs of the bank and
  in doing so the Superintendent

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} may perform any of the duties and functions that
    the persons referred to in subsection (1) were performing prior to
    the taking of control; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has and may exercise any power, right or privilege
    that any such person had or could have exercised prior to the taking
    of control.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Persons to assist

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent takes control of a bank under
  subparagraph 648(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 648(1.11)(d), the
  Superintendent may appoint one or more persons to assist in the
  management of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 51
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2081
- [2023, c. 26, s. 561(E)](#1411021-1415493){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411021-1415493.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-649-20121219.html "Link to previous version of section 649"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expiration of control

- **[[650]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-650
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under
  subsection 648(1) of a bank or of the assets of a bank expires on the
  day on which a notice by the Superintendent is sent to the directors
  and officers who conducted the business and affairs of the bank
  stating that the Superintendent is of the opinion that the
  circumstances leading to the taking of control by the Superintendent
  have been substantially rectified and that the bank can resume control
  of its business and affairs.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expiration of control --- Minister's
  direction

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under subsection
  648(1.11) of a bank or of the assets of a bank expires on the day on
  which a notice by the Superintendent is sent to the directors and
  officers who conducted the business and affairs of the bank stating
  that the Minister is of the opinion, on the recommendation of the
  Superintendant, that corrective measures have been taken in response
  to the reasons related to national security and that the bank can
  resume control of its business and affairs.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 52
- [2023, c. 26, s. 562](#1411028-1415499){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411028-1415499.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-650-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 650"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may request winding-up

**[[651]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-651 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may,
at any time before the receipt of a request under section 652 to
relinquish control of a bank or of the assets of a bank, request the
Attorney General of Canada to apply for a winding-up order under section
10.1 of the [Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11) in
respect of the bank, where

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the assets of the bank are under the control of the
  Superintendent under subparagraph 648(1)(b)(i) or (ii) or paragraph
  648(1.11)(b) or (c); or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the bank is under the control of the Superintendent
  under subparagraph 648(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 648(1.11)(d).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 52
- [2023, c. 26, s. 563](#1411030-1415502){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411030-1415502.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-651-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 651"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement to relinquish control

**[[652]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-652 .sectionLabel}** If no action has been
taken by the Superintendent under section 651 and, after 30 days
following the taking of control by the Superintendent under subsection
648(1) or (1.11) of a bank or of the assets of a bank, the
Superintendent receives from its board of directors a notice in writing
requesting the Superintendent to relinquish control, the Superintendent
shall, not later than 12 days after receipt of the notice,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} comply with the request; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} request the Attorney General of Canada to apply for a
  winding-up order under section 10.1 of the [Winding-up and
  Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11) in respect of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 53
- [2023, c. 26, s. 564(E)](#1411032-1415504){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411032-1415504.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-652-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 652"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advisory committee

**[[653]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-653 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may,
from among the banks and authorized foreign banks that are subject to an
assessment under section 23 of the [Office of the Superintendent of
Financial Institutions Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7) and required to share in
the expenses resulting from the taking of control of a bank under
subsection 648(1) or (1.11), appoint a committee of not more than six
members to advise the Superintendent in respect of assets, management
and all other matters pertinent to the duties and responsibilities of
the Superintendent in exercising control of the bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 54
- [2023, c. 26, s. 565(E)](#1411034-1415507){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411034-1415507.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-653-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 653"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses payable by bank

- **[[654]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-654 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Superintendent has taken control of a bank under subparagraph
  648(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 648(1.11)(d) and the control expires or is
  relinquished under section 650 or paragraph 652(a), the Superintendent
  may direct that the bank be liable for repayment of all or part of the
  expenses resulting from the taking of control of the bank and assessed
  against and paid by other banks and by authorized foreign banks under
  section 23 of the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial
  Institutions Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), together with any interest in
  respect of the expenses at any rate that is specified by the
  Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Debt due to Her Majesty

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where any direction is made under subsection (1), the
  amount for which the bank is liable is a debt due to Her Majesty in
  right of Canada payable on demand and is recoverable in the Federal
  Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 55
- [2023, c. 26, s. 566(E)](#1411036-1415509){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411036-1415509.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-654-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 654"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Priority of claim in liquidation

**[[655]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-655 .sectionLabel}** In the case of the
winding-up of a bank, the expenses resulting from the taking of control
of the bank under subsection 648(1) or (1.11) and assessed against and
paid by other banks and by authorized foreign banks under section 23 of
the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), and interest in respect of the expenses at any
rate that is specified by the Superintendent, constitute a claim of His
Majesty in right of Canada against the assets of the bank that ranks
after all other claims but prior to any claim in respect of the shares
or membership shares of the bank.

- 1999, c. 28, s. 56

:::

Version](section-655-20121219.html "Link to previous version of section 655"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of assessment

**[[656]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-656 .sectionLabel}** Any amount recovered
pursuant to section 654 or 655 shall be applied to reduce the total
amount of expenses incurred for or in connection with the administration
of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 57
:::

## [PART XIV]{.HLabel1}[Regulation of Banks and External Complaints Bodies --- Commissioner]{.HTitleText1} {#h-19692 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required information

**[[657]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-657 .sectionLabel}** A bank, authorized
foreign bank or external complaints body must provide the Commissioner
with the information at the times and in the form that he or she may
require for the purposes of the administration of the [Financial
Consumer Agency of Canada Act](/eng/acts/F-11.1) and the consumer
provisions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 58
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2010, c. 25, s. 151
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-657-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 657"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidential information

- **[[658]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-658
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2),
  information regarding the business or affairs of a bank, authorized
  foreign bank or external complaints body or regarding persons dealing
  with any of them that is obtained by the Commissioner or by any person
  acting under the Commissioner's direction, in the course of the
  exercise or performance of powers, duties and functions referred to in
  subsection 5(1) of the [Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
  Act](/eng/acts/F-11.1), and any information prepared from that
  information, is confidential and shall be treated accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure permitted

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Commissioner is satisfied that the information
  will be treated as confidential by the agency, body or person to whom
  it is disclosed, subsection (1) does not prevent the Commissioner from
  disclosing it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to any government agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to any other agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} to the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation, for
    purposes related to its operation; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} to the Deputy Minister of Finance or any officer of
    the Department of Finance authorized in writing by the Deputy
    Minister of Finance or to the Governor of the Bank of Canada or any
    officer of the Bank of Canada authorized in writing by the Governor
    of the Bank of Canada, for the purposes of policy analysis related
    to the regulation of financial institutions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 59
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2010, c. 25, s. 152
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-658-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 658"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of banks

- **[[659]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-659 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Commissioner, from time to time but at least once in each calendar
  year, shall make or cause to be made any examination and inquiry that
  the Commissioner considers necessary for the purposes of satisfying
  the Commissioner that the applicable consumer provisions are being
  complied with and, after the conclusion of each examination and
  inquiry, shall report on it to the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special audit

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner may direct that a special audit be
  made in accordance with any terms and conditions that he or she
  considers appropriate if, in the opinion of the Commissioner, it is
  required for the purposes of the administration of the [Financial
  Consumer Agency of Canada Act](/eng/acts/F-11.1) and the consumer
  provisions, and may appoint for that purpose

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to a bank or an authorized foreign
    bank, a firm of accountants qualified under subsection 315(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to the external complaints body, a
    [[firm of accountants]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in section
    313.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report to Commissioner

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} If a bank, an authorized foreign bank or the
  external complaints body is the subject of a special audit, it shall
  provide the Commissioner with the results of the audit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses payable

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} The expenses incurred in respect of any special
  audit are payable by the bank, the authorized foreign bank or the
  external complaints body that is the subject of the audit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to records of bank

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner, or a person acting under the
  Commissioner's direction, in carrying out his or her duties under this
  section

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a right of access to any records, including
    electronic records, of a bank, authorized foreign bank or external
    complaints body; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may require the directors or officers of a bank,
    authorized foreign bank or external complaints body to provide
    information and explanations, to the extent that they are reasonably
    able to do so, in respect of any matter subject to examination,
    inquiry or audit under this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 59
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2010, c. 25, s. 153
- [2018, c. 27, s. 331](#1039575-1245209){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039575-1245209.html"}
- [2023, c. 26, s. 134](#1409420-1415341){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409420-1415341.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-659-20200430.html "Link to previous version of section 659"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power of Commissioner on inquiry

**[[660]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-660 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner, in
carrying out his or her duties in relation to consumer provisions, has
all the powers of a person appointed as a commissioner under Part II of
the [Inquiries Act](/eng/acts/I-11) for the purpose of obtaining
evidence under oath, and may delegate those powers to any person acting
under the Commissioner's direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 60
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance agreement

**[[661]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-661 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner may
enter into an agreement, called a "compliance agreement", with a bank,
an authorized foreign bank or the external complaints body for the
purposes of implementing any measure that is designed so as to further
compliance by it with the consumer provisions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 61
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2010, c. 25, s. 154
- [2023, c. 26, s. 135](#1409422-1415344){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409422-1415344.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-661-20130902.html "Link to previous version of section 661"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Commissioner's directions

- **[[661.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-661.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the
  Commissioner, a bank, authorized foreign bank or person, in conducting
  the business of the bank or authorized foreign bank, fails to comply,
  or there are reasonable grounds to believe that the bank, authorized
  foreign bank or person will fail to comply, with a compliance
  agreement, a consumer provision or this Part, the Commissioner may
  direct the bank, authorized foreign bank or person to comply with them
  and to perform any act that in the opinion of the Commissioner is
  necessary to do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directions --- external complaints body

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Commissioner, the
  external complaints body fails, or there are reasonable grounds to
  believe that it will fail, to comply with a compliance agreement or
  any of paragraphs 627.49(b) to (m) or to discharge its functions and
  perform its activities in a manner that is consistent with the purpose
  set out in section 627.471, the Commissioner may direct the external
  complaints body to comply with them or to so discharge its functions
  and perform its activities and to perform any act that in the opinion
  of the Commissioner is necessary to do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opportunity for representations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no direction shall be
  issued under subsection (1) or (1.1) unless the bank, authorized
  foreign bank or person or the external complaints body is provided
  with a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of
  the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary direction

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Commissioner, the length of
  time required for representations to be made under subsection (2)
  might be prejudicial to the public interest, the Commissioner may make
  a temporary direction with respect to the matters referred to in
  subsection (1) or (1.1) that has effect for a period of not more than
  15 days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continued effect

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A temporary direction under subsection (3) continues
  to have effect after the end of the 15-day period referred to in that
  subsection if no representations are made to the Commissioner within
  that period or, if representations have been made, the Commissioner
  notifies the bank, authorized foreign bank, person or external
  complaints body that the Commissioner is not satisfied that there are
  sufficient grounds for revoking the direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 332](#1039582-1245220){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039582-1245220.html"}
- [2023, c. 26, s. 136](#1409424-1415353){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409424-1415353.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-661.1-20200430.html "Link to previous version of section 661.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement

- **[[661.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-661.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a bank, authorized foreign bank
  or person, in conducting the business of the bank or authorized
  foreign bank, contravenes or fails to comply with a compliance
  agreement or a direction made under subsection 661.1(1) or (3),
  contravenes this Act or omits to do any thing that is required to be
  done under this Act by or on the part of the bank, authorized foreign
  bank or person, the Commissioner may, in addition to any other action
  that may be taken under this Act, apply to a court for an order
  requiring the bank, authorized foreign bank or person to comply with
  the compliance agreement or the direction, cease the contravention or
  do any thing that is required to be done, and on the application the
  court may so order and make any other order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement --- external
  complaints body

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If the external complaints body contravenes or
  fails to comply with a compliance agreement, any of paragraphs
  627.49(b) to (m) or a direction made under subsection 661.1(1.1) or
  (3), the Commissioner may, in addition to any other action that may be
  taken under this Act, apply to a court for an order requiring the
  external complaints body to comply with the compliance agreement or
  the direction, cease the contravention or do any thing that is
  required to be done, and on the application the court may so order and
  make any other order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from a decision of a court under
  subsection (1) or (1.1) lies in the same manner, and to the same
  court, as an appeal from any other order of the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 332](#1039582-1245227){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039582-1245227.html"}
- [2023, c. 26, s. 137](#1409426-1415358){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1409426-1415358.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-661.2-20200430.html "Link to previous version of section 661.2"){.PITLink}
:::

## [PART XV]{.HLabel1}[Bank Holding Companies]{.HTitleText1} {#h-19725 .Part}

### [Purpose]{.HTitleText2} {#h-19726 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purpose

**[[662]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-662 .sectionLabel}** The purpose of this
Part is to provide for the incorporation, formation and regulation of
bank holding companies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 61
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

### [DIVISION 1]{.HLabel2}[Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-19731 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[663]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-663 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  following definitions apply in this Part.

  [[complainant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[complainant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to a bank holding
      company or any matter concerning a bank holding company, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a registered holder or beneficial owner, and a
        former registered holder or beneficial owner, of a security of a
        bank holding company or any of its affiliates;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a director or an officer, or a former director
        or officer, of a bank holding company or any of its affiliates;
        or

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other person who, in the discretion of a
        court, is a proper person to make an application under section
        334, 338 or 989. ([plaignant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[subordinated indebtedness]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[subordinated indebtedness]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
      instrument evidencing an indebtedness of a bank holding company
      that by its terms provides that the indebtedness will, in the
      event of the insolvency or winding-up of the bank holding company,
      be subordinate in right of payment to all liabilities of the bank
      holding company except those that, by their terms, rank equally
      with or are subordinate to such indebtedness. ([titre
      secondaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions in other Parts

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A reference in a provision of this Part to a
  provision in any other Part is deemed to be a reference to that
  provision as it has been made applicable by this Part in respect of
  bank holding companies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}References in other Parts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A reference in a provision of another Part to a
  provision that has been made applicable in respect of bank holding
  companies by this Part is to be read as including a reference to that
  provision as it has been made applicable in respect of bank holding
  companies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 61
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

### [DIVISION 2]{.HLabel2}[Status and Powers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-19746 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corporate powers

- **[[664]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-664 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank holding company has the capacity of a natural person and, subject
  to this Act, the rights, powers and privileges of a natural person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers restricted

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company shall not carry on any
  business or exercise any power that it is restricted by this Act from
  carrying on or exercising, or exercise any of its powers in a manner
  contrary to this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Business in Canada

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company may carry on business
  throughout Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers outside Canada

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, a bank holding company has the
  capacity to carry on its business, conduct its affairs and exercise
  its powers in any jurisdiction outside Canada to the extent and in the
  manner that the laws of that jurisdiction permit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 61
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policies and procedures --- integrity or
security

**[[664.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-664.1 .sectionLabel}** A bank holding
company shall establish and adhere to policies and procedures to protect
itself against threats to its integrity or security, including foreign
interference.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2023, c. 26, s. 568](#1411040-1437061){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411040-1437061.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No invalidity

**[[665]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-665 .sectionLabel}** No act of a bank
holding company, including any transfer of property to or by a bank
holding company, is invalid by reason only that the act or transfer is
contrary to the bank holding company's incorporating instrument or this
Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 62
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law not necessary

**[[666]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-666 .sectionLabel}** It is not necessary for
a bank holding company to pass a by-law in order to confer any
particular power on the bank holding company or its directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 63
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No personal liability

**[[667]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-667 .sectionLabel}** The shareholders of a
bank holding company are not, as shareholders, liable for any liability,
act or default of the bank holding company except as otherwise provided
by this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 63
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No constructive notice

**[[668]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-668 .sectionLabel}** No person is affected
by or is deemed to have notice or knowledge of the contents of a
document concerning a bank holding company by reason only that the
document has been filed with the Superintendent or the Minister or is
available for inspection at an office of the bank holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 64, c. 31, ss. 16(F), 250
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authority of directors, officers and
representatives

- **[[669]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-669 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  bank holding company and no guarantor of an obligation of a bank
  holding company may assert against a person dealing with the bank
  holding company or against a person who has acquired rights from the
  bank holding company that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the bank holding company's incorporating instrument
    or any by-laws of the bank holding company have not been complied
    with;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the persons named as directors of the bank holding
    company in the most recent return sent to the Superintendent under
    section 951 are not the directors of the bank holding company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the place named in the incorporating instrument or
    by-laws of the bank holding company is not the place where the head
    office of the bank holding company is situated;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person held out by the bank holding company as a
    director, officer or representative of the bank holding company has
    not been duly appointed or has no authority to exercise the powers
    and perform the duties that are customary in the business of the
    bank holding company or usual for a director, officer or
    representative; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a document issued by any director, officer or
    representative of the bank holding company with actual or usual
    authority to issue the document is not valid or not genuine.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- knowledge

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a person
  who has or ought to have knowledge of a situation described in that
  subsection by virtue of their relationship to the bank holding
  company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 65
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 83
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-669-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 669"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sunset provision

- **[[670]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-670
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (4),
  bank holding companies shall not carry on business after June 30,
  2026.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may, by order, extend by up
  to six months the time during which bank holding companies may
  continue to carry on business. No more than one order may be made
  under this subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order not a regulation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The order is not a regulation for the purposes of the
  [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22). However, it shall be
  published in Part II of the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- dissolution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If Parliament dissolves on the day set out in
  subsection (1) or on any day within the six-month period before that
  day or on any day within an extension ordered under subsection (2),
  bank holding companies may continue to carry on business until the end
  of the 180th day after the first day of the first session of the next
  Parliament.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 65
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2006, c. 4, s. 199.1
- 2007, c. 6, s. 105
- 2012, c. 5, s. 77
- 2016, c. 7, s. 119
- 2018, c. 12, s. 356
- [2021, c. 23, s. 155](#1307140-1311358){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1307140-1311358.html"}
- [2024, c. 17, s. 405](#1468535-1479710){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1468535-1479710.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-670-20210629.html "Link to previous version of section 670"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 3]{.HLabel2}[Incorporation and Continuance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-19797 .Subheading}

#### [Formalities of Incorporation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-19798 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporation of bank holding company

**[[671]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-671 .sectionLabel}** On the application of
one or more persons made in accordance with this Part, the Minister may,
subject to this Division, issue letters patent incorporating a bank
holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 66
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restrictions on incorporation

**[[672]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-672 .sectionLabel}** Letters patent
incorporating a bank holding company may not be issued if the
application therefor is made by or on behalf of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of Canada or in right of a
  province, an agency of Her Majesty in either of those rights, or an
  entity controlled by Her Majesty in either of those rights;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the government of a foreign country or any political
  subdivision thereof;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an agency of the government of a foreign country or
  any political subdivision thereof; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} an entity, other than a foreign institution or any
  subsidiary of a foreign institution, that is controlled by the
  government of a foreign country or any political subdivision thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 66
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}National treatment

**[[673]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-673 .sectionLabel}** If a proposed bank
holding company would be a subsidiary of a foreign bank, within the
meaning of any of paragraphs (a) to (f) of the definition [[foreign
bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 2, letters patent to incorporate
the bank holding company may not be issued unless the Minister is
satisfied that, if the application is made by a non-WTO Member foreign
bank, treatment as favourable for bank holding companies to which this
Act applies exists or will be provided in the jurisdiction in which the
foreign bank principally carries on business, either directly or through
a subsidiary.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 67
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for incorporation

**[[674]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-674 .sectionLabel}** An application for
letters patent to incorporate a bank holding company setting out the
names of the first directors of the bank holding company shall be filed
with the Superintendent, together with such other information, material
and evidence as the Superintendent may require.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 68
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters for consideration

**[[675]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-675 .sectionLabel}** Before issuing letters
patent to incorporate a bank holding company, the Minister shall take
into account all matters that the Minister considers relevant to the
application, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the nature and sufficiency of the financial resources
  of the applicant or applicants as a source of continuing financial
  support for the bank that is proposed to be its subsidiary;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the soundness and feasibility of the plans of the
  applicant or applicants for the future conduct and development of the
  business of the bank that is proposed to be its subsidiary;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business record and experience of the applicant
  or applicants;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the character and integrity of the applicant or
  applicants or, if the applicant or any of the applicants is a body
  corporate, its reputation for being operated in a manner that is
  consistent with the standards of good character and integrity;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} whether the bank holding company will be operated
  responsibly by persons with the competence and experience suitable for
  involvement in the operation of a financial institution;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the impact of any integration of the businesses and
  operations of the applicant or applicants with those of the bank
  holding company and its affiliates on the conduct of those businesses
  and operations; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the best interests of the financial system in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 69
- 2000, c. 12, s. 6
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of letters patent

- **[[676]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-676
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} There shall be set out in the
  letters patent incorporating a bank holding company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the bank holding company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the province in which the head office of the bank
    holding company is to be situated; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date that the bank holding company came, or is
    to come, into existence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions in letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may set out in the letters patent
  incorporating a bank holding company any provision not contrary to
  this Act that the Minister considers advisable in order to take into
  account the particular circumstances of the proposed bank holding
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms and conditions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may impose such terms and conditions in
  respect of the issuance of letters patent incorporating a bank holding
  company as the Minister considers necessary or appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 70
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 84
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-676-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 676"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent of incorporation on
application of banks

- **[[677]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-677 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If,
  under section 671, the Minister issues letters patent incorporating a
  bank holding company on the application of a bank, there may, on the
  request of the bank, and with the approval of the Minister, be
  included in the letters patent of incorporation of the bank holding
  company a provision deeming shares of the bank holding company to be
  issued, on a share for share basis, to all shareholders of the bank in
  exchange for all the issued and outstanding shares of the bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of provision

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Shares of a bank holding company deemed to be issued
  under subsection (1) are subject to the same designation, rights,
  privileges and restrictions or conditions and, subject to any
  agreement to the contrary, to the same charges, encumbrances and other
  restrictions as the shares of the bank for which they are exchanged
  and the shares of the bank, on the issuance of the letters patent,
  become the property of the bank holding company free and clear of any
  charge, encumbrance or other restriction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of provision

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An exchange of shares of a bank referred to in
  subsection (1) under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating a bank holding company does not deprive a person who was
  a holder of shares of the bank immediately before the exchange of any
  right or privilege with respect to the shares or relieve the person of
  any liability in respect of the shares, but that right or privilege
  must be exercised in accordance with this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer and voting of shares

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3), no share of a bank holding
  company that is deemed to be issued under a provision included in the
  letters patent incorporating a bank holding company may subsequently
  be transferred or voted contrary to this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No provision described in subsection (1) may be
  included in letters patent issued under section 671 unless the
  application for the letters patent is accompanied by evidence that the
  request for the provision was approved by a special resolution of the
  shareholders of the bank at a shareholders' meeting called to consider
  the application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exchange of share certificates

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If, under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating a bank holding company, a share exchange is deemed to
  have taken place, the bank holding company shall, within ninety days
  after the issuance of the letters patent, make provision for the issue
  of share certificates representing shares of the bank holding company
  and for the exchange of those certificates for share certificates
  representing the shares of the bank that were outstanding on the
  effective date of the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 71
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal involving fundamental change

- **[[678]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  application, made in accordance with the regulations, by a bank to
  give effect to a proposal to incorporate a bank holding company as the
  holding body corporate of the bank, to continue a body corporate as a
  bank holding company of the bank or to amalgamate two or more bodies
  corporate and continue those bodies corporate as a bank holding
  company of the bank --- and to make any other fundamental change to or
  in respect of the bank, including an exchange of any or all of the
  shares of the bank for shares of the bank holding company --- , the
  Minister may, to give effect to the proposal,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include in the letters patent of the bank holding
    company issued under section 671, 684 or 809 any provision the
    Minister considers necessary; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} despite any provision of the Act specified in
    regulations made under paragraph 2(e), give any approval that the
    Minister considers necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting applications referred to in subsection
    (1), including their form and the information to be contained in
    them, and authorizing the requesting of additional information in
    respect of such applications;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting proposals to which subsection (1)
