  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A natural person authorized under subsection (1) to
  represent an entity may exercise on behalf of the entity all the
  powers the entity could exercise if it were a natural person as well
  as a shareholder.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Joint shareholders

**[[739]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-739 .sectionLabel}** Unless the by-laws
otherwise provide, if two or more persons hold shares jointly, one of
those holders present at a meeting of shareholders may in the absence of
the others vote the shares, but if two or more of those persons who are
present in person or represented by proxyholder vote, they shall vote as
one on the shares jointly held by them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting by hands or ballot

- **[[740]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-740
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise
  provide, voting at a meeting of shareholders shall take place by show
  of hands except when a ballot is demanded by either a shareholder or
  proxyholder entitled to vote at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder or proxyholder may demand a ballot
  either before or after any vote by show of hands.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic voting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1) and unless the by-laws provide
  otherwise, any vote referred to in that subsection may be held
  entirely by means of a telephonic, electronic or other communication
  facility if the bank holding company makes one available.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting while participating
  electronically

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise, any person who
  is participating in a meeting of shareholders under subsection 725(2)
  and entitled to vote at that meeting may vote by means of the
  telephonic, electronic or other communication facility that the bank
  holding company has made available for that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the manner of and conditions for voting at a meeting of
  shareholders by means of a telephonic, electronic or other
  communication facility.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 98
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-740-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 740"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution in lieu of meeting

- **[[741]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-741
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where a written statement is
  submitted by a director under section 762 or by an auditor under
  subsection 853(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a resolution in writing signed by all the
    shareholders entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of
    shareholders is as valid as if it had been passed at a meeting of
    the shareholders; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a resolution in writing dealing with all matters
    required by this Part to be dealt with at a meeting of shareholders,
    and signed by all the shareholders entitled to vote at that meeting,
    satisfies all the requirements of this Part relating to meetings of
    shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing resolution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A copy of every resolution referred to in
  subsection (1) shall be kept with the minutes of the meetings of
  shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless a ballot is demanded, an entry in the minutes
  of a meeting that the chairperson declared a resolution to be carried
  or defeated is in the absence of evidence to the contrary proof of
  that fact without proof of the number or proportion of votes recorded
  in favour of or against the resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 99
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-741-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 741"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requisitioned meeting

- **[[742]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-742
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Shareholders who together hold not
  less than 5 per cent of the issued and outstanding shares of a bank
  holding company that carry the right to vote at a meeting sought to be
  held may requisition the directors to call a meeting of shareholders
  for the purposes stated in the requisition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A requisition referred to in subsection (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} must state the business to be transacted at the
    meeting and must be sent to each director and to the head office of
    the bank holding company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may consist of several documents of like form, each
    signed by one or more shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors calling meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of a requisition referred to in subsection
  (1), the directors shall call a meeting of shareholders to transact
  the business stated in the requisition, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a record date has been fixed under paragraph
    726(5)(c) and notice of it has been given under subsection 726(7);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors have called a meeting of shareholders
    and have given notice thereof under section 727; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business of the meeting as stated in the
    requisition includes matters described in paragraphs 732(5)(b) to
    (e).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholders' power

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the directors do not call a meeting within
  twenty-one days after receiving the requisition referred to in
  subsection (1), any shareholder who signed the requisition may call
  the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A meeting called under this section shall be called
  as nearly as possible in the manner in which meetings are to be called
  pursuant to the by-laws and this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reimbursement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Unless the shareholders otherwise resolve at a
  meeting called under subsection (4), the bank holding company shall
  reimburse the shareholders for any expenses reasonably incurred by
  them in requisitioning, calling and holding the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 100
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-742-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 742"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may order meeting to be called

- **[[743]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-743 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  court may, on the application of a director, a shareholder who is
  entitled to vote at a meeting of shareholders or the Superintendent,
  order a meeting to be called, held or conducted in the manner that the
  court directs if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is impracticable to call the meeting within the
    time or in the manner in which it is to be called;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is impracticable to conduct the meeting in the
    manner required by this Part or the by-laws; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the court thinks that the meeting ought to be
    called, held or conducted within the time or in the manner that it
    directs for any other reason.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Varying quorum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without restricting the generality of subsection (1),
  a court may order that the quorum required by the by-laws or this Part
  be varied or dispensed with at a meeting called, held and conducted
  pursuant to this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Valid meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A meeting called, held and conducted pursuant to this
  section is for all purposes a meeting of shareholders of the bank
  holding company duly called, held and conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 101
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-743-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 743"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court review of election

- **[[744]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-744 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank holding company or a shareholder or director of a bank holding
  company may apply to a court to resolve any dispute in respect of the
  election or appointment of a director or an auditor of the bank
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On an application under subsection (1), a court may
  make any order it thinks fit including, without limiting the
  generality of the foregoing,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an order restraining a director or auditor whose
    election or appointment is challenged from acting pending
    determination of the dispute;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an order declaring the result of the disputed
    election or appointment;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an order requiring a new election or appointment,
    and including in the order directions for the management of the
    business and affairs of the bank holding company until a new
    election is held or the new appointment is made; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an order determining the voting rights of
    shareholders and of persons claiming to own shares.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

- **[[745]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-745 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who makes an application under subsection 743(1) or 744(1)
  shall give notice of the application to the Superintendent before the
  hearing and shall deliver a copy of the order of the court, if any, to
  the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent representation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may appear and be heard in person
  or by counsel at the hearing of an application referred to in
  subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

#### [Proxies and Voting Restrictions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-20566 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sections 156.01 to 156.09 apply

**[[746]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-746 .sectionLabel}** Sections 156.01 to
156.09 apply in respect of bank holding companies, subject to the
following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} references to "bank" in those sections are to be read
  as references to "bank holding company";

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} references to "this Part" in those sections are to be
  read as references to "this Division";

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the English version of subsection 156.05(1) is to be
  read without reference to "or auditors";

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the reference to "section 375" in subsection
  156.09(4) is to be read as a reference to "section 878";

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the reference to "subsection 138(1.1)" in subsection
  156.09(11) is to be read as a reference to "subsection 727(2)"; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the reference to "paragraph 143(1.1)(b)" in
  subparagraph (b)(vi) of the definition
  [[solicitation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 156.01 is to be read
  as a reference to "paragraph 732(1.1)(b)".

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- [2005, c. 54, s. 102](#1033265-1485873){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1033265-1485873.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-746-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 746"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Directors and Officers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-20576 .Subheading}

##### [Duties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20577 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to manage

- **[[747]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-747
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, the directors
  of a bank holding company shall manage or supervise the management of
  the business and affairs of the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Specific duties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without limiting the generality of subsection (1),
  the directors of a bank holding company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish an audit committee to perform the duties
    referred to in subsections 782(3) and (4);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish procedures to resolve conflicts of
    interest, including techniques for the identification of potential
    conflict situations and for restricting the use of confidential
    information;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} designate a committee of the board of directors to
    monitor the procedures referred to in paragraph (b); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} establish investment and lending policies,
    standards and procedures in accordance with section 927.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (2)(a) does not apply to the directors of a
  bank holding company if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all the voting shares of the bank holding company
    are beneficially owned by a Canadian financial institution described
    in any of paragraphs (a) to (d) of the definition [[financial
    institution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 2; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the audit committee of the financial institution
    performs for and on behalf of the bank holding company all the
    functions that would otherwise be required to be performed by the
    audit committee of the bank holding company under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of care

- **[[748]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-748
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every director and officer of a bank
  holding company in exercising any of the powers of a director or an
  officer and discharging any of the duties of a director or an officer
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} act honestly and in good faith with a view to the
    best interests of the bank holding company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} exercise the care, diligence and skill that a
    reasonably prudent person would exercise in comparable
    circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every director, officer and employee of a bank
  holding company shall comply with this Act, the regulations, the bank
  holding company's incorporating instrument and the by-laws of the bank
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No exculpation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No provision in any contract, in any resolution or in
  the by-laws of a bank holding company relieves any director, officer
  or employee of the bank holding company from the duty to act in
  accordance with this Act and the regulations or relieves a director,
  officer or employee from liability for a breach thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Qualification and Number --- Directors]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20604 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum number of directors

- **[[749]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-749 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank holding company shall have at least seven directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Residency requirement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} At least one half of the directors of a bank holding
  company that is a subsidiary of a foreign bank and a majority of the
  directors of any other bank holding company must be, at the time of
  each director's election or appointment, resident Canadians.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2007, c. 6, s. 114
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-749-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 749"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualified persons

**[[750]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-750 .sectionLabel}** The following persons
are disqualified from being directors of a bank holding company:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is less than eighteen years of age;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who is of unsound mind and has been so found
  by a court in Canada or elsewhere;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person who has the status of a bankrupt;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who is not a natural person;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a person who is prohibited by subsection 156.09(9) or
  section 901 or 914 from exercising voting rights attached to shares of
  the bank holding company;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an officer, director or full time
  employee of an entity that is prohibited by subsection 156.09(9) or
  section 901 or 914 from exercising voting rights attached to shares of
  the bank holding company;

- [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an officer, director, employee or
  agent of --- or any other person acting on behalf of --- an eligible
  agent within the meaning of subsection 370(1);

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2013, c. 40, s. 163\]]{.Repealed}

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a minister of Her Majesty in right of Canada or in
  right of a province; and

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an agent or employee of the
  government of a foreign country or any political subdivision thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2012, c. 19, s. 335, c. 31, s. 119
- 2013, c. 40, s. 163
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-750-20121214.html "Link to previous version of section 750"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No shareholder requirement

**[[751]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-751 .sectionLabel}** A director of a bank
holding company is not required to hold shares of the bank holding
company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on directors

**[[752]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-752 .sectionLabel}** No more than 15 per
cent of the directors of a bank holding company may, at each director's
election or appointment, be employees of the bank holding company or a
subsidiary of the bank holding company, except that up to four persons
who are employees of the bank holding company or a subsidiary of the
bank holding company may be directors of the bank holding company if
those directors constitute not more than one half of the directors of
the bank holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Election and Tenure --- Directors]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20634 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of directors

- **[[753]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-753
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 217, subsection
  749(1) and section 756, the directors of a bank holding company shall,
  by by-law, determine the number of directors or the minimum and
  maximum number of directors, but no by-law that decreases the number
  of directors shortens the term of an incumbent director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election at annual meeting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A by-law made pursuant to subsection (1) that
  provides for a minimum and maximum number of directors may provide
  that the number of directors to be elected at any annual meeting of
  the shareholders be such number as is fixed by the directors prior to
  the annual meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election or appointment as director

**[[753.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-753.1 .sectionLabel}** The election or
appointment of a person as a director is subject to the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person was present at the meeting when the
  election or appointment took place and did not refuse to hold office
  as a director; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person was not present at the meeting when the
  election or appointment took place but

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} consented in writing to hold office as a director
    before the election or appointment or within 10 days after it, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} acted as a director after the election or
    appointment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 103
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of directors

- **[[754]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-754
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where this Part or the
  by-laws of a bank holding company provide for cumulative voting, a
  bank holding company may, by by-law, provide that the directors be
  elected for terms of one, two or three years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of one, two or three years

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director elected for a term of one, two or three
  years holds office until the close of the first, second or third
  annual meeting of shareholders, as the case may be, following the
  election of the director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No stated term

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director who is not elected for an expressly stated
  term of office ceases to hold office at the close of the next annual
  meeting of shareholders following the election of the director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} It is not necessary that all directors elected at a
  meeting of shareholders hold office for the same term.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law of a bank holding company provides that
  the directors be elected for a term of two or three years, it may also
  provide that the term of office of each director be for the whole of
  that term, or that, as nearly as may be, one half of the directors
  retire each year if the term is two years, and that one third of the
  directors retire each year if the term is three years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Composition requirements

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a director of a bank holding company is elected or
  appointed for a term of more than one year, the bank holding company
  shall comply with subsection 749(2) and section 752 at each annual
  meeting of shareholders during the director's term of office as if
  that director were elected or appointed on that date.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determining election of directors

- **[[755]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-755
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where this Part or the
  by-laws of a bank holding company provide for cumulative voting, the
  persons, to the number authorized to be elected, who receive the
  greatest number of votes at an election of directors of a bank holding
  company shall be the directors thereof.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determining election of directors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at any election of directors referred to in
  subsection (1), two or more persons receive an equal number of votes
  and there are not sufficient vacancies remaining to enable all the
  persons receiving an equal number of votes to be elected, the
  directors who receive a greater number of votes or the majority of
  them shall, in order to complete the full number of directors,
  determine which of the persons so receiving an equal number of votes
  are to be elected.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cumulative voting

- **[[756]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-756
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where this Part or the by-laws
  provide for cumulative voting,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there shall be a stated number of directors fixed
    by by-law and not a minimum and maximum number of directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each shareholder entitled to vote at an election of
    directors has the right to cast a number of votes equal to the
    number of votes attached to the shares held by the shareholder
    multiplied by the number of directors to be elected, and the
    shareholder may cast all such votes in favour of one candidate or
    distribute them among the candidates in any manner;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a separate vote of shareholders shall be taken with
    respect to each candidate nominated for director unless a resolution
    is passed unanimously permitting two or more persons to be elected
    by a single vote;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a shareholder has voted for more than one
    candidate without specifying the distribution of the votes among the
    candidates, the shareholder is deemed to have distributed the votes
    equally among the candidates for whom the shareholder voted;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if the number of candidates nominated for director
    exceeds the number of positions to be filled, the candidates who
    receive the least number of votes shall be eliminated until the
    number of candidates remaining equals the number of positions to be
    filled;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} each director ceases to hold office at the close of
    the next annual meeting of shareholders following the director's
    election;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a director may be removed from office only if the
    number of votes cast in favour of a motion to remove the director is
    greater than the product of the number of directors required by the
    by-laws and the number of votes cast against the motion; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the number of directors required by the by-laws may
    be decreased only if the number of votes cast in favour of a motion
    to decrease the number of directors is greater than the product of
    the number of directors required by the by-laws and the number of
    votes cast against the motion.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory cumulative voting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the aggregate of the voting shares beneficially
  owned by a person and any entities controlled by the person carries
  more than 10 per cent of the voting rights attached to all the
  outstanding voting shares of a bank holding company, the directors
  shall be elected by cumulative voting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply if all the voting
  shares of the bank holding company that are outstanding are
  beneficially owned by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} one person and one or more entities controlled by
    that person; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} one or more entities controlled by the same person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply to a widely held bank
  holding company with equity of twelve billion dollars or more or to a
  widely held bank holding company that controls a bank to which
  subsection 378(1) applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional election

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where this Part or the by-laws of a bank holding
  company provide for cumulative voting, the shareholders of the bank
  holding company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the first annual meeting of shareholders held
    not earlier than ninety days following the date that cumulative
    voting is required under subsection (2) or provided for in the
    by-laws, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at each succeeding annual meeting,

  elect the stated number of directors to hold office until the close of
  the next annual meeting of shareholders following their election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this Part precludes the holders of any
  class or series of shares of a bank holding company from having an
  exclusive right to elect one or more directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 104
- 2007, c. 6, s. 132
- 2012, c. 5, s. 79
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-756-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 756"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Re-election of directors

**[[757]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-757 .sectionLabel}** A director who has
completed a term of office is, if otherwise qualified, eligible for
re-election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Incomplete Elections and Director Vacancies]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20705 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Void election or appointment

- **[[758]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-758 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If,
  immediately after the time of any purported election or appointment of
  directors, the board of directors would fail to comply with subsection
  749(2) or section 752, the purported election or appointment of all
  persons purported to be elected or appointed at that time is void
  unless the directors, within forty-five days after the discovery of
  the non-compliance, develop a plan, approved by the Superintendent, to
  rectify the non-compliance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to elect minimum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where, at the close of a meeting of shareholders of a
  bank holding company, the shareholders have failed to elect the number
  or minimum number of directors required by this Part or the by-laws of
  a bank holding company, the purported election of directors at the
  meeting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is valid if the directors purported to be elected
    and those incumbent directors, if any, whose terms did not expire at
    the close of the meeting, together constitute a quorum; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is void if the directors purported to be elected
    and those incumbent directors, if any, whose terms did not expire at
    the close of the meeting, together do not constitute a quorum.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors where elections incomplete or
void

- **[[759]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-759
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding subsections 754(2)
  and (3) and paragraphs 756(1)(f) and 760(1)(a), where subsection
  758(1) or (2) applies at the close of any meeting of shareholders of a
  bank holding company, the board of directors shall, until their
  successors are elected or appointed, consist solely of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where paragraph 758(2)(a) applies, the directors
    referred to in that paragraph; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where subsection 758(1) or paragraph 758(2)(b)
    applies, the persons who were the incumbent directors immediately
    before the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where there is no approved
  rectification plan

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding subsections 754(2) and (3) and
  paragraphs 756(1)(f) and 760(1)(a), where a plan to rectify the
  non-compliance referred to in subsection 758(1) has not been approved
  by the Superintendent by the end of the forty-five day period referred
  to in that subsection, the board of directors shall, until their
  successors are elected or appointed, consist solely of the persons who
  were the incumbent directors immediately before the meeting at which
  the purported election or appointment referred to in that subsection
  occurred.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors to call meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where subsection (1) or (2) applies, the board of
  directors referred to in that subsection shall without delay call a
  special meeting of shareholders to fill the vacancies, where paragraph
  758(2)(a) applies, or elect a new board of directors, where subsection
  758(1) or paragraph 758(2)(b) applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder may call meeting

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where the directors fail to call a special meeting
  required by subsection (3), the meeting may be called by any
  shareholder.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ceasing to hold office

- **[[760]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-760 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director ceases to hold office

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the close of the annual meeting at which the
    director's term of office expires;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the director dies or resigns;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when the director becomes disqualified under
    section 750 or ineligible to hold office pursuant to subsection
    790(2);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} when the director is removed under section 761; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} when the director is removed from office under
    section 963 or 964.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Date of resignation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The resignation of a director of a bank holding
  company becomes effective at the time a written resignation is sent to
  the bank holding company by the director or at the time specified in
  the resignation, whichever is later.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of director

- **[[761]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-761
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraph 756(1)(g), the
  shareholders of a bank holding company may by resolution at a special
  meeting remove any director or all the directors from office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the holders of any class or series of shares of
  a bank holding company have the exclusive right to elect one or more
  directors, a director so elected may be removed only by a resolution
  at a meeting of the shareholders of that class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vacancy by removal

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraphs 756(1)(b) to (e), a vacancy
  created by the removal of a director may be filled at the meeting of
  the shareholders at which the director is removed or, if not so
  filled, may be filled under section 765 or 766.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of director

- **[[762]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-762 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} resigns,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns of a meeting
    of shareholders called for the purpose of removing the director from
    office, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns of a meeting
    of directors or shareholders at which another person is to be
    appointed or elected to fill the office of director, whether because
    of the director's resignation or removal or because the director's
    term of office has expired or is about to expire,

  is entitled to submit to the bank holding company a written statement
  giving the reasons for the resignation or the reasons why the director
  opposes any proposed action or resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement re disagreement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a director resigns as a result of a
  disagreement with the other directors or the officers of a bank
  holding company, the director shall submit to the bank holding company
  and the Superintendent a written statement setting out the nature of
  the disagreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circulation of statement

- **[[763]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-763 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank holding company shall without delay on receipt of a director's
  statement referred to in subsection 762(1) relating to a matter
  referred to in paragraph 762(1)(b) or (c), or a director's statement
  referred to in subsection 762(2), send a copy of it to each
  shareholder entitled to receive a notice of meetings and to the
  Superintendent, unless the statement is attached to a notice of a
  meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Immunity for statement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No bank holding company or person acting on its
  behalf incurs any liability by reason only of circulating a director's
  statement in compliance with subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholders filling vacancy

**[[764]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-764 .sectionLabel}** The by-laws of a bank
holding company may provide that a vacancy among the directors is to be
filled only

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} by a vote of the shareholders; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a vote of the holders of any class or series of
  shares having an exclusive right to elect one or more directors if the
  vacancy occurs among the directors elected by the holders of that
  class or series.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors filling vacancy

- **[[765]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-765
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 772 but subject to
  subsection (2) and sections 764 and 766, a quorum of directors may
  fill a vacancy among the directors except a vacancy resulting from a
  change in the by-laws by which the number or the minimum or maximum
  number of directors is increased or from a failure to elect the number
  or minimum number of directors provided for in the by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where composition fails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding sections 764 and 772, where by reason
  of a vacancy the number of directors or the composition of the board
  of directors fails to meet any of the requirements of section 749 or
  section 752, the directors who, in the absence of any by-law, would be
  empowered to fill that vacancy shall do so forthwith.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 105
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-765-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 765"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vacancy

**[[766]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-766 .sectionLabel}** Notwithstanding section
772, where the holders of any class or series of shares of a bank
holding company have an exclusive right to elect one or more directors
and a vacancy occurs among those directors, then, subject to section
764,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the remaining directors elected by the holders of
  that class or series of shares may fill the vacancy except one
  resulting from an increase in the number or the minimum or maximum
  number of directors for that class or series or from a failure to
  elect the number or minimum number of directors provided for in the
  by-laws for that class or series;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if there are no such remaining directors and, by
  reason of the vacancy, the number of directors or the composition of
  the board of directors fails to meet any of the requirements of
  section 749 or section 752, the other directors may fill that vacancy;
  and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if there are no such remaining directors and
  paragraph (b) does not apply, any holder of shares of that class or
  series may call a meeting of the holders thereof for the purpose of
  filling the vacancy.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 106
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-766-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 766"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unexpired term

**[[767]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-767 .sectionLabel}** Unless the by-laws
otherwise provide, a director elected or appointed to fill a vacancy
holds office for the unexpired term of the director's predecessor in
office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional directors

- **[[768]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-768 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a bank holding company may appoint one or more additional
  directors where the by-laws of the bank holding company allow them to
  do so and the by-laws determine the minimum and maximum numbers of
  directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of office

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director appointed under subsection (1) holds
  office for a term expiring not later than the close of the next annual
  meeting of shareholders of the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on number appointed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The total number of directors appointed under
  subsection (1) may not exceed one third of the number of directors
  elected at the previous annual meeting of shareholders of the bank
  holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Meetings of the Board]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20800 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meetings required

- **[[769]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-769 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors shall meet at least four times during each financial year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place for meetings

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors may meet at any place unless the
  by-laws provide otherwise.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice for meetings

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The notice for the meetings must be given as required
  by the by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of meeting

- **[[770]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-770 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  notice of a meeting of directors shall specify each matter referred to
  in section 785 that is to be dealt with at the meeting but, unless the
  by-laws otherwise provide, need not otherwise specify the purpose of
  or the business to be transacted at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver of notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director may in any manner waive notice of a
  meeting of directors and the attendance of a director at a meeting of
  directors is a waiver of notice of that meeting except where the
  director attends the meeting for the express purpose of objecting to
  the transaction of any business on the grounds that the meeting is not
  lawfully called.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjourned meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notice of an adjourned meeting of directors is not
  required to be given if the time and place of the adjourned meeting
  were announced at the original meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum

- **[[771]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-771
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 772, the number
  of directors referred to in subsection (2) constitutes a quorum at any
  meeting of directors or a committee of directors and, notwithstanding
  any vacancy among the directors, a quorum of directors may exercise
  all the powers of the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The number of directors constituting a quorum at any
  meeting of directors or a committee of directors shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a majority of the minimum number of directors
    required by this Part for the board of directors or a committee of
    directors; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} such greater number of directors than the number
    calculated pursuant to paragraph (a) as may be established by the
    by-laws of the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director continues to be present

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director who is present at a meeting of directors
  or of a committee of directors but is not, in accordance with
  subsection 790(1), present at any particular time during the meeting
  is considered to be present for the purposes of this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 107
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-771-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 771"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resident Canadian majority

- **[[772]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-772 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a bank holding company shall not transact business at a
  meeting of directors unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a bank holding company that is a
    subsidiary of a foreign bank, at least one half of the directors
    present are resident Canadians; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, a majority of the directors
    present are resident Canadians.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the directors of a bank
  holding company may transact business at a meeting of directors
  without the required proportion of directors who are resident
  Canadians if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a director who is a resident Canadian unable to be
    present approves, in writing or by telephonic, electronic or other
    communications facilities, the business transacted at the meeting;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there would have been present the required
    proportion of directors who are resident Canadians had that director
    been present at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2013, c. 33, s. 106
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-772-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 772"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic meeting

- **[[773]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-773
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the by-laws of a bank
  holding company, a meeting of directors or of a committee of directors
  may be held by means of such telephonic, electronic or other
  communications facilities as permit all persons participating in the
  meeting to communicate adequately with each other during the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed present

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director participating in a meeting by any means
  referred to in subsection (1) is deemed for the purposes of this Part
  to be present at that meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution outside board meeting

- **[[774]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-774 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  resolution in writing signed by all the directors entitled to vote on
  that resolution at a meeting of directors is as valid as if it had
  been passed at a meeting of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing directors' resolution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the resolution referred to in
  subsection (1) shall be kept with the minutes of the proceedings of
  the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution outside committee meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A resolution in writing signed by all the directors
  entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of a committee of
  directors, other than a resolution of the audit committee in carrying
  out its duties under subsection 782(3), is as valid as if it had been
  passed at a meeting of that committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing committee resolution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the resolution referred to in
  subsection (3) shall be kept with the minutes of the proceedings of
  that committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Unless a ballot is demanded, an entry in the minutes
  of a meeting that the chairperson declared a resolution to be carried
  or defeated is in the absence of evidence to the contrary proof of
  that fact without proof of the number or proportion of votes recorded
  in favour of or against the resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 108
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-774-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 774"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissent of director

- **[[775]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-775 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director of a bank holding company who is present at a meeting of
  directors or a committee of directors is deemed to have consented to
  any resolution passed or action taken at that meeting unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director requests that the director's dissent
    be entered or the director's dissent is entered in the minutes of
    the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the director sends a written dissent to the
    secretary of the meeting before the meeting is adjourned; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the director sends the director's dissent by
    registered mail or delivers it to the head office of the bank
    holding company immediately after the meeting is adjourned.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loss of right to dissent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director of a bank holding company who votes for or
  consents to a resolution is not entitled to dissent under subsection
  (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissent of absent director

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director of a bank holding company who is not
  present at a meeting at which a resolution is passed or action taken
  is deemed to have consented thereto unless, within seven days after
  the director becomes aware of the resolution, the director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} causes the director's dissent to be placed with the
    minutes of the meeting; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sends the director's dissent by registered mail or
    delivers it to the head office of the bank holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record of attendance

- **[[776]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-776 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank holding company shall keep a record of the attendance at each
  meeting of directors and each committee meeting of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement to shareholders

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company shall attach to the notice of
  each annual meeting it sends to its shareholders a statement showing,
  in respect of the financial year immediately preceding the meeting,
  the total number of directors' meetings and directors' committee
  meetings held during the financial year and the number of those
  meetings attended by each director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meeting required by Superintendent

- **[[777]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-777
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where in the opinion of the
  Superintendent it is necessary, the Superintendent may, by notice in
  writing, require a bank holding company to hold a meeting of directors
  of the bank holding company to consider the matters set out in the
  notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance of Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may attend and be heard at a
  meeting referred to in subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [By-laws]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20889 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws

- **[[778]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-778
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless this Part otherwise provides,
  the directors of a bank holding company may by resolution make, amend
  or repeal any by-law that regulates the business or affairs of the
  bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors shall submit a by-law, or an amendment
  to or a repeal of a by-law, that is made under subsection (1) to the
  shareholders at the next meeting of shareholders, and the shareholders
  may, by resolution, confirm or amend the by-law, amendment or repeal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless this Part otherwise provides, a by-law, or an
  amendment to or a repeal of a by-law, is effective from the date of
  the resolution of the directors under subsection (1) until it is
  confirmed, confirmed as amended or rejected by the shareholders under
  subsection (2) or until it ceases to be effective under subsection (4)
  and, where the by-law is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, it
  continues in effect in the form in which it was so confirmed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect where no shareholder approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law, or an amendment to or a repeal of a
  by-law, is rejected by the shareholders, or is not submitted to the
  shareholders by the directors as required under subsection (2), the
  by-law, amendment or repeal ceases to be effective from the date of
  its rejection or the date of the next meeting of shareholders, as the
  case may be, and no subsequent resolution of the directors to make,
  amend or repeal a by-law having substantially the same purpose or
  effect is effective until it is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, by
  the shareholders.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder proposal of by-law

**[[779]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-779 .sectionLabel}** A shareholder entitled
to vote at an annual meeting of shareholders may, in accordance with
sections 732 and 733, make a proposal to make, amend or repeal a by-law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed by-laws

- **[[780]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-780 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  matter that, immediately prior to the day a body corporate is
  continued as a bank holding company, was provided for in the
  incorporating instrument of the body corporate, and that, under this
  Part, would be provided for in the by-laws of a bank holding company,
  is deemed to be provided for in the by-laws of the bank holding
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law prevails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a by-law of the bank holding company made in
  accordance with sections 778 and 779 amends or repeals any matter
  referred to in subsection (1), the by-law prevails.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Committees of the Board]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20912 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committees

**[[781]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-781 .sectionLabel}** The directors of a bank
holding company may appoint from their number, in addition to the
committees referred to in subsection 747(2), such other committees as
they deem necessary and, subject to section 785, delegate to those
committees such powers of the directors, and assign to those committees
such duties, as the directors consider appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Audit committee

- **[[782]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-782 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  audit committee of a bank holding company shall consist of at least
  three directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Membership

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} None of the members of the audit committee may be
  officers or employees of the bank holding company or any of its
  subsidiaries.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of audit committee

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The audit committee of a bank holding company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} review the annual statement of the bank holding
    company before the annual statement is approved by the directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review such returns of the bank holding company as
    the Superintendent may specify;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the bank holding company
    to implement and maintain appropriate internal control procedures;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} review, evaluate and approve those procedures;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} review such investments and transactions that could
    adversely affect the well-being of the bank holding company as the
    auditor or any officer of the bank holding company may bring to the
    attention of the committee;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} meet with the auditor to discuss the annual
    statement and the returns and transactions referred to in this
    subsection; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} meet with the chief internal auditor of the bank
    holding company, or the officer or employee of the bank holding
    company acting in a similar capacity, and with management of the
    bank holding company, to discuss the effectiveness of the internal
    control procedures established for the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of the annual statement and returns of a
  bank holding company that under this Part must be approved by the
  directors of the bank holding company, the audit committee of the bank
  holding company shall report thereon to the directors before the
  approval is given.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required meeting of directors

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The audit committee of a bank holding company may
  call a meeting of the directors of the bank holding company to
  consider any matter of concern to the committee.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Directors and Officers --- Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20937 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief executive officer

**[[783]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-783 .sectionLabel}** The directors of a bank
holding company shall appoint from their number a chief executive
officer who must be ordinarily resident in Canada and, subject to
section 785, may delegate to that officer any of the powers of the
directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of officers

- **[[784]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-784 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a bank holding company may, subject to the by-laws,
  designate the offices of the bank holding company, appoint officers
  thereto, specify the duties of those officers and delegate to them
  powers, subject to section 785, to manage the business and affairs of
  the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors as officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 752, a director of a bank holding
  company may be appointed to any office of the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Two or more offices

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Two or more offices of a bank holding company may be
  held by the same person.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limits on power to delegate

**[[785]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-785 .sectionLabel}** The directors of a bank
holding company may not delegate any of the following powers, namely,
the power to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the shareholders a question or matter
  requiring the approval of the shareholders;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} fill a vacancy among the directors, on a committee of
  directors or in the office of auditor or appoint additional directors;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} issue or cause to be issued securities, including an
  issue of shares of a series that is authorized in accordance with
  section 706, except in accordance with any authorization made by the
  directors;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} declare a dividend;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} authorize the redemption or other acquisition by the
  bank holding company pursuant to section 715 of shares issued by the
  bank holding company;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} authorize the payment of a commission on a share
  issue;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} approve a management proxy circular;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} except as provided in this Part, approve the annual
  statement of the bank holding company and any other financial
  statements issued by the bank holding company; or

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} adopt, amend or repeal by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 109
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-785-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 785"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration of directors, officers and
employees

- **[[786]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-786
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this section and the
  by-laws, the directors of a bank holding company may fix the
  remuneration of the directors, officers and employees of the bank
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law required

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No remuneration shall be paid to a director as
  director until a by-law fixing the aggregate of all amounts that may
  be paid to all directors in respect of directors' remuneration during
  a fixed period of time has been confirmed by special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

- **[[787]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-787 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  act of a director or an officer of a bank holding company is valid
  notwithstanding a defect in the director's qualification or an
  irregularity in the director's election or in the appointment of the
  director or officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An act of the board of directors of a bank holding
  company is valid notwithstanding a defect in the composition of the
  board or an irregularity in the election of the board or in the
  appointment of a member of the board.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to attend meetings

**[[788]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-788 .sectionLabel}** A director of a bank
holding company is entitled to attend and to be heard at every meeting
of shareholders.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

##### [Conflicts of Interest]{.HTitleText4} {#h-20982 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure of interest

- **[[789]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-789 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director or officer of a bank holding company shall disclose to the
  bank holding company, in writing or by requesting to have it entered
  in the minutes of a meeting of directors or a meeting of a committee
  of directors, the nature and extent of any interest they have in a
  material contract or material transaction with the bank holding
  company, whether entered into or proposed, if they

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are a party to the contract or transaction;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are a director or officer of a party to the
    contract or transaction or a person acting in a similar capacity; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} have a material interest in a party to the contract
    or transaction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- director

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure shall be made in the case of a
  director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the meeting of directors, or of a committee of
    directors, at which the proposed contract or transaction is first
    considered;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if at the time of the meeting referred to in
    paragraph (a) the director was not interested in the proposed
    contract or transaction, at the first one after they become
    interested in it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the director becomes interested after a contract
    or transaction is entered into, at the first one after they become
    interested; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a person who is interested in a contract or
    transaction becomes a director, at the first one after they become a
    director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure required by subsection (1) shall be
  made in the case of an officer who is not a director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately after they become aware that the
    contract, transaction, proposed contract or proposed transaction is
    to be considered or has been considered at a meeting of directors or
    of a committee of directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if they become interested after the contract or
    transaction is entered into, immediately after they become
    interested; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if a person who is interested in a contract or
    transaction becomes an officer, immediately after they become an
    officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- contract not
  requiring approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the material contract or material transaction,
  whether entered into or proposed, is one that in the ordinary course
  of the bank holding company's business would not require approval by
  the directors or shareholders, the director or officer shall disclose
  to the bank holding company, in writing or by requesting to have it
  entered in the minutes of a meeting of directors or of a committee of
  directors, the nature and extent of their interest immediately after
  they become aware of the contract or transaction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 110
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-789-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 789"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director to abstain

- **[[790]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-790 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who is required to make a disclosure under subsection 789(1)
  shall not be present at any meeting of directors, or of a committee of
  directors, while the contract or transaction is being considered or
  vote on any resolution to approve it unless the contract or
  transaction

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} relates primarily to their remuneration as a
    director, officer, employee or agent of the bank holding company, an
    entity controlled by the bank holding company or an entity in which
    the bank holding company has a substantial investment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is for indemnity under section 799 or insurance
    under section 800; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is with an affiliate of the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any director who knowingly contravenes subsection (1)
  ceases to hold office as director and is not eligible, for a period of
  five years after the date on which the contravention occurred, for
  election or appointment as a director of any bank holding company, any
  insurance holding company or any financial institution that is
  incorporated or formed by or under an Act of Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An act of the board of directors of a bank holding
  company, or of a committee of the board of directors, is not invalid
  because a person acting as a director had ceased under subsection (2)
  to hold office as a director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 111
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-790-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 790"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}General notice

- **[[791]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-791 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purposes of subsection 789(1), a general notice to the directors
  declaring that a director or officer is to be regarded as interested
  for any of the following reasons in a contract or transaction entered
  into with a party is a sufficient declaration of interest in relation
  to any contract or transaction with that party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer is a director or officer of
    a party referred to in paragraph 789(1)(b) or (c) or a person acting
    in a similar capacity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer has a material interest in
    the party; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} there has been a material change in the nature of
    the director's or officer's interest in the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to disclosures

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The shareholders of the bank holding company may
  examine the portions of any minutes of meetings of directors or
  committees of directors that contain disclosures under subsection
  789(1), or the portions of any other documents that contain those
  disclosures, during the usual business hours of the bank holding
  company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 112
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-791-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 791"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Avoidance standards

- **[[792]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-792 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  contract or transaction for which disclosure is required under
  subsection 789(1) is not invalid and a director or officer is not
  accountable to the bank holding company or its shareholders for any
  profit realized from it by reason only of the director's or officer's
  interest in the contract or transaction or the fact that the director
  was present or was counted to determine whether a quorum existed at
  the meeting of directors, or of a committee of directors, that
  considered it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer disclosed their interest in
    accordance with section 789 and subsection 791(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors approved the contract or transaction;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction was reasonable and fair
    to the bank holding company at the time that it was approved.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation by shareholders

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Even if the conditions set out in subsection (1) are
  not met, a director or officer acting honestly and in good faith is
  not accountable to the bank holding company or its shareholders for
  any profit realized from a contract or transaction for which
  disclosure was required and the contract or transaction is not invalid
  by reason only of the director's or officer's interest in it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction is approved or
    confirmed by special resolution at a meeting of shareholders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} disclosure of the interest was made to the
    shareholders in a manner sufficient to indicate its nature before
    the contract or transaction was approved or confirmed; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction was reasonable and fair
    to the bank holding company at the time that it was approved or
    confirmed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 112
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-792-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 792"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may set aside or require accounting

**[[793]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-793 .sectionLabel}** If a director or
officer of a bank holding company fails to comply with any of sections
789 to 792, a court, on application of the bank holding company or any
of its shareholders, may set aside the contract or transaction on any
terms that the court thinks fit and may require the director or officer
to account to the bank holding company for any profit or gain realized
on it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 112
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-793-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 793"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Liability, Exculpation and Indemnification]{.HTitleText4} {#h-21043 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director liability

- **[[794]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-794
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Directors of a bank holding company
  who vote for or consent to a resolution of the directors authorizing
  the issue of a share contrary to subsection 709(1) or the issue of
  subordinated indebtedness contrary to section 723 for a consideration
  other than money are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable to
  the bank holding company to make good any amount by which the
  consideration received is less than the fair equivalent of the money
  that the bank holding company would have received if the share or
  subordinated indebtedness had been issued for money on the date of the
  resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Further liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Directors of a bank holding company who vote for or
  consent to a resolution of the directors authorizing any of the
  following are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable to restore
  to the bank holding company any amounts so distributed or paid and not
  otherwise recovered by the bank holding company and any amounts in
  relation to any loss suffered by the bank holding company:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a redemption or purchase of shares contrary to
    section 715;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a reduction of capital contrary to section 718;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a payment of a dividend contrary to section 722; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a payment of an indemnity contrary to section 799.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 113(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-794-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 794"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution

- **[[795]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-795 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who has satisfied a judgment in relation to the director's
  liability under section 794 is entitled to contribution from the other
  directors who voted for or consented to the unlawful act on which the
  judgment was founded.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director who is liable under section 794 is
  entitled to apply to a court for an order compelling a shareholder or
  other person to pay or deliver to the director any money or property
  that was paid or distributed to the shareholder or other person
  contrary to section 715, 718, 722 or 799.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court order

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an application is made to a court under
  subsection (2), the court may, where it is satisfied that it is
  equitable to do so,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} order a shareholder or other person to pay or
    deliver to a director any money or property that was paid or
    distributed to the shareholder or other person contrary to section
    715, 718, 722 or 799;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} order a bank holding company to return or issue
    shares to a person from whom the bank holding company has purchased,
    redeemed or otherwise acquired shares; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make any further order it thinks fit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

**[[796]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-796 .sectionLabel}** An action to enforce a
liability imposed by section 794 may not be commenced after two years
from the date of the resolution authorizing the action complained of.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors liable for wages

- **[[797]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-797
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  the directors of a bank holding company are jointly and severally, or
  solidarily, liable to each employee of the bank holding company for
  all debts not exceeding six months wages payable to the employee for
  services performed for the bank holding company while they are
  directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions precedent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director is not liable under subsection (1) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the bank holding company has been sued for the debt
    within six months after it has become due and execution has been
    returned unsatisfied in whole or in part;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the bank holding company has commenced liquidation
    and dissolution proceedings or has been dissolved and a claim for
    the debt has been proven within six months after the earlier of the
    date of commencement of the liquidation and dissolution proceedings
    and the date of dissolution; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the bank holding company has made an assignment or
    a bankruptcy order has been made against it under the [Bankruptcy
    and Insolvency Act](/eng/acts/B-3) and a claim for the debt has been
    proved within six months after the assignment or bankruptcy order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director is not liable under subsection (1) unless
  the director is sued for a debt referred to in that subsection while a
  director or within two years after the director has ceased to be a
  director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amount due after execution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where execution referred to in paragraph (2)(a) has
  issued, the amount recoverable from a director is the amount remaining
  unsatisfied after execution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subrogation of director

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a director of a bank holding company pays a
  debt referred to in subsection (1) that is proven in liquidation and
  dissolution or bankruptcy proceedings, the director is entitled to any
  preference that the employee would have been entitled to and, where a
  judgment has been obtained, the director is entitled to an assignment
  of the judgment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution entitlement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A director of a bank holding company who has
  satisfied a claim under this section is entitled to a contribution
  from the other directors of the bank holding company who are liable
  for the claim.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2004, c. 25, s. 186
- 2005, c. 54, s. 114(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-797-20041215.html "Link to previous version of section 797"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Defence --- due diligence

- **[[798]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-798 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director, officer or employee of a bank holding company is not liable
  under section 794 or 797 and has fulfilled their duty under subsection
  748(2) if they exercised the care, diligence and skill that a
  reasonably prudent person would have exercised in comparable
  circumstances, including reliance in good faith on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the bank holding company
    that were represented to them by an officer of the bank holding
    company or in a written report of the auditor of the bank holding
    company fairly to reflect the financial condition of the bank
    holding company; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report of a person whose profession lends
    credibility to a statement made by them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Defence --- good faith

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director or officer of a bank holding company has
  fulfilled their duty under subsection 748(1) if they relied in good
  faith on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the bank holding company
    that were represented to them by an officer of the bank holding
    company or in a written report of the auditor of the bank holding
    company fairly to reflect the financial condition of the bank
    holding company; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report of a person whose profession lends
    credibility to a statement made by them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 115
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-798-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 798"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Indemnification

- **[[799]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-799 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  bank holding company may indemnify a director or officer of the bank
  holding company, a former director or officer of the bank holding
  company or another person who acts or acted, at the bank holding
  company's request, as a director or officer of or in a similar
  capacity for another entity against all costs, charges and expenses,
  including an amount paid to settle an action or satisfy a judgment,
  reasonably incurred by them in respect of any civil, criminal,
  administrative, investigative or other proceeding in which they are
  involved because of that association with the bank holding company or
  other entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advances

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company may advance amounts to the
  director, officer or other person for the costs, charges and expenses
  of a proceeding referred to in subsection (1). They shall repay the
  amounts if they do not fulfil the conditions set out in subsection
  (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No indemnification

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company may not indemnify a person
  under subsection (1) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person acted honestly and in good faith with a
    view to the best interests of, as the case may be, the bank holding
    company or the other entity for which they acted at the bank holding
    company's request as a director or officer or in a similar capacity;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a criminal or administrative action
    or proceeding that is enforced by a monetary penalty, the person had
    reasonable grounds for believing that their conduct was lawful.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Indemnification --- derivative actions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company may with the approval of a
  court indemnify a person referred to in subsection (1) or advance
  amounts to them under subsection (2) --- in respect of an action by or
  on behalf of the bank holding company or other entity to procure a
  judgment in its favour to which the person is made a party because of
  the association referred to in subsection (1) with the bank holding
  company or other entity --- against all costs, charges and expenses
  reasonably incurred by them in connection with that action if they
  fulfil the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to indemnity

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person referred to in that
  subsection is entitled to be indemnified by the bank holding company
  in respect of all costs, charges and expenses reasonably incurred by
  them in connection with the defence of any civil, criminal,
  administrative, investigative or other proceeding to which the person
  is subject because of the association referred to in subsection (1)
  with the bank holding company or other entity described in that
  subsection if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was not judged by the court or other competent
    authority to have committed any fault or omitted to do anything that
    they ought to have done; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fulfils the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Heirs and personal representatives

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A bank holding company may, to the extent referred to
  in subsections (1) to (5) in respect of the person, indemnify the
