- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation, suspension or amendment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} At the request of the person concerned, the Minister
  or the Superintendent, as the case may be, may revoke, suspend or
  amend any terms or conditions imposed by him or her and may revoke or
  suspend an undertaking given to him or her or approve its amendment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 125
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Multiple approval --- other approvals

**[[973.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-973.05 .sectionLabel}** The Minister or
the Superintendent may grant more than one approval, other than letters
patent, in a single instrument if he or she considers it appropriate to
do so, and if the Minister or Superintendent does so, he or she may
specify different effective dates for each of the approvals.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 125
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption in relation to notices of
intention

**[[973.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-973.06 .sectionLabel}** The
Superintendent may, on application, exempt an applicant or applicants
from the provisions of this Act respecting the publication of a notice
of intention in respect of applications for approvals and impose any
terms and conditions respecting the publication of the notice of
intention that he or she considers appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 125
:::

### [Exceptions to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23132 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calculations --- generally accepted
accounting principles

- **[[973.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-973.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, as a result of a change to the
  accounting principles referred to in subsections 308(4) and 840(4) ---
  whether the change is made before or after this section comes into
  force --- the Superintendent considers, given any prudential
  considerations that he or she considers relevant, that any amount,
  calculation or valuation under this Act or the regulations is not
  appropriate, the Superintendent may specify the amount that is to be
  used or the calculation or valuation that is to be performed instead.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}[Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall cause a notice of the
  specification to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) within 60 days after the day on
  which the specification has effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Five-year limit

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The specification ceases to have effect on the day
  indicated in the notice, which may be no later than five years after
  the day on which the specification is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2012, c. 5, s. 102
:::

### [Short-term Exemption Order]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23142 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Short-term exemption order

- **[[973.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-973.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite sections 378.1 and 378.2,
  paragraph 522.32(2)(b), subsection 522.32(4), paragraphs 522.32(7)(c)
  and (d) and sections 524.1, 524.2, 885 and 886, the Minister may, by
  order, provide that any of those provisions do not apply in respect of
  a person specified in the order for a period of up to twelve months,
  subject to any terms and conditions that the Minister considers
  appropriate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If section 516 or 517 applies in respect of a foreign
  bank or an entity associated with a foreign bank, the Minister may
  only make an order under subsection (1) to the extent that the
  aggregate of the period that applied under that section and the period
  specified in the order under subsection (1) does not exceed twelve
  months.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

### [Orders to Exempt or Adapt]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23150 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order

- **[[973.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-973.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On the recommendation of the
  Minister, the Governor in Council may, by order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide that any provision of this Act or the
    regulations shall not apply to a bank, to Her Majesty in right of
    Canada or an agent or agency of Her Majesty or to any other person
    otherwise subject to the provision; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide that any provision of this Act or the
    regulations applies to a bank, to Her Majesty in right of Canada or
    Her Majesty's agent or agency or to any other person subject to the
    provision only in the manner and to the extent provided for in the
    order, and adapt the provision for the purposes of that application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister's recommendation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may make a recommendation under
  subsection (1) only if the Minister

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is of the opinion that the order would relate to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the acquisition, holding, sale or other
      disposition of, or other dealing with, shares of a bank by, or the
      transfer or issue of shares of a bank to, Her Majesty in right of
      Canada or Her Majesty's agent or agency, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the management of the business and affairs or
      the regulation and supervision of a bank during the time that Her
      Majesty or Her Majesty's agent or agency is acquiring, holding,
      selling or otherwise disposing of, or otherwise dealing with,
      shares of the bank, or during the time that shares of the bank are
      transferred or issued to Her Majesty or Her Majesty's agent or
      agency; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is of the opinion --- after considering measures
    other than an order under that subsection and after consulting with
    the Superintendent, the Governor of the Bank of Canada and the Chief
    Executive Officer of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation ---
    that the order will promote the stability of the financial system in
    Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms and conditions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the recommendation of the Minister, the Governor
  in Council may, by order, impose any terms and conditions relating to
  the acquisition of shares of a bank by, or transfer or issue of shares
  of a bank to, Her Majesty in right of Canada or Her Majesty's agent or
  agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Repeal of order under subsection (1)

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may recommend the repeal of an order
  made under subsection (1) without regard to subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms, conditions and undertakings

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} From the time that Her Majesty in right of Canada or
  an agent or agency of Her Majesty acquires shares of a bank to the
  time that the shares are sold or otherwise disposed of, the Minister
  may, by order, impose any terms and conditions on --- or require any
  undertaking from --- the bank that the Minister considers appropriate,
  including any terms and conditions or undertakings relating to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the remuneration of the bank's senior officers, as
    defined in section 646.1, and directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the appointment or removal of the bank's senior
    officers, as defined in section 646.1, and directors;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the payment of dividends by the bank; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the bank's lending policies and practices.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Acquisition

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Despite Part X of the [Financial Administration
  Act](/eng/acts/F-11), the Minister or an agent or agency of Her
  Majesty in right of Canada may, on any terms and conditions imposed
  under subsection (3), acquire and hold shares of a bank on behalf of
  or in trust for Her Majesty if, as a result of an order under
  subsection (1), the bank may record in its securities register or
  members register, as the case may be, the transfer or issue of shares
  to Her Majesty or an agent or agency of Her Majesty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment out of C.R.F.

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} On the requisition of the Minister, there may be paid
  out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund the amount that the Minister or
  an agent or agency of Her Majesty in right of Canada is required to
  pay for the acquisition of shares under subsection (6) and any costs
  and expenses incurred in connection with the acquisition, holding,
  sale or other disposition of, or other dealing with, the shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration of shares

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Shares acquired under subsection (6) by the Minister
  or an agent or agency of Her Majesty in right of Canada are to be
  registered in the name of the Minister, agent or agency, as the case
  may be, in the bank's securities register or members register, as the
  case may be, if they are capable of being registered in it, and they
  are to be held by the Minister, agent or agency, as the case may be,
  on behalf of or in trust for Her Majesty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition by Minister

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, at any time, sell or otherwise
  dispose of shares acquired under subsection (6). The [Surplus Crown
  Assets Act](/eng/acts/S-27) and section 61 of the [Financial
  Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11) do not apply to the sale or
  disposition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition by agent or agency

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} An agent or agency of Her Majesty in right of Canada
  --- at the request of the Minister, which may be made at any time ---
  shall sell or otherwise dispose of shares acquired under subsection
  (6). The [Surplus Crown Assets Act](/eng/acts/S-27) and section 61 of
  the [Financial Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11) do not apply to the
  sale or disposition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consideration by Minister

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister or an agent or agency of Her Majesty
  in right of Canada is holding shares of a bank on behalf of or in
  trust for Her Majesty on the day that is two years after the day on
  which the shares were acquired, the Minister shall consider whether
  holding the shares continues to promote the stability of the financial
  system in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory disposition

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister, under subsection (11), considers
  that holding shares acquired under subsection (6) no longer continues
  to promote the stability of the financial system in Canada, the
  Minister --- or, at the request of the Minister, the agent or agency
  of Her Majesty in right of Canada --- shall take the measures that the
  Minister considers practicable in the circumstances to sell or
  otherwise dispose of the shares. The [Surplus Crown Assets
  Act](/eng/acts/S-27) and section 61 of the [Financial Administration
  Act](/eng/acts/F-11) do not apply to the sale or disposition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not a Crown corporation

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} Even if the acquisition of a bank's shares under
  subsection (6) would otherwise cause the bank to be a Crown
  corporation, as defined in subsection 83(1) of the [Financial
  Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11), the bank is not a Crown
  corporation for the purposes of that Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}[Statutory Instruments
  Act](/eng/acts/S-22)

  [(14)]{.lawlabel} The [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22) does
  not apply to an order made under this section.

- Definition of [[shares]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(15)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section,
  [[shares]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes membership shares and any
  conversion or exchange privilege, option or right to acquire shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bank holding company

  [(16)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, a reference to a
  "bank" includes a reference to a "bank holding company", and the
  references to "section 646.1" in paragraphs (5)(a) and (b) are to be
  read, in relation to a bank holding company, as references to "section
  962".

::: HistoricalNote
- 2009, c. 2, s. 275
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2090
- 2016, c. 7, s. 175
:::

[Previous
Version](section-973.2-20121219.html "Link to previous version of section 973.2"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Orders and Directives]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23196 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not statutory instruments

**[[974]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-974 .sectionLabel}** An instrument issued or
made under this Act and directed to a single bank, bank holding company,
authorized foreign bank or person, other than a regulation made under
paragraph 627.998(o) or an order referred to in section 499, is not a
statutory instrument for the purposes of the [Statutory Instruments
Act](/eng/acts/S-22).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

**[[975]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-975 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may,
by order, establish the form of any application to be made to the
Minister or the Superintendent under this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

### [Applications to Superintendent]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23205 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Content of applications

- **[[976]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-976 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  following applications to the Superintendent must contain the
  information, material and evidence that the Superintendent may
  require:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} applications for approval under subsection 65(1),
    72(2), 75(4), 79(5), 79.1(2), 80(1), 170(1), 192.03(6), 217(3),
    421(1), 468(6) or (11), 471(1) or (2) or 482(1), subparagraph
    487(2)(a)(vi), section 490 or subsection 494(3) or (4), 495.3(1),
    553.1(1), 709(1), 716(2), 718(4), 723(1), 758(1), 924(1), 930(6) or
    (11), 933(1) or 944(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} applications for consent under subsection 71(1) or
    715(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} applications for exemptions under subsection
    156.05(3); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} applications for extensions of time under
    subsection 471(3) or (5), 472(4), 473(4), 933(2) or (4), 934(3) or
    935(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Receipt

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without delay after receiving the application, the
  Superintendent shall send a receipt to the applicant certifying the
  date on which it was received.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of decision to applicant

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the Superintendent shall,
  within a period of thirty days after the receipt of the application,
  send to the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a notice approving the application, subject to any
    terms and conditions that the Superintendent considers appropriate;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the Superintendent is not satisfied that it
    should be approved, a notice to that effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of period

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is unable to complete the
  consideration of the application within the period referred to in
  subsection (3), the Superintendent shall, within that period, send a
  notice to the applicant informing the applicant that the
  Superintendent has extended the period for a further period set out in
  the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed approval

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the applicant does not receive the notice required
  by subsection (3) and, where applicable, subsection (4), within the
  required period, the Superintendent is deemed to have approved the
  application and granted the approval, consent, extension or exemption
  to which the application relates, regardless of whether the approval,
  consent, extension or exemption is to be in writing or not.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2007, c. 6, s. 126
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2091
:::

[Previous
Version](section-976-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 976"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Applications for Certain Approvals]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23225 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for certain approvals

- **[[976.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-976.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An application for the prior written
  approval of the Minister in respect of any of the following provisions
  must be filed with the Superintendent and contain the information,
  material and evidence that the Superintendent may require:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 410(1)(c) and (c.1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 468(5)(b.1), (c), (d) and (d.1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 522.22(1)(c), (d) and (d.1);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 539(1)(b.1) and (b.2); and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 930(5)(b.1), (c), (d) and (d.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certification of receipt of application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the
  application contains all the required information, the Superintendent
  must refer it to the Minister, together with his or her analysis in
  relation to the application, and send a receipt to the applicant
  certifying the date on which the application was referred to the
  Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incomplete application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the
  application is incomplete, the Superintendent must send a notice to
  the applicant specifying the information required by the
  Superintendent to complete it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of decision

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), the Minister must, within
  30 days after the certified date referred to in subsection (2), send
  to the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a notice approving the application; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the Minister is not satisfied that the
    application should be approved, a notice to that effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of period

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister is unable to complete the
  consideration of an application within the 30-day period, the Minister
  must, within that period, send a notice to the applicant informing the
  applicant that the Minister has extended the period for a further
  period set out in the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed approval

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister does not send the notice referred to
  in subsection (4) or, where applicable, subsection (5), within the
  required period, the Minister is deemed to have approved the
  application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 127
- 2012, c. 5, s. 103
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-976.1-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 976.1"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Appeals]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23248 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal to Federal Court

- **[[977]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-977 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  appeal lies to the Federal Court from any direction of the Minister
  made under subsection 401.2(7), 402(1), 402.2(1), 913(7) or 915(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Federal Court may, in an appeal under subsection
  (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} dismiss the appeal;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} set aside the direction or decision; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} set aside the direction or decision and refer the
    matter back for re-determination.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of an appeal under subsection (1),
  the Minister shall, at the request of the bank, bank holding company
  or person making the appeal, provide the bank, bank holding company or
  person with a certificate in writing setting out the direction or
  decision appealed from and the reasons why the direction or decision
  was made.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2012, c. 31, s. 130
- [2023, c. 26, s. 577](#1411058-1415553){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411058-1415553.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-977-20121214.html "Link to previous version of section 977"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Regulations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23261 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to make regulations

- **[[978]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-978 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} prescribing anything that is required or authorized
    by this Act to be prescribed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} prescribing the way in which anything that is
    required or authorized by this Act to be prescribed is to be
    determined;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting, for any purpose of any provision of the
    Act, the determination of the equity of a bank or a bank holding
    company;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} defining words and expressions to be defined for
    the purposes of this Act;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} requiring the payment of a fee in respect of the
    filing, examining or issuing of any document or in respect of any
    action that the Superintendent is required or authorized to take
    under this Act, and fixing the amount of the fee or the manner of
    determining its amount;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} respecting the regulatory capital and total assets
    of a bank or a bank holding company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} respecting the retention, in Canada, of assets of a
    bank or a bank holding company;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} respecting the value of assets of a bank or a bank
    holding company to be held in Canada and the manner in which those
    assets are to be held;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} respecting the protection and maintenance of assets
    of a bank or a bank holding company, including regulations
    respecting the bonding of directors, officers and employees of a
    bank or a bank holding company;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} respecting the holding of shares, membership shares
    and ownership interests for the purposes of sections 70, 74 and 714;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} respecting information, in addition to the
    information required by section 634 or 953, to be maintained in the
    register referred to in that section; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} generally for carrying out the purposes and
    provisions of this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporation by reference

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The regulations may incorporate any material by
  reference regardless of its source and either as it exists on a
  particular date or as amended from time to time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporated material is not a
  regulation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Material does not become a regulation for the
  purposes of the [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22) because it
  is incorporated by reference.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 135
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2092
:::

### [Delegation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-23283 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

**[[979]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-979 .sectionLabel}** The Minister may
delegate any of the Minister's powers, duties and functions under this
Act to any Minister of State appointed under the [Ministries and
Ministers of State Act](/eng/acts/M-8) to assist the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

## [PART XVI.1]{.HLabel1}[Whistleblowing]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1370402 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of
[[wrongdoing]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

**[[979.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-979.1 .sectionLabel}** In this Part,
[[wrongdoing]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes a contravention of

:   - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any provision of this Act or the regulations;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a voluntary code of conduct that a bank or
      authorized foreign bank has adopted or a public commitment that it
      has made; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a policy or procedure established by a bank or
      authorized foreign bank.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 334](#1039586-1370410){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039586-1370410.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Whistleblowing

- **[[979.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-979.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any employee of a bank or authorized
  foreign bank who has reasonable grounds to believe that the bank,
  authorized foreign bank or any person has committed or intends to
  commit a wrongdoing may report the particulars of the matter to the
  bank or authorized foreign bank or to the Commissioner, the
  Superintendent, a government agency or body that regulates or
  supervises financial institutions or a law enforcement agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidentiality

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The bank, authorized foreign bank, Commissioner,
  Superintendent, government agency or body or law enforcement agency
  shall keep confidential the identity of the employee and any
  information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their
  identity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- bank or authorized
  foreign bank

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), the bank or authorized
  foreign bank may disclose the identity of the employee and information
  that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identity to the
  Commissioner, Superintendent, government agency or body or law
  enforcement agency if the Commissioner, Superintendent, government
  agency or body or law enforcement agency considers the disclosure
  necessary for purposes related to an investigation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- Commissioner,
  Superintendent, agency and body

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), the Commissioner,
  Superintendent, government agency or body or law enforcement agency
  may disclose to each other the identity of the employee and
  information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identity
  for purposes related to an investigation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Informing of disclosure

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the bank, authorized foreign bank, Commissioner,
  Superintendent, government agency or body or law enforcement agency
  has disclosed, under subsection (3) or (4), the identity of the
  employee or any information that could reasonably be expected to
  reveal their identity, the bank, authorized foreign bank,
  Commissioner, Superintendent, government agency or body or law
  enforcement agency shall make every reasonable effort to inform the
  employee of the disclosure.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 334](#1039586-1370423){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039586-1370423.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedures --- wrongdoing

**[[979.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-979.3 .sectionLabel}** A bank or
authorized foreign bank shall establish and implement procedures for
dealing with matters the particulars of which have been reported to it
by employees under subsection 979.2(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 334](#1039586-1370427){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039586-1370427.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

- **[[979.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-979.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No bank or authorized foreign bank
  shall dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, harass or otherwise
  disadvantage an employee, or deny an employee a benefit of employment,
  by reason that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the employee, acting on the basis of reasonable
    belief, has reported particulars under subsection 979.2(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the employee, acting on the basis of reasonable
    belief, has refused or stated an intention of refusing to do
    anything that is a wrongdoing;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the employee, acting on the basis of reasonable
    belief, has done or stated an intention of doing anything that is
    required to be done in order to prevent a wrongdoing from being
    committed; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the bank or authorized foreign bank believes that
    the employee will do anything referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Saving

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this section impairs any right of an
  employee either at law or under an employment contract or collective
  agreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 27, s. 334](#1039586-1370438){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1039586-1370438.html"}
:::

## [PART XVII]{.HLabel1}[Sanctions]{.HTitleText1} {#h-23288 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offence

**[[980]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-980 .sectionLabel}** Every person who,
without reasonable cause, contravenes any provision of this Act or the
regulations is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}False or misleading information

**[[980.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-980.1 .sectionLabel}** Every person who
knowingly provides false or misleading information in relation to any
matter under this Act or the regulations is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 128
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Undue preference to creditor

**[[981]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-981 .sectionLabel}** Every director, officer
or employee of a bank or an authorized foreign bank who wilfully gives
or concurs in giving to any creditor of the bank or authorized foreign
bank any fraudulent, undue or unfair preference over other creditors, by
giving security to the creditor, by changing the nature of the
creditor's claim or otherwise, is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to provide information

**[[982]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-982 .sectionLabel}** Every person who,
without reasonable cause, refuses or fails to comply with a requirement
made under paragraph 643(2)(b) or 957(2)(b) is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use of name

- **[[983]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-983
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except to the extent permitted by
  the regulations, every person who uses the name of a bank or of a bank
  holding company in a prospectus, offering memorandum, takeover bid
  circular, advertisement for a transaction related to securities or in
  any other document in connection with a transaction related to
  securities is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized name

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1), (6) and (12), every entity, other than a bank, that acquires,
  adopts or retains a name, a domain name or an identifying mark that
  includes the word "bank", "banker" or "banking", either alone or in
  combination with other words, to indicate or describe a business in
  Canada or any part of a business in Canada, without being authorized
  to do so by this Act or any other Act of Parliament, is guilty of an
  offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized name --- "credit union"
  and "bank"

  [(2.01)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1) and (12), every entity, other than a federal credit union, that
  acquires, adopts or retains a name that includes both the phrase
  "credit union" and the word "bank", either alone or in combination
  with other words, to indicate or describe a business in Canada or any
  part of a business in Canada, without being authorized to do so by
  this Act or any other Act of Parliament, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized name --- "credit union"
  and "federal"

  [(2.02)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1) and (12), every entity, other than a federal credit union, that
  acquires, adopts or retains a name that includes both the phrase
  "credit union" and the word "federal", either alone or in combination
  with other words, to indicate or describe a business in Canada or any
  part of a business in Canada, without being authorized to do so by
  this Act or any other Act of Parliament, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized name --- "cooperative" and
  "bank"

  [(2.03)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1) and (12), every entity, other than a federal credit union, that
  acquires, adopts or retains a name that includes both of the words
  "cooperative" and "bank", either alone or in combination with other
  words, to indicate or describe a business in Canada or any part of a
  business in Canada, without being authorized to do so by this Act or
  any other Act of Parliament, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized name --- "cooperative" and
  "federal"

  [(2.04)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1) and (12), every entity, other than a federal credit union, that
  acquires, adopts or retains a name that includes both of the words
  "cooperative" and "federal", either alone or in combination with other
  words, to indicate or describe a business in Canada or any part of a
  business in Canada, without being authorized to do so by this Act or
  any other Act of Parliament, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized use of word "bank",
  "banker" or "banking"

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1), (6) and (12), every person, other than a bank, who uses the
  word "bank", "banker" or "banking", without being authorized to do so
  by this Act or any other Act of Parliament, to indicate or describe a
  business in Canada or any part of a business in Canada, including any
  of its products or services or the means by which any of those
  products or services may be obtained, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized use of word "bank",
  "banker" or "banking"

  [(2.11)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4) to
  (5.1), (6) and (12), every person, other than a bank, who, in respect
  of their own business, causes or authorizes another person to use the
  word "bank", "banker" or "banking", without being authorized to do so
  by this Act or any other Act of Parliament, to indicate or describe
  that business in Canada, or any part of that business in Canada,
  including any of its products or services or the means by which any of
  those products or services may be obtained, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized use of name or identifying
  mark of bank or foreign bank

  [(2.2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4),
  (5), (5.2), (5.3) and (10) to (12), every person who uses the name or
  any identifying mark of a bank or a foreign bank to indicate or
  describe a business in Canada or any part of a business in Canada,
  without being authorized to do so by this Act or any other Act of
  Parliament, is guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized statements regarding
  association with a bank, etc.

  [(2.3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (4),
  (5.2) and (12), every person is guilty of an offence who, without
  being authorized to do so by this Act or any other Act of Parliament,
  makes any statement that a business is connected, associated or
  affiliated with a bank or a foreign bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unauthorized use of name or identifying
  mark of a bank holding company

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations and subsections (7) to
  (9.1) and (12), every entity that acquires, adopts or retains the name
  of a bank holding company and every person who uses the name or any
  identifying mark of a bank holding company to indicate or describe a
  business in Canada or any part of a business in Canada, without being
  authorized to do so by this Act or any other Act of Parliament, is
  guilty of an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person commits an offence under any of
  subsections (2) to (2.3) if the activity referred to in that
  subsection is done

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in a description of the corporate relationship
    between a bank and an entity controlled by the bank;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to the regulations, in a description of a
    corporate relationship between a bank and an entity affiliated with
    the bank;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} in a description of the corporate relationship
    between a bank holding company and an entity controlled by the bank
    holding company;

  - [(b.2) and (b.3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s.
    129\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in an advertisement in Canada by or on behalf of a
    foreign bank in respect of its facilities outside Canada;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the identification of representative offices of
    a foreign bank in Canada;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the business in Canada of an
    authorized foreign bank;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in a description of the corporate relationship
    between a bank or a bank holding company and a foreign bank that
    controls the bank or the bank holding company;

  - [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} in a description of the corporate relationship
    between a bank or a bank holding company and an entity that is
    associated with a foreign bank and that controls the bank or the
    bank holding company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} subject to the regulations, in a description of the
    corporate relationship between a non-bank affiliate of a foreign
    bank, within the meaning of subsection 507(1), and a foreign bank
    that controls the non-bank affiliate, if the non-bank affiliate is
    not a bank holding company or an entity that is controlled by a bank
    holding company;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} subject to the regulations, in a description of the
    corporate relationship between a non-bank affiliate of a foreign
    bank, within the meaning of subsection 507(1), and an entity that is
    associated with a foreign bank that controls the non-bank affiliate,
    if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the non-bank affiliate is not a bank holding
      company or an entity that is controlled by a bank holding company,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the entity is not a bank, a bank holding
      company, a foreign bank or an entity controlled by a bank or a
      bank holding company;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the identification of a body corporate that was
    a non-bank affiliate of a foreign bank within the meaning of
    subsection 303(1) of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), being chapter
    B-1 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, at any time before June
    1, 1981;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} in the identification of a Canadian financial
    institution that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} was controlled by a bank that was a subsidiary of
      a foreign bank before June 15, 1997 but that has ceased to be so
      controlled,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is controlled by a foreign bank that, before
      June 15, 1997, controlled the subsidiary, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} used, before June 15, 1997, the word "bank",
      "banker" or "banking" to identify itself; or

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} in the identification of a bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} No person commits an offence under any of
  subsections (2.01) to (2.04) if the activity referred to in that
  subsection is done

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in relation to a prescribed use;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under prescribed circumstances; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with a prescribed approval and any
    terms and conditions that the Minister may impose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(4.2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations, no person commits an
  offence under subsection (2.1) or (2.11) if they meet the requirements
  set out in subsection (4.3) and they are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a body corporate to which the [Trust and Loan
    Companies Act](/eng/acts/T-19.8) applies;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a trust or loan corporation incorporated or formed
    by or under an Act of the legislature of a province;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a central cooperative credit society;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a local cooperative credit society;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a federation of cooperative credit societies;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the corporation known as "ATB Financial" and
    referred to in section 2 of the ATB Financial Act, chapter A-45.2 of
    the Revised Statutes of Alberta 2000, or a successor of that
    corporation; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a prescribed entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirements

  [(4.3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (4.2), the
  requirements are the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} subject to the regulations, the entity discloses

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the type of entity it is, as described in any of
      paragraphs (4.2)(a) to (g) or in the regulations,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the jurisdiction under whose laws the entity is
      primarily regulated,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} whether it participates in a deposit insurance
      system in Canada, and if so, the name of that system, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} any other prescribed information; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entity complies with any prescribed
    requirements or conditions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No subsidiary of a bank commits an offence by reason
  only that it uses the name of the bank of which it is a subsidiary in
  its corporate name or a name under which it carries on business or by
  reason only that it uses any identifying mark or domain name of that
  bank in carrying on its business.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} No person commits an offence under subsections (2)
  to (2.1) if the activity referred to in that subsection is in relation
  to a business that is not engaged in financial activities, unless the
  business is carried out by a prescribed entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(5.2)]{.lawlabel} No bank commits an offence under subsection (2.2)
  or (2.3) if it is affiliated with the bank or the foreign bank.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(5.3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations, no entity affiliated
  with a bank commits an offence by reason only that the entity uses the
  name of the bank in the entity's corporate name or in a name under
  which the entity carries on business or by reason only that it uses
  any identifying mark of the bank in carrying on its business, if the
  entity does not use any of the words "bank", "banker" or "banking" or
  the phrase "federal credit union" in its corporate name, in a name
  under which it carries on business or in any of its identifying marks.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} No financial institution that was controlled by a
  bank on June 25, 1999 and that had a name that included the word
  "bank", "banker" or "banking" on that day commits an offence by reason
  only that it uses that word in its corporate name or in a name under
  which it carries on business if the financial institution is a
  subsidiary of a bank holding company that controls the bank.

- [(6.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 129\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} No subsidiary of a bank holding company commits an
  offence by reason only that it uses the name of the bank holding
  company in the subsidiary's corporate name or in a name under which it
  carries on business, or by reason only that it uses any identifying
  mark of the bank holding company in carrying on its business, so long
  as, if the subsidiary is not a bank or a subsidiary of a bank, it does
  not use the word "bank", "banker" or "banking" in its corporate name,
  in a name under which it carries on business or in any of its
  identifying marks.

- [(7.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 129\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations, no entity affiliated with
  a bank holding company commits an offence by reason only that the
  entity uses the name of the bank holding company in the entity's
  corporate name or in a name under which the entity carries on business
  or by reason only that it uses any identifying mark of the bank
  holding company in carrying on its business, if the entity does not
  use the word "bank", "banker" or "banking" in its corporate name, in a
  name under which it carries on business or in any of its identifying
  marks.

- [(8.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 129\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} No subsidiary of a bank holding company commits an
  offence by reason only that it uses the name of the bank holding
  company in a description of its corporate relationship to the bank
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(9.1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations, no entity affiliated
  with a bank holding company commits an offence by reason only that the
  entity uses the name of the bank holding company in a description of
  the entity's corporate relationship with the bank holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations, no Canadian entity that
  is an entity associated with a foreign bank commits an offence by
  reason only that it uses the name of the foreign bank in its corporate
  name or in a name under which it carries on business, or by reason
  only that it uses any identifying mark of the foreign bank in carrying
  on its business, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it does not use the word "bank", "banker" or
    "banking" in its corporate name, in a name under which it carries on
    business or in any of its identifying marks; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign bank has consented to the use.

- [(10.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 129\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the regulations, no foreign bank that
  carries on a business or activity referred to in section 510.1,
  522.05, 522.18 or 522.19, and no entity incorporated or formed by or
  under the laws of a country other than Canada that carries on a
  business or activity referred to in any of those provisions and that
  is an entity associated with a foreign bank, commits an offence by
  reason only that it uses its name or any of its identifying marks if
  it does not use the word "bank", "banker" or "banking".

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted use --- consent

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} No person commits an offence under any of
  subsections (2) to (3) if the activity referred to in that subsection
  has been approved by the Superintendent and is in accordance with any
  terms and conditions that the Superintendent may impose and, if the
  activity involves the use of the name or any identifying mark of a
  bank, a bank holding company or a foreign bank, the bank, bank holding
  company or foreign bank has consented to the use.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Words [[bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef},
  [[banker]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} or [[banking]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the word
  [[bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, [[banker]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or
  [[banking]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any of those words in any language; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any word or words, in any language, that are
    equivalent to any of those words.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Phrase [[credit
  union]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(13.1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the phrase
  [[credit union]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that phrase in any language; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any word or words, in any language, that are
    equivalent to any of the words in that phrase.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Words
  [[cooperative]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} and
  [[federal]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(13.2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the words
  [[cooperative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and
  [[federal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any of those words in any language; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any word or words, in any language, that are
    equivalent to any of those words.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entity's name

  [(14)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, other than
  subsection (1), an entity's name includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a name that is substantially similar to the
    entity's name; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entity's name in any language.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Identifying marks

  [(15)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, an identifying
  mark of an entity includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any logogram, insignia or logo of the entity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the initials or any acronym of the entity;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} any trademark of the entity; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any mark that is substantially similar to any
    identifying mark of the entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[foreign
  bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(16)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[foreign
  bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a foreign bank to which Part XII
  applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entity associated with a foreign bank

  [(17)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, an entity is
  associated with a foreign bank if the entity is or is deemed to be
  associated with the foreign bank within the meaning of section 507 and
  is an entity to which Part XII applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(18)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations for the
  purposes of subsections (1) to (3), paragraphs (4)(b), (g) and (h) and
  subsections (4.2), (4.3), (5.3), (8) and (9.1) to (11).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2007, c. 6, s. 129
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2093
- 2018, c. 12, s. 352
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-983-20121219.html "Link to previous version of section 983"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Making false statements

- **[[984]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-984
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence
  who wilfully makes a false statement

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in a warehouse receipt or bill of lading given to a
    bank or authorized foreign bank under the authority of this Act; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in a document giving or purporting to give security
    on property to a bank under section 426 or 427 or to an authorized
    foreign bank under either of those sections as incorporated by
    section 555.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Wilfully disposing of or withholding
  goods covered by security

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence who, having
  possession or control of property mentioned in or covered by a
  warehouse receipt, bill of lading or any security given to a bank
  under section 426 or 427 or to an authorized foreign bank under either
  of those sections as incorporated by section 555, and having knowledge
  of the receipt, bill of lading or security, without the consent of the
  bank or authorized foreign bank in writing before the loan, advance,
  debt or liability secured by it has been fully paid

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} wilfully alienates or parts with any of the
    property; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} wilfully withholds from the bank or authorized
    foreign bank possession of any of the property if demand for its
    possession is made by the bank or authorized foreign bank after
    failure to pay the loan, advance, debt or liability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-compliance with requirements for
  sale

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a debt or liability to a bank or authorized
  foreign bank is secured by a warehouse receipt or bill of lading or
  security on property given to a bank under section 426 or 427 or to an
  authorized foreign bank under either of those sections as incorporated
  by section 555 and is not paid, the bank or authorized foreign bank is
  guilty of an offence if it sells the property covered by the warehouse
  receipt, bill of lading or security under the power of sale conferred
  on it by this Act without complying with the provisions of this Act
  applicable to the exercise of the power of sale.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Acquisition of warehouse receipts,
  bills of lading, etc.

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Every bank or authorized foreign bank that acquires
  or holds a warehouse receipt or bill of lading or a document signed
  and delivered to it giving or purporting to give to the bank security
  on property under section 426 or 427, or to give the authorized
  foreign bank security or property under either of those sections as
  incorporated by section 555, to secure the payment of any debt,
  liability, loan or advance, is guilty of an offence unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the debt, liability, loan or advance is contracted
    or made at the time of the acquisition by the bank or authorized
    foreign bank of the warehouse receipt, bill of lading or document;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the debt, liability, loan or advance was contracted
    or made on the written promise or agreement that the warehouse
    receipt, bill of lading or security would be given to the bank or
    authorized foreign bank; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the acquisition or holding by the bank or
    authorized foreign bank of the warehouse receipt, bill of lading or
    security is otherwise authorized by an Act of Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the expressions
  [[warehouse receipt]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and [[bill of
  lading]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} have the meaning assigned to those
  expressions by section 425.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment

- **[[985]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-985
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an
  offence under any of sections 980 to 984 is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a natural person, liable

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than
      \$100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than twelve
      months, or to both, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not
      more than \$1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more
      than five years, or to both; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an entity, liable

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than
      \$500,000, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not
      more than \$5,000,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person has been convicted of an offence under
  this Act, the court may, in addition to any punishment it may
  otherwise impose, order the person to comply with the provisions of
  this Act or the regulations in respect of which the person was
  convicted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional fine

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a person has been convicted of an offence under
  this Act, the court may, if it is satisfied that as a result of the
  commission of the offence the convicted person acquired any monetary
  benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the convicted person or
  their spouse, common-law partner or other dependant, order the
  convicted person to pay, despite the maximum amount of any fine that
  may otherwise be imposed under this Act, an additional fine in an
  amount equal to three times the court's estimation of the amount of
  those monetary benefits.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 136
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-985-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 985"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liability of officers, directors, etc.

**[[986]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-986 .sectionLabel}** If an entity commits an
offence under this Act, any officer, director, agent or principal
officer of the entity who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced
in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and
guilty of the offence and liable on summary conviction or on conviction
on indictment to the punishment provided under paragraph 985(1)(a) for
the offence, whether or not the entity has been prosecuted or convicted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation period

- **[[987]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-987
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Proceedings by way of summary
  conviction in respect of an offence under a provision of this Act may
  be commenced at any time within, but not later than, two years after
  the day on which the subject-matter of the proceedings became known,
  in the case of an offence under a consumer provision, to the
  Commissioner and, in any other case, to the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate of Superintendent or
  Commissioner

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A document appearing to have been issued by the
  Superintendent or the Commissioner, as the case may be, certifying the
  day on which the subject-matter of any proceedings became known to the
  Superintendent or the Commissioner is admissible in evidence without
  proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing
  to have signed it and is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary,
  proof of the matter asserted in it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of offence on contracts

**[[988]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-988 .sectionLabel}** Unless otherwise
expressly provided in this Act, a contravention of any provision of this
Act or the regulations does not invalidate any contract entered into in
contravention of the provision.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance or restraining order --- bank

- **[[989]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-989 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  bank or a bank holding company or any director, officer, employee or
  agent of one does not comply with any provision of this Act or the
  regulations other than a consumer provision, or of the incorporating
  instrument or any by-law of the bank or bank holding company, the
  Superintendent, any complainant or any creditor of the bank or bank
  holding company may, in addition to any other right that that person
  has, apply to a court for an order directing the bank, bank holding
  company, director, officer, employee or agent to comply with --- or
  restraining the bank, bank holding company, director, officer,
  employee or agent from acting in breach of --- the provision and, on
  the application, the court may so order and make any further order it
  thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance or restraining order ---
  authorized foreign bank

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an authorized foreign bank or any of its
  directors, officers, employees or agents does not comply with any
  provision of this Act or the regulations other than a consumer
  provision, or of an order made under subsection 524(1), 528(1) or
  (1.1) or 534(1) in respect of the authorized foreign bank, the
  Superintendent, any complainant or any creditor of the authorized
  foreign bank may, in addition to any other right that that person has,
  apply to a court for an order directing the authorized foreign bank,
  director, officer, employee or agent to comply with --- or restraining
  the authorized foreign bank, director, officer, employee or agent from
  acting in breach of --- the provision and, on the application, the
  court may so order and make any further order that it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance or restraining order ---
  consumer provisions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a bank or an authorized foreign bank or any
  director, officer, employee or agent of one does not comply with any
  applicable consumer provision, the Commissioner or any complainant
  may, in addition to any other right that that person has, apply to a
  court for an order directing the bank, authorized foreign bank,
  director, officer, employee or agent to comply with --- or restraining
  the bank, authorized foreign bank, director, officer, employee or
  agent from acting in breach of --- the consumer provision and, on the
  application, the court may so order and make any further order it
  thinks fit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2007, c. 6, s. 130
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-989-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 989"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Production of information and documents

**[[989.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-989.1 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
may direct an entity to provide him or her with the information or
documents that he or she specifies if he or she is of the opinion that
their production is necessary in order to be satisfied that the entity
is meeting the requirements of subsection 983(4.3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 12, s. 353
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent's directions

- **[[989.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-989.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the
  Superintendent, a person is acting in a manner that is prohibited by
  section 983, the Superintendent may direct the person to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} cease or refrain from acting in that manner; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} perform the acts that in the opinion of the
    Superintendent are necessary to remedy the situation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opportunity for representations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no direction is to be
  issued to a person under subsection (1) unless the person is provided
  with a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of
  the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary direction

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the length
  of time required for representations to be made might be prejudicial
  to the public interest, the Superintendent may make a temporary
  direction with respect to the matters referred to in paragraphs (1)(a)
  and (b) having effect for a period of not more than 15 days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continued effect

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A temporary direction under subsection (3) continues
  to have effect after the expiration of the 15-day period referred to
  in that subsection if no representations are made within that period
  or, if representations have been made, the Superintendent notifies the
  person that the Superintendent is not satisfied that there are
  sufficient grounds for revoking the direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 12, s. 353
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement

- **[[989.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-989.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a person contravenes a direction
  made under subsection 989.2(1) or (3), the Superintendent may, in
  addition to any other action that may be taken under this Act or the
  [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
  Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), apply to a court for an order requiring the
  person to comply with the direction, and on such application the court
  may so order and make any other order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from an order of a court under
  subsection (1) lies in the same manner, and to the same court, as an
  appeal from any other order of the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 12, s. 353
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal of final order

- **[[990]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-990 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  appeal lies to the court of appeal of a province from any final order
  made by a court of that province under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal with leave

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal lies to the court of appeal of a province
  from any order, other than a final order made by a court of that
  province, only with leave of the court of appeal in accordance with
  the rules applicable to that court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
- 2005, c. 54, s. 137
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-990-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 990"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery and application of fines

**[[991]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-991 .sectionLabel}** All fines payable under
this Act are recoverable and enforceable, with costs, at the suit of Her
Majesty in right of Canada, instituted by the Attorney General of
Canada, and, when recovered, belong to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 183
:::

## [PART XVIII]{.HLabel1}[Documents in Electronic or Other Form]{.HTitleText1} {#h-23525 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[992]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-992 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Part.

[[electronic document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[electronic document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, except in section
    1001, any form of representation of information or concepts that is
    fixed in any medium in or by electronic, optical or other similar
    means and that can be read or perceived by a person or by any
    means. ([document électronique]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[information system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[information system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a system used to
    generate, send, receive, store or otherwise process an electronic
    document. ([système de traitement de l'information]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

**[[993]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-993 .sectionLabel}** This Part other than
sections 1004 and 1005 does not apply in respect of any notice, document
or other information that under this Act or the regulations is sent to
or issued by the Minister, the Superintendent, the Commissioner or the
Bank of Canada or any prescribed notice, document or information.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use not mandatory

**[[994]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-994 .sectionLabel}** Nothing in this Act or
the regulations requires a person to create or provide an electronic
document.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consent and other requirements

- **[[995]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-995
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite anything in this Part, a
  requirement under this Act or the regulations to provide a notice,
  document or other information is not satisfied by providing an
  electronic document unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the addressee consents and designates an
    information system for the receipt of the electronic document;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the electronic document is, unless otherwise
    prescribed, provided to the designated information system; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consent and notice in electronic form

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the requirements referred
  to in paragraph (1)(c) may provide that the consent referred to in
  paragraph (1)(a) and any notice related to that consent may be
  provided in electronic form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations --- revocation of consent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the revocation of the consent referred to in paragraph
  (1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
- 2018, c. 27, s. 153
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-995-20110601.html "Link to previous version of section 995"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Creation or provision of information

**[[996]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-996 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to create or provide a notice, document or
other information is satisfied by creating or providing an electronic
document if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the incorporating instrument or by-laws of the bank,
  bank holding company or authorized foreign bank, as the case may be,
  do not provide otherwise; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Creation of information in writing

**[[997]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-997 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to create a notice, document or other
information in writing is satisfied by creating an electronic document
if in addition to the conditions set out in section 996

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information in the electronic document is
  accessible so as to be usable for subsequent reference; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of information in writing

**[[998]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-998 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to provide a notice, document or other
information in writing is satisfied by providing an electronic document
if in addition to the conditions set out in section 996

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information in the electronic document is
  accessible by the addressee and capable of being retained by them so
  as to be usable for subsequent reference; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Multiple copies

**[[999]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-999 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to provide two or more copies of a document
at the same time to one addressee is satisfied by providing one copy of
the electronic document.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered mail

**[[1000]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to provide a document by registered mail is
not satisfied by providing an electronic document except in the
prescribed circumstances.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statutory declarations and affidavits

- **[[1001]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1001 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  statutory declaration or affidavit required under this Act or the
  regulations may be created or provided in an electronic document if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person who makes the statutory declaration or
    affidavit signs it with their secure electronic signature;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the authorized person before whom the statutory
    declaration or affidavit is made signs it with their secure
    electronic signature; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of sections 994 to 1000 are
    complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, [[electronic
  document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and [[secure electronic
  signature]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} have the same meaning as in subsection
  31(1) of the [Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents
  Act](/eng/acts/P-8.6).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}References to "electronic document"

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of complying with paragraph (1)(c),
  references to "electronic document" in sections 994 to 1000 are to be
  read as references to "electronic document within the meaning of
  subsection 31(1) of the [Personal Information Protection and
  Electronic Documents Act](/eng/acts/P-8.6)".

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Signatures

**[[1002]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1002 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations for a signature or for a document to be
executed, except in respect of a statutory declaration or affidavit, is
satisfied in respect of an electronic document if the prescribed
requirements are complied with and the signature results from the
application by the person of a technology or process that permits the
following to be proved:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the signature resulting from the use by the person of
  the technology or process is unique to the person;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the technology or process is used by the person to
  incorporate their signature into, attach it to or associate it with
  the electronic document; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the technology or process can be used to identify the
  person using the technology or process.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations --- provision and receipt of
documents

**[[1003]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1003 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations respecting the time and place at which and
the circumstances under which an electronic document is considered to be
provided or received.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Content and form of notices and documents

**[[1004]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1004 .sectionLabel}** The Minister,
Superintendent, Commissioner or Bank of Canada may establish the
requirements for the content and fix the form, including electronic and
other forms, of notices and documents sent to or issued by each of them
under this Act or the regulations, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the notices and documents that may be sent in
  electronic or other form;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the persons or classes of persons who may send
  notices and documents;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} their signature in electronic or other form or their
  execution, adoption or authorization in a manner that is to have the
  same effect for the purposes of this Act as their signature;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the time and place at which and the circumstances
  under which electronic documents are considered to be sent or
  received; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} any matter necessary for the purposes of the
  application of this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption

**[[1005]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1005 .sectionLabel}** In the prescribed
circumstances, the Minister, Superintendent, Commissioner or Bank of
Canada may, on any conditions that they consider appropriate, exempt
from the application of any provision of this Act requiring a notice or
document to be sent to them any notice or document, or class of notice
or document, containing information similar to that contained in a
notice or document required to be made public under any other Act of
Parliament or any Act of the legislature of a province.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 138
:::

- --- 2018, c. 27, s. 335

  - ###### Body corporate deemed to be approved {#body-corporate-deemed-to-be-approved .MarginalNote}

    [335]{.lawlabel} A body corporate that has been approved under
    section 455.01 of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), as it read
    immediately before the day on which section 329 comes into force, is
    deemed to have been approved under section 627.48 of that Act as
    enacted by that section 329.

- --- 2023, c. 26, s. 139

  - ###### Definitions {#definitions .MarginalNote}

    - [139]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply
      in this section.

      [[former external complaints body]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[former external complaints body]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
          an external complaints body as defined in section 2 of the
          [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01) as it read before the day on
          which section 128 of this Act comes into force. ([ancien
          organisme externe de traitement des plaintes]{.DefinedTermLink
          lang="fr"})

      [[new external complaints body]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[new external complaints body]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
          body corporate designated under subsection 627.48(1) of the
          [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), as amended by section 129 of
          this Act. ([nouvel organisme externe de traitement des
          plaintes]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

    - ###### Revocation of approval {#revocation-of-approval .MarginalNote}

      [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any approval given to a former external
      complaints body under subsection 627.48(1) of the [Bank
      Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), as it read immediately before the day on
      which section 129 of this Act comes into force, is revoked on the
      later of the day on which the designation of the new external
      complaints body takes effect and the day on which the former
      external complaints body resolves every complaint pending before
      it.

    - ###### Application before designation {#application-before-designation .MarginalNote}

      [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the day on which section 129 of this Act comes
      into force, sections 627.48 and 627.49 of the [Bank
      Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), as they read immediately before that day,
      continue to apply in respect of former external complaints bodies
      until the day on which the designation of the new external
      complaints body takes effect.

    - ###### Application on designation {#application-on-designation .MarginalNote}

      [(4)]{.lawlabel} On the day on which the designation of the new
      external complaints body takes effect,

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} unless otherwise specified by the Commissioner,
        a former external complaints body shall continue the resolution
        of any complaint pending before it;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sections 627.48 and 627.49 of the [Bank
        Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), as they read immediately before the day
        on which section 129 of this Act comes into force, continue to
        apply for the purposes of paragraph (a); and

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the new external complaints body shall resolve
        all complaints that are not pending before any former external
        complaints body.
